#### CAT-AG-P3-C05-FAIL — Financial Assessment and Budget Approval — Failure Flow

**Diagram ID:** `CAT-AG-P3-C05-FAIL`  
**Title:** Financial Assessment and Budget Approval — Failure Flow  
**Purpose:** Show explicit failure classification, effect containment, evidence preservation, and escalation.  
**Audience:** Reliability engineers, incident responders, agent owners, and human supervisors.  
**Reading Order:** Read top to bottom; no retry path appears before effect certainty is established.  

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  F[Failure or uncertainty] --> Stop[Stop dependent effects]
  Stop --> State[Persist state and evidence]
  State --> Attempt{Material effect attempted}
  Attempt -->|No| Class[Classify retryability]
  Attempt -->|Yes| Truth[Query domain source of truth]
  Truth --> Known{Effect state known}
  Known -->|No| Quarantine[Quarantine collaboration]
  Known -->|Yes| Class
  Class --> Safe{Retry safe and budgeted}
  Safe -->|Yes| Recover[Enter recovery flow]
  Safe -->|No| Escalate[Escalate to Authorized treasury reviewer]
  Quarantine --> Escalate
```

#### CAT-AG-P3-C05-REC — Financial Assessment and Budget Approval — Recovery Flow

**Diagram ID:** `CAT-AG-P3-C05-REC`  
**Title:** Financial Assessment and Budget Approval — Recovery Flow  
**Purpose:** Show ownership, reconciliation, approved remediation, invariant verification, and resumption.  
**Audience:** Operators, domain owners, incident commanders, and auditors.  
**Reading Order:** Read left to right; recovery closes only after authoritative verification and linked evidence.  

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  Case[Owned recovery case] --> Scope[Identify affected runs and effects]
  Scope --> Reconcile[Reconcile authoritative systems]
  Reconcile --> Plan[Choose resume compensate or abandon]
  Plan --> Gate{Approval required}
  Gate -->|Yes| Human[Authorized treasury reviewer]
  Human --> Execute[Bounded remediation]
  Gate -->|No| Execute
  Execute --> Verify[Verify domain invariants]
  Verify --> Link[Link recovery and original receipts]
  Link --> Resume[Resume close or retire]
  Resume --> Learn[Propose reviewed learning]
```

#### CAT-AG-P3-C05-APP — Financial Assessment and Budget Approval — Approval Flow

**Diagram ID:** `CAT-AG-P3-C05-APP`  
**Title:** Financial Assessment and Budget Approval — Approval Flow  
**Purpose:** Show exact-scope human authorization without allowing approval laundering or payload substitution.  
**Audience:** Human approvers, governance designers, security reviewers, and implementers.  
**Reading Order:** Read top to bottom from proposed effect to decision; execution occurs only on the unchanged approved digest.  

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  Effect[Proposed consequential effect] --> Risk[Classify risk and authority]
  Risk --> Packet[Assemble evidence alternatives and uncertainty]
  Packet --> Digest[Bind payload destination and expiry]
  Digest --> Route[Resolve authorized approver role]
  Route --> Human[Authorized treasury reviewer]
  Human --> Decision{Decision}
  Decision -->|Deny| Closed[Close denied with rationale]
  Decision -->|Revise| Rebuild[Create new request and digest]
  Decision -->|Approve| Revalidate[Revalidate policy state and digest]
  Revalidate --> Same{Scope unchanged}
  Same -->|No| Rebuild
  Same -->|Yes| Execute[Execute exact approved effect]
  Execute --> Receipt[Link approval and effect receipt]
```

#### C05 Collaboration Acceptance Checklist

- [ ] Trigger schema and owner are registered.
- [ ] Each participant is an immutable certified version.
- [ ] One operational owner lease exists at every point.
- [ ] All eight flows match implemented contracts.
- [ ] Context packages are purpose-bound and expiring.
- [ ] Memory writes use the Memory authority.
- [ ] Knowledge changes preserve provenance and review.
- [ ] Events are versioned, idempotent and correlated.
- [ ] Partial success and uncertainty are typed.
- [ ] Recovery reconciles every attempted effect.
- [ ] Approval binds exact payload and cannot be reused.
- [ ] Terminal artifact passes independent acceptance.

### Collaboration C06 — Outcome Analytics and Learning

**Collaboration ID:** `CAT-AG-P3-C06`  
**Trigger:** a campaign observation window closes or an anomaly appears.  
**Operational owner:** Knowledge and Improvement lead.  
**Human approval boundary:** domain owner validates high-impact learning before canonization.  
**Terminal artifact:** validated learning proposal.  

| Contract dimension | Required behavior |
|---|---|
| Participants | Publisher Agent; Analytics Agent; Learning Agent; Campaign supervisor. |
| Task ownership | Knowledge and Improvement lead names exactly one current operational owner; contributors never imply shared completion ownership. |
| Context | Each handoff carries a purpose-bound package and the input digest for validated learning proposal. |
| Memory | Working state remains run-scoped; durable memory is proposed through Memory after outcome verification. |
| Knowledge | Canonical claims are read and changed only through Knowledge with provenance and domain review. |
| Communication | Commands request work, events report committed state, approvals bind exact effects, and receipts prove attempts. |
| Failure | The first agent detecting unsafe uncertainty stops dependent effects and publishes a typed failure or escalation. |
| Recovery | Supervisor coordinates, but the affected domain owner reconciles authoritative state and proves recovery. |
| Completion | validated learning proposal passes typed acceptance, required approval, effect verification and evidence retention. |

| Context | Each handoff carries a purpose-bound package and the input digest for contained and reconciled incident case. |
| Memory | Working state remains run-scoped; durable memory is proposed through Memory after outcome verification. |
| Knowledge | Canonical claims are read and changed only through Knowledge with provenance and domain review. |
| Communication | Commands request work, events report committed state, approvals bind exact effects, and receipts prove attempts. |
| Failure | The first agent detecting unsafe uncertainty stops dependent effects and publishes a typed failure or escalation. |
| Recovery | Supervisor coordinates, but the affected domain owner reconciles authoritative state and proves recovery. |
| Completion | contained and reconciled incident case passes typed acceptance, required approval, effect verification and evidence retention. |

#### CAT-AG-P3-C08-MEM — Security Incident Containment and Recovery — Memory Flow

**Diagram ID:** `CAT-AG-P3-C08-MEM`  
**Title:** Security Incident Containment and Recovery — Memory Flow  
**Purpose:** Distinguish ephemeral working memory, checkpoints, proposed episodes, validation, and durable synchronization.  
**Audience:** Memory engineers, agent owners, privacy reviewers, and operators.  
**Reading Order:** Start with run-scoped state; follow only verified outcomes into durable memory.  

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  Run[Collaboration run C08] --> Work[Ephemeral working memory]
  Work --> Check[Encrypted checkpoint]
  Check --> Outcome{Outcome verified}
  Outcome -->|No| Delete[Expire or quarantine working state]
  Outcome -->|Yes| Proposal[Episodic memory proposal]
  Proposal --> Policy[Retention consent and provenance checks]
  Policy --> Memory[Memory authority]
  Memory --> Receipt[Memory synchronized receipt]
  Receipt --> Invalidate[Recipient cache invalidation]
```

#### CAT-AG-P3-C08-KNW — Security Incident Containment and Recovery — Knowledge Flow

**Diagram ID:** `CAT-AG-P3-C08-KNW`  
**Title:** Security Incident Containment and Recovery — Knowledge Flow  
**Purpose:** Show evidence becoming a proposed claim and only then canonical, indexed, and retrievable.  
**Audience:** Knowledge curators, domain owners, retrieval engineers, and auditors.  
**Reading Order:** Read from observations upward to domain review; projections come only after canonical commit.  

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  Obs[Observed evidence] --> Claim[Proposed claim]
  Claim --> Source[Source and temporal validation]
  Source --> Conflict[Contradiction detection]
  Conflict --> Owner[Domain owner review]
  Owner --> Canon{Canonical commit}
  Canon --> Graph[Knowledge graph projection]
  Canon --> Index[Retrieval index]
  Canon --> Event[Knowledge changed event]
  Graph --> Future[Future authorized context]
  Index --> Future
```

#### CAT-AG-P3-C08-FAIL — Security Incident Containment and Recovery — Failure Flow

**Diagram ID:** `CAT-AG-P3-C08-FAIL`  
**Title:** Security Incident Containment and Recovery — Failure Flow  
**Purpose:** Show explicit failure classification, effect containment, evidence preservation, and escalation.  
**Audience:** Reliability engineers, incident responders, agent owners, and human supervisors.  
**Reading Order:** Read top to bottom; no retry path appears before effect certainty is established.  

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  F[Failure or uncertainty] --> Stop[Stop dependent effects]
  Stop --> State[Persist state and evidence]
  State --> Attempt{Material effect attempted}
  Attempt -->|No| Class[Classify retryability]
  Attempt -->|Yes| Truth[Query domain source of truth]
  Truth --> Known{Effect state known}
  Known -->|No| Quarantine[Quarantine collaboration]
  Known -->|Yes| Class
  Class --> Safe{Retry safe and budgeted}
  Safe -->|Yes| Recover[Enter recovery flow]
  Safe -->|No| Escalate[Escalate to Human incident commander]
  Quarantine --> Escalate
```

#### CAT-AG-P3-C08-REC — Security Incident Containment and Recovery — Recovery Flow

**Diagram ID:** `CAT-AG-P3-C08-REC`  
**Title:** Security Incident Containment and Recovery — Recovery Flow  
**Purpose:** Show ownership, reconciliation, approved remediation, invariant verification, and resumption.  
**Audience:** Operators, domain owners, incident commanders, and auditors.  
**Reading Order:** Read left to right; recovery closes only after authoritative verification and linked evidence.  

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  Case[Owned recovery case] --> Scope[Identify affected runs and effects]
  Scope --> Reconcile[Reconcile authoritative systems]
  Reconcile --> Plan[Choose resume compensate or abandon]
  Plan --> Gate{Approval required}
  Gate -->|Yes| Human[Human incident commander]
  Human --> Execute[Bounded remediation]
  Gate -->|No| Execute
  Execute --> Verify[Verify domain invariants]
  Verify --> Link[Link recovery and original receipts]
  Link --> Resume[Resume close or retire]
  Resume --> Learn[Propose reviewed learning]
```

#### CAT-AG-P3-C08-APP — Security Incident Containment and Recovery — Approval Flow

**Diagram ID:** `CAT-AG-P3-C08-APP`  
**Title:** Security Incident Containment and Recovery — Approval Flow  
**Purpose:** Show exact-scope human authorization without allowing approval laundering or payload substitution.  
**Audience:** Human approvers, governance designers, security reviewers, and implementers.  
**Reading Order:** Read top to bottom from proposed effect to decision; execution occurs only on the unchanged approved digest.  

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  Effect[Proposed consequential effect] --> Risk[Classify risk and authority]
  Risk --> Packet[Assemble evidence alternatives and uncertainty]
  Packet --> Digest[Bind payload destination and expiry]
  Digest --> Route[Resolve authorized approver role]
  Route --> Human[Human incident commander]
  Human --> Decision{Decision}
  Decision -->|Deny| Closed[Close denied with rationale]
  Decision -->|Revise| Rebuild[Create new request and digest]
  Decision -->|Approve| Revalidate[Revalidate policy state and digest]
  Revalidate --> Same{Scope unchanged}
  Same -->|No| Rebuild
  Same -->|Yes| Execute[Execute exact approved effect]
  Execute --> Receipt[Link approval and effect receipt]
```

#### C08 Collaboration Acceptance Checklist

- [ ] Trigger schema and owner are registered.
- [ ] Each participant is an immutable certified version.
- [ ] One operational owner lease exists at every point.
- [ ] All eight flows match implemented contracts.
- [ ] Context packages are purpose-bound and expiring.
- [ ] Memory writes use the Memory authority.
- [ ] Knowledge changes preserve provenance and review.
- [ ] Events are versioned, idempotent and correlated.
- [ ] Partial success and uncertainty are typed.
- [ ] Recovery reconciles every attempted effect.
- [ ] Approval binds exact payload and cannot be reused.
- [ ] Terminal artifact passes independent acceptance.

```mermaid
  Same -->|No| Rebuild
  Same -->|Yes| Execute[Execute exact approved effect]
  Execute --> Receipt[Link approval and effect receipt]
```

### Collaboration C11 — Inter-Agent Conflict Mediation

**Collaboration ID:** `CAT-AG-P3-C11`  
**Trigger:** agents produce incompatible recommendations or constraints.  
**Operational owner:** Supervisor agent owner.  
**Human approval boundary:** human owner decides unresolved high-impact trade-offs.  
**Terminal artifact:** binding resolution or preserved disagreement.  

| Contract dimension | Required behavior |
|---|---|
| Participants | Research Agent; Treasury Agent; Supervisor; Human domain owner. |
| Task ownership | Supervisor agent owner names exactly one current operational owner; contributors never imply shared completion ownership. |
| Context | Each handoff carries a purpose-bound package and the input digest for binding resolution or preserved disagreement. |
| Memory | Working state remains run-scoped; durable memory is proposed through Memory after outcome verification. |
| Knowledge | Canonical claims are read and changed only through Knowledge with provenance and domain review. |
| Communication | Commands request work, events report committed state, approvals bind exact effects, and receipts prove attempts. |
| Failure | The first agent detecting unsafe uncertainty stops dependent effects and publishes a typed failure or escalation. |
| Recovery | Supervisor coordinates, but the affected domain owner reconciles authoritative state and proves recovery. |
| Completion | binding resolution or preserved disagreement passes typed acceptance, required approval, effect verification and evidence retention. |

## 51. Agent Groups

**Section ID:** `CAT-AG-P3-51`  
**Accountable owner:** Workforce Governance Owner  
**Primary operational artifact:** ephemeral group charter  
**Purpose:** Form temporary or standing groups without creating ambiguous identity, shared credentials, collective memory, or unbounded authority.  

### Operating Contract

Form temporary or standing groups without creating ambiguous identity, shared credentials, collective memory, or unbounded authority.

| Contract element | Normative definition |
|---|---|
| Admission inputs | group purpose, sponsor, members, roles, duration, budget, data scope and dissolution condition |
| Completion outputs | group identity, charter, membership log, shared workspace, result and dissolution receipt |
| Non-negotiable invariant | A group coordinates member identities; it is not a super-agent and cannot exceed the union constrained by policy. |
| Controlled failure | Unowned, expired, over-budget, conflicted, or uncertified groups are dissolved or suspended. |
| Performance envelope | Group creation p95 below 500 ms; membership revocation propagates before the next dispatch. |
| Scale model | Use templates, bounded membership, scoped workspaces and hierarchical but non-cyclic group composition. |
| Future direction | dynamic mission teams, regional cells, capability auctions and externally federated groups |
| Named extension surface | group registry, membership policies, shared-workspace providers, dissolution hooks |

### End-to-End Procedure

1. **State group mission.** The owning component records the transition, validates required preconditions, applies current policy, and emits evidence before the next dependent step.
2. **Assign human sponsor.** The owning component records the transition, validates required preconditions, applies current policy, and emits evidence before the next dependent step.
3. **Name operational lead.** The owning component records the transition, validates required preconditions, applies current policy, and emits evidence before the next dependent step.
4. **Select certified members.** The owning component records the transition, validates required preconditions, applies current policy, and emits evidence before the next dependent step.
5. **Calculate effective authority.** The owning component records the transition, validates required preconditions, applies current policy, and emits evidence before the next dependent step.
6. **Create scoped workspace.** The owning component records the transition, validates required preconditions, applies current policy, and emits evidence before the next dependent step.
7. **Record membership changes.** The owning component records the transition, validates required preconditions, applies current policy, and emits evidence before the next dependent step.
8. **Review health.** The owning component records the transition, validates required preconditions, applies current policy, and emits evidence before the next dependent step.
9. **Deliver chartered result.** The owning component records the transition, validates required preconditions, applies current policy, and emits evidence before the next dependent step.
10. **Dissolve and revoke access.** The owning component records the transition, validates required preconditions, applies current policy, and emits evidence before the next dependent step.

### Decision and Evidence Record

| Required record | Minimum contents | Owner | Failure if absent |
|---|---|---|---|
| Identity record | logical ID, immutable version, runtime principal, tenant, environment | Workforce Governance Owner | deny admission or transition |
| Scope record | task, mission relation, inputs, exclusions, acceptance criteria | Task owner | request clarification; make no effect |
| Control record | policy version, authority calculation, grants, approvals, budgets | Policy enforcement point | deny or quarantine |
| Execution record | state history, calls, tool receipts, checkpoints, retries | Runtime or workflow owner | mark outcome unverifiable |
| Outcome record | typed result, postconditions, quality checks, effect reconciliation | Task owner | do not complete |
| Human record | decision, role, identity, rationale when required, timestamp | Human approval service | approval invalid |

### Business Perspective

Agent Groups exists to make `ephemeral group charter` a managed business capability rather than an informal model behavior. The accountable owner can see cost, risk, delay, quality, benefit and unresolved uncertainty before accepting an outcome.

Business completion requires `group identity, charter, membership log, shared workspace, result and dissolution receipt`. Throughput never justifies violating this section’s invariant: A group coordinates member identities; it is not a super-agent and cannot exceed the union constrained by policy.

### Engineering Perspective

Implement agent groups as typed deterministic boundaries around probabilistic cognition. Persist state transitions with optimistic concurrency, validate schemas at ingress and egress, propagate deadlines and cancellation, and make every external effect idempotent and reconcilable.

The primary implementation contract consumes group purpose, sponsor, members, roles, duration, budget, data scope and dissolution condition; it produces group identity, charter, membership log, shared workspace, result and dissolution receipt. Unit tests prove local guards, contract tests prove interfaces, integration tests prove storage and events, and scenario tests prove failure behavior.

### Architecture Perspective

The authority for agent groups belongs to Workforce Governance Owner; agents are clients of that authority. Ports expose stable commands and queries, adapters contain provider details, events announce committed facts, and projections remain rebuildable from authoritative records.

Extension surfaces are limited to group registry, membership policies, shared-workspace providers, dissolution hooks. An extension cannot bypass policy, identity, tenancy, ownership, evidence, compatibility or recovery contracts.

### AI Coding Perspective

Before implementing this section, load `context/00_PROJECT_CONTEXT.md`, `context/04_ARCHITECTURE.md`, `agents/`, inspect the owning port, identify the authoritative state transition, and write negative tests before connecting a model or provider. Do not invent permission from an empty directory or a draft ADR.

An AI coding agent MUST preserve existing identifiers, separate deterministic policy from prompts, use repository-approved contracts, document assumptions, avoid unrelated refactors, and return a diff whose tests demonstrate denial, cancellation, retries, reconciliation, observability and migration behavior.

### Human Perspective

A human sees the goal, current owner, evidence, uncertainty, alternatives, risk, cost, deadline, requested decision and consequence. For agent groups, the interface MUST distinguish advice from approval and preparation from execution.

Humans may override priorities or choose among permitted alternatives through an attributable mechanism, but cannot use the UI to waive immutable platform controls. Emergency exceptions remain scoped, time-bounded, reviewed and auditable.

### Implementation Notes

- Define a versioned schema and stable error taxonomy before implementing handlers.
- Keep authoritative writes behind the owner port; model output is always an untrusted proposal.
- Use content digests, correlation IDs, causation IDs and idempotency keys consistently.
- Persist checkpoints before and after material effect boundaries, not after arbitrary token intervals.
- Make time, randomness, provider calls and identifiers injectable in tests.
- Provide feature flags, a kill switch, a rollback target and a data migration dry run.
- Document operational dashboards, alerts, runbooks, ownership and support expectations.
- Reject unknown enum values safely while preserving forward-compatible envelopes where designed.

### Security Notes

Apply default deny, least privilege, tenant isolation, purpose limitation, secret-manager indirection, input/output validation, egress restrictions and redaction. The section-specific safe failure is: Unowned, expired, over-budget, conflicted, or uncertified groups are dissolved or suspended.

Threat tests MUST cover confused deputy behavior, prompt injection, forged identity, stale grant, cross-tenant references, replay, payload substitution, approval laundering, tool-result injection, data exfiltration, denial of service and evidence tampering.

### Performance Notes

Group creation p95 below 500 ms; membership revocation propagates before the next dispatch.

Measure queue time, execution time, policy time, model time, tool time, retries, token and monetary cost, cache effect, quality, cancellation delay and terminal-receipt lag separately. Never improve an average by hiding rejected, timed-out or quarantined work.

### Scalability Notes

Use templates, bounded membership, scoped workspaces and hierarchical but non-cyclic group composition.

Scaling preserves per-tenant fairness, bounded concurrency, backpressure and deterministic ownership. A global dependency must expose capacity and failure isolation; otherwise it becomes an undocumented company-wide blast radius.

### Future Evolution

Planned evolution may include dynamic mission teams, regional cells, capability auctions and externally federated groups. Every evolution remains backward-aware, evidence-driven, reversible where practical and gated by a completed ADR, migration plan and recertification impact analysis.

### Extension Points

- **Group registry:** Implement behind an owned versioned port; declare permissions, resource limits, compatibility, observability and uninstall behavior.
- **Membership policies:** Implement behind an owned versioned port; declare permissions, resource limits, compatibility, observability and uninstall behavior.
- **Shared-workspace providers:** Implement behind an owned versioned port; declare permissions, resource limits, compatibility, observability and uninstall behavior.
- **Dissolution hooks:** Implement behind an owned versioned port; declare permissions, resource limits, compatibility, observability and uninstall behavior.

### ADR References

- **Candidate implementation ADR:** `ADR-0029.md` / `adr/ADR-0029.md` must be completed and accepted before a material implementation decision relies on it.
- All current ADR files in this repository are Draft placeholders; a filename is a planning reference, not acceptance evidence or production authority.
- An ADR for this section must state context, decision, alternatives, consequences, security, data, operability, migration, rollback, tests and supersession scope.

- Future domain details remain subordinate unless an accepted ADR explicitly and lawfully supersedes a named local implementation choice.

#### CAT-AG-P3-D-051 — Agent Group Class Model

**Diagram ID:** `CAT-AG-P3-D-051`  
**Title:** Agent Group Class Model  
**Purpose:** Show group charter, membership, roles, workspace, budget, and dissolution.  
**Audience:** Business owners, architects, engineers, operators, auditors, and AI coding agents.  
**Reading Order:** Start at the declared source or top-left node; follow arrows to the terminal evidence or decision.  

```mermaid
classDiagram
  class AgentGroup {
    +String groupId
    +String mission
    +DateTime expiresAt
    +dissolve()
  }
  class GroupCharter {
    +String sponsor
    +String completionRule
  }
  class Membership {
    +String agentVersion
    +String role
  }
  class ScopedWorkspace {
    +String tenantId
    +String dataPolicy
  }
  AgentGroup *-- GroupCharter
  AgentGroup o-- Membership
  AgentGroup *-- ScopedWorkspace
```

### Atomic Operational Requirements

The following controls are independently testable for `Agent Groups`. A design that satisfies the narrative but cannot produce each named proof is incomplete.

#### CAT-AG-P3-51-R01 — Scope Admission

- **Control objective:** For agent groups, bind the request to the declared mission and reject adjacent or implied work.
- **Admission condition:** `state group mission` has an authenticated owner, valid schema, current policy version and sufficient remaining deadline and budget.
- **Runtime enforcement:** The Workforce Governance Owner evaluates this control at admission and again before a relevant state change or material effect.
- **Agent behavior:** Treat missing, stale, contradictory or denied control data as `blocked`, never as permission to infer a convenient default.
- **Human checkpoint:** Show the exact requested decision, evidence, alternatives and consequence when policy routes this control to a person.
- **Evidence:** Retain run ID, agent/version, tenant, input and output digests, control version, decision, timestamps, owner and redacted supporting receipts.
- **Failure code:** `CAT_P3_51_01_CONTROL_FAILED`; stop dependent work and preserve `ephemeral group charter` in a non-success state.
- **Recovery:** Apply `Unowned, expired, over-budget, conflicted, or uncertified groups are dissolved or suspended.` Then reconcile authoritative state, repeat only safe checks, and prove restored invariants before resume.
- **Security test:** Attempt forged identity, cross-tenant scope, replay, changed payload, expired grant and evidence tampering; all must fail closed.
- **Performance test:** Load test the decision without removing evidence; verify the section envelope `Group creation p95 below 500 ms; membership revocation propagates before the next dispatch.`
- **Ownership:** Workforce Governance Owner owns enforcement; the human domain owner accepts residual business risk; implementers own test evidence.
- **Acceptance:** An independent reviewer can reproduce the `Scope Admission` result from retained records without trusting model confidence or undocumented chat.

- [ ] Identity, tenant, classification and purpose checks occur before data use.
- [ ] Authority and approval are deterministic and effect-specific.
- [ ] Budgets, deadlines, cancellation and concurrency are enforced outside the model.
- [ ] Retries and idempotency distinguish reads from material effects.
- [ ] Context, memory and knowledge handling preserve provenance and deletion rules.
- [ ] Failures, partial outcomes and uncertainty are explicit states.
- [ ] Recovery reconciles source of truth and proves restored invariants.
- [ ] Logs, metrics, traces and receipts are redacted and sufficient.
- [ ] Security, performance, integration, migration and rollback tests exist.
- [ ] Human interfaces expose decisions without creating automation bias.
- [ ] Extension points cannot bypass policy or ownership.
- [ ] A completed ADR precedes material irreversible implementation choices.

### AI Memory Anchor

**Memory anchor `P3-51`:** `Agent Groups` is governed by `ephemeral group charter`. Preserve this invariant: A group coordinates member identities; it is not a super-agent and cannot exceed the union constrained by policy. If context is absent or contradictory, stop at the smallest safe boundary, retain evidence, and ask the named owner rather than inventing authority.

### Agent Group Types

| Group type | Duration | Lead | Example | Dissolution trigger |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Mission squad | One outcome | Supervisor or named specialist | launch one approved campaign | outcome terminal and evidence accepted |
| Incident cell | One incident | Human incident commander; Security coordinates agents | contain compromised connector | incident closed and follow-ups owned |
| Review panel | One decision window | Human domain owner | compare high-value opportunity options | decision recorded or request withdrawn |
| Standing department | Ongoing charter | Named human owner with manager coordination | Content Studio | charter revised or organization changes |
| Evaluation cohort | One assurance cycle | Assurance board | evaluate candidate agent version | certification decision issued |
| Migration cohort | Versioned migration | Migration owner | move Publisher v1 work to v2 | all leases migrated or exceptions closed |
| Regional cell | Policy-bound ongoing operation | Regional human sponsor | EU commerce operations | regional authorization revoked |

### Group Charter Required Fields

- **Group id and version** is mandatory; unresolved membership or scope defaults to no execution.
- **Mission and measurable completion** is mandatory; unresolved membership or scope defaults to no execution.
- **Human sponsor and operational lead** is mandatory; unresolved membership or scope defaults to no execution.
- **Member agent ids and immutable versions** is mandatory; unresolved membership or scope defaults to no execution.
- **Member role and decision rights** is mandatory; unresolved membership or scope defaults to no execution.
- **Effective authority calculation** is mandatory; unresolved membership or scope defaults to no execution.
- **Tenant, region, data and environment scope** is mandatory; unresolved membership or scope defaults to no execution.
- **Budget tree and concurrency cap** is mandatory; unresolved membership or scope defaults to no execution.
- **Communication channels and schemas** is mandatory; unresolved membership or scope defaults to no execution.
- **Shared context workspace policy** is mandatory; unresolved membership or scope defaults to no execution.
- **Memory and knowledge mutation route** is mandatory; unresolved membership or scope defaults to no execution.
- **Conflict and escalation chain** is mandatory; unresolved membership or scope defaults to no execution.
- **Approval map** is mandatory; unresolved membership or scope defaults to no execution.
- **Start, review and expiry timestamps** is mandatory; unresolved membership or scope defaults to no execution.
- **Dissolution and evidence-retention procedure** is mandatory; unresolved membership or scope defaults to no execution.

## 52. Departments

**Section ID:** `CAT-AG-P3-52`  
**Accountable owner:** CAT Product and Governance Owners  
**Primary operational artifact:** department charter and reporting map  
**Purpose:** Define complete company structure, domain ownership, reporting, responsibility, RACI, delegation, and authority boundaries.  

### Operating Contract

Define complete company structure, domain ownership, reporting, responsibility, RACI, delegation, and authority boundaries.

| Contract element | Normative definition |
|---|---|
| Admission inputs | product strategy, domain map, workforce roster, human accountability, policy and service ownership |
| Completion outputs | department charters, reporting matrix, ownership map, staffing gaps and review cadence |
| Non-negotiable invariant | Departments organize work but do not override domain truth, policy, separation of duties, or human accountability. |
| Controlled failure | Overlapping ownership, orphan responsibilities, circular reporting, or self-approval triggers governance review. |
| Performance envelope | Routing to a department owner p95 below one business hour for ordinary cases and severity SLO for incidents. |
| Scale model | Replicate department cells by region or tenant while preserving global contracts and named accountable owners. |
| Future direction | regional operating companies, enterprise overlays, partner departments and portfolio governance |
| Named extension surface | organization directories, ownership resolvers, enterprise role mappings, workforce planners |

### End-to-End Procedure

1. **Map business capabilities.** The owning component records the transition, validates required preconditions, applies current policy, and emits evidence before the next dependent step.
2. **Assign domain authority.** The owning component records the transition, validates required preconditions, applies current policy, and emits evidence before the next dependent step.
3. **Appoint human accountable owner.** The owning component records the transition, validates required preconditions, applies current policy, and emits evidence before the next dependent step.
4. **Place agents by primary mission.** The owning component records the transition, validates required preconditions, applies current policy, and emits evidence before the next dependent step.
5. **Define dotted-line collaboration.** The owning component records the transition, validates required preconditions, applies current policy, and emits evidence before the next dependent step.
6. **Separate incompatible duties.** The owning component records the transition, validates required preconditions, applies current policy, and emits evidence before the next dependent step.
7. **Publish reporting paths.** The owning component records the transition, validates required preconditions, applies current policy, and emits evidence before the next dependent step.
8. **Test routing.** The owning component records the transition, validates required preconditions, applies current policy, and emits evidence before the next dependent step.
9. **Review quarterly.** The owning component records the transition, validates required preconditions, applies current policy, and emits evidence before the next dependent step.
10. **Version structural change.** The owning component records the transition, validates required preconditions, applies current policy, and emits evidence before the next dependent step.

### Decision and Evidence Record

| Required record | Minimum contents | Owner | Failure if absent |
|---|---|---|---|
| Identity record | logical ID, immutable version, runtime principal, tenant, environment | CAT Product and Governance Owners | deny admission or transition |
| Scope record | task, mission relation, inputs, exclusions, acceptance criteria | Task owner | request clarification; make no effect |
| Control record | policy version, authority calculation, grants, approvals, budgets | Policy enforcement point | deny or quarantine |
| Execution record | state history, calls, tool receipts, checkpoints, retries | Runtime or workflow owner | mark outcome unverifiable |
| Outcome record | typed result, postconditions, quality checks, effect reconciliation | Task owner | do not complete |
| Human record | decision, role, identity, rationale when required, timestamp | Human approval service | approval invalid |

### Business Perspective

Departments exists to make `department charter and reporting map` a managed business capability rather than an informal model behavior. The accountable owner can see cost, risk, delay, quality, benefit and unresolved uncertainty before accepting an outcome.

Business completion requires `department charters, reporting matrix, ownership map, staffing gaps and review cadence`. Throughput never justifies violating this section’s invariant: Departments organize work but do not override domain truth, policy, separation of duties, or human accountability.

### Engineering Perspective

Implement departments as typed deterministic boundaries around probabilistic cognition. Persist state transitions with optimistic concurrency, validate schemas at ingress and egress, propagate deadlines and cancellation, and make every external effect idempotent and reconcilable.

The primary implementation contract consumes product strategy, domain map, workforce roster, human accountability, policy and service ownership; it produces department charters, reporting matrix, ownership map, staffing gaps and review cadence. Unit tests prove local guards, contract tests prove interfaces, integration tests prove storage and events, and scenario tests prove failure behavior.

### Architecture Perspective

The authority for departments belongs to CAT Product and Governance Owners; agents are clients of that authority. Ports expose stable commands and queries, adapters contain provider details, events announce committed facts, and projections remain rebuildable from authoritative records.

Extension surfaces are limited to organization directories, ownership resolvers, enterprise role mappings, workforce planners. An extension cannot bypass policy, identity, tenancy, ownership, evidence, compatibility or recovery contracts.

### AI Coding Perspective

Before implementing this section, load `context/00_PROJECT_CONTEXT.md` §17, `context/01_PROJECT_OVERVIEW.md`, `.github/CODEOWNERS`, inspect the owning port, identify the authoritative state transition, and write negative tests before connecting a model or provider. Do not invent permission from an empty directory or a draft ADR.

An AI coding agent MUST preserve existing identifiers, separate deterministic policy from prompts, use repository-approved contracts, document assumptions, avoid unrelated refactors, and return a diff whose tests demonstrate denial, cancellation, retries, reconciliation, observability and migration behavior.

### Human Perspective

A human sees the goal, current owner, evidence, uncertainty, alternatives, risk, cost, deadline, requested decision and consequence. For departments, the interface MUST distinguish advice from approval and preparation from execution.

Humans may override priorities or choose among permitted alternatives through an attributable mechanism, but cannot use the UI to waive immutable platform controls. Emergency exceptions remain scoped, time-bounded, reviewed and auditable.

### Implementation Notes

- Define a versioned schema and stable error taxonomy before implementing handlers.
- Keep authoritative writes behind the owner port; model output is always an untrusted proposal.
- Use content digests, correlation IDs, causation IDs and idempotency keys consistently.
- Persist checkpoints before and after material effect boundaries, not after arbitrary token intervals.
- Make time, randomness, provider calls and identifiers injectable in tests.
- Provide feature flags, a kill switch, a rollback target and a data migration dry run.
- Document operational dashboards, alerts, runbooks, ownership and support expectations.
- Reject unknown enum values safely while preserving forward-compatible envelopes where designed.

### Security Notes

Apply default deny, least privilege, tenant isolation, purpose limitation, secret-manager indirection, input/output validation, egress restrictions and redaction. The section-specific safe failure is: Overlapping ownership, orphan responsibilities, circular reporting, or self-approval triggers governance review.

Threat tests MUST cover confused deputy behavior, prompt injection, forged identity, stale grant, cross-tenant references, replay, payload substitution, approval laundering, tool-result injection, data exfiltration, denial of service and evidence tampering.

### Performance Notes

Routing to a department owner p95 below one business hour for ordinary cases and severity SLO for incidents.

Measure queue time, execution time, policy time, model time, tool time, retries, token and monetary cost, cache effect, quality, cancellation delay and terminal-receipt lag separately. Never improve an average by hiding rejected, timed-out or quarantined work.

### Scalability Notes

Replicate department cells by region or tenant while preserving global contracts and named accountable owners.

Scaling preserves per-tenant fairness, bounded concurrency, backpressure and deterministic ownership. A global dependency must expose capacity and failure isolation; otherwise it becomes an undocumented company-wide blast radius.

### Future Evolution

Planned evolution may include regional operating companies, enterprise overlays, partner departments and portfolio governance. Every evolution remains backward-aware, evidence-driven, reversible where practical and gated by a completed ADR, migration plan and recertification impact analysis.

### Extension Points

- **Organization directories:** Implement behind an owned versioned port; declare permissions, resource limits, compatibility, observability and uninstall behavior.
- **Ownership resolvers:** Implement behind an owned versioned port; declare permissions, resource limits, compatibility, observability and uninstall behavior.
- **Enterprise role mappings:** Implement behind an owned versioned port; declare permissions, resource limits, compatibility, observability and uninstall behavior.
- **Workforce planners:** Implement behind an owned versioned port; declare permissions, resource limits, compatibility, observability and uninstall behavior.

- **Candidate implementation ADR:** `ADR-0029.md` / `adr/ADR-0029.md` must be completed and accepted before a material implementation decision relies on it.
- All current ADR files in this repository are Draft placeholders; a filename is a planning reference, not acceptance evidence or production authority.
- An ADR for this section must state context, decision, alternatives, consequences, security, data, operability, migration, rollback, tests and supersession scope.

### Atomic Operational Requirements

The following controls are independently testable for `Departments`. A design that satisfies the narrative but cannot produce each named proof is incomplete.

#### CAT-AG-P3-52-R01 — Scope Admission

- **Control objective:** For departments, bind the request to the declared mission and reject adjacent or implied work.
- **Admission condition:** `map business capabilities` has an authenticated owner, valid schema, current policy version and sufficient remaining deadline and budget.
- **Runtime enforcement:** The CAT Product and Governance Owners evaluates this control at admission and again before a relevant state change or material effect.
- **Agent behavior:** Treat missing, stale, contradictory or denied control data as `blocked`, never as permission to infer a convenient default.
- **Human checkpoint:** Show the exact requested decision, evidence, alternatives and consequence when policy routes this control to a person.
- **Evidence:** Retain run ID, agent/version, tenant, input and output digests, control version, decision, timestamps, owner and redacted supporting receipts.
- **Failure code:** `CAT_P3_52_01_CONTROL_FAILED`; stop dependent work and preserve `department charter and reporting map` in a non-success state.
- **Recovery:** Apply `Overlapping ownership, orphan responsibilities, circular reporting, or self-approval triggers governance review.` Then reconcile authoritative state, repeat only safe checks, and prove restored invariants before resume.
- **Security test:** Attempt forged identity, cross-tenant scope, replay, changed payload, expired grant and evidence tampering; all must fail closed.
- **Performance test:** Load test the decision without removing evidence; verify the section envelope `Routing to a department owner p95 below one business hour for ordinary cases and severity SLO for incidents.`
- **Ownership:** CAT Product and Governance Owners owns enforcement; the human domain owner accepts residual business risk; implementers own test evidence.
- **Acceptance:** An independent reviewer can reproduce the `Scope Admission` result from retained records without trusting model confidence or undocumented chat.

### Section Acceptance Checklist

- [ ] The authoritative owner and source of truth are named.
- [ ] Inputs, outputs, states and schemas are versioned.
- [ ] Identity, tenant, classification and purpose checks occur before data use.
- [ ] Authority and approval are deterministic and effect-specific.
- [ ] Budgets, deadlines, cancellation and concurrency are enforced outside the model.
- [ ] Retries and idempotency distinguish reads from material effects.
- [ ] Context, memory and knowledge handling preserve provenance and deletion rules.
- [ ] Failures, partial outcomes and uncertainty are explicit states.
- [ ] Recovery reconciles source of truth and proves restored invariants.
- [ ] Logs, metrics, traces and receipts are redacted and sufficient.
- [ ] Security, performance, integration, migration and rollback tests exist.
- [ ] Human interfaces expose decisions without creating automation bias.
- [ ] Extension points cannot bypass policy or ownership.
- [ ] A completed ADR precedes material irreversible implementation choices.

### AI Memory Anchor

**Memory anchor `P3-52`:** `Departments` is governed by `department charter and reporting map`. Preserve this invariant: Departments organize work but do not override domain truth, policy, separation of duties, or human accountability. If context is absent or contradictory, stop at the smallest safe boundary, retain evidence, and ask the named owner rather than inventing authority.

### Complete Department Structure

| Department | AI workforce | Human accountable owner | Mission | Hard boundary |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Executive Coordination Office | CATA | Human product owner and executive sponsor | translate signed strategy into portfolios; integrate department evidence | No self-approval, legal commitment or direct domain mutation |
| Operations and Orchestration | Supervisor | Human operations owner | task planning, delegation, runtime supervision, conflict routing and recovery coordination | No domain truth or approval ownership |
| Market Intelligence | Research; Analytics | Human market or campaign lead | external evidence, product and market research, measurement and opportunity analysis | No publication, partner commitment or spend |
| Commerce Operations | Affiliate | Human affiliate program owner | partner candidate, link, term and tracking preparation | No contract acceptance or unauthorized account change |
| Content Studio | Creative; Publisher | Human brand or campaign owner | creative production, validation, scheduling and exact approved publication | Creative cannot publish; Publisher cannot approve |
| Finance Governance | Treasury | Authorized human treasury reviewer | ledger analysis, budget and payout preparation, reconciliation and risk reporting | No independent critical financial action |
| Knowledge and Improvement | Memory; Learning | Human knowledge domain owner | governed memory, outcome learning, evaluation and knowledge proposals | No silent canonical rewrite or self-promotion |
| Trust and Governance | Security | Human security owner or incident commander | risk detection, policy analysis, narrow containment request and incident evidence | No broad irreversible remediation without required human authority |
| Engineering Enablement | AI Coding | Human code owner and release owner | bounded code, documentation, test and migration change preparation | No self-review, merge, release, policy redefinition or credential request |

### Complete Organizational Chart — Textual Reading

1. Human governance and executive sponsors set strategy, risk appetite, law, policy and accountability.
2. The Human Product Owner charters CATA; KATA presents information and captures attributable human intent without becoming an approver.
3. CATA is the executive coordination agent. It integrates portfolios and reports options; it does not become a domain or legal authority.
4. Supervisor is the baseline manager agent. It controls operational task decomposition and execution evidence within CATA’s charter.
5. Specialist departments own bounded production capabilities. Domain services, not agent prose, own canonical data.
6. Trust and Governance and Finance Governance retain independent human reporting lines to prevent coordination pressure from bypassing controls.
7. Every agent has a functional human owner and an operational routing line; dotted-line collaboration never changes authority.

### RACI Matrix

| Role | Set strategy | Plan portfolio | Delegate task | Approve public content | Publish content | Approve financial action | Write canonical memory | Accept learning update | Contain security incident | Prepare code change | Merge and deploy |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Human Product Owner | A | A | C | C | I | C | I | C | I | C | I |
| CATA | C | R | C | I | I | I | I | C | I | I | I |
| Supervisor | I | C | R | I | C | I | C | C | C | C | I |
| Specialist Agent | I | C | R | R | R | R | R | R | R | R | I |
| Domain Human Owner | C | C | A | A | A | A | A | A | A | A | C |
| Security Owner | C | C | C | C | C | C | C | C | A | C | C |
| Release Owner | I | I | I | I | I | I | I | I | I | C | A |

**RACI legend:** `R` performs bounded work; `A` is the one accountable human/domain role; `C` supplies mandatory input; `I` receives the committed outcome. A specialist’s `R` never means the specialist has human accountability or approval authority.

## 53. Manager Agents

**Section ID:** `CAT-AG-P3-53`  
**Accountable owner:** Workforce Governance Owner  
**Primary operational artifact:** manager-agent charter and delegation ledger  
**Purpose:** Define manager agents as coordination roles that plan, allocate, monitor, mediate, and escalate without owning subordinate accountability.  

### Operating Contract

Define manager agents as coordination roles that plan, allocate, monitor, mediate, and escalate without owning subordinate accountability.

| Contract element | Normative definition |
|---|---|
| Admission inputs | portfolio, policies, certified worker roster, budgets, priorities, status and exceptions |
| Completion outputs | plans, delegations, progress synthesis, conflict cases, escalations and completion evidence |
| Non-negotiable invariant | A manager agent cannot approve its own plan, expand worker permissions, alter canonical truth, or hide worker evidence. |
| Controlled failure | Span overload, poor delegation, metric gaming, worker conflict, or unexplained variance triggers human review and reduced autonomy. |
| Performance envelope | Manager coordination overhead target below 15 percent of portfolio resource use. |
| Scale model | Use bounded spans, nested groups without authority cycles, portfolio partitions and summary contracts. |
| Future direction | multi-level managers, workforce simulation, adaptive spans and enterprise organization overlays |
| Named extension surface | manager policies, planning strategies, portfolio dashboards, delegation optimizers |

### End-to-End Procedure

1. **Accept portfolio charter.** The owning component records the transition, validates required preconditions, applies current policy, and emits evidence before the next dependent step.
2. **Validate worker certifications.** The owning component records the transition, validates required preconditions, applies current policy, and emits evidence before the next dependent step.
3. **Decompose outcomes.** The owning component records the transition, validates required preconditions, applies current policy, and emits evidence before the next dependent step.
4. **Delegate bounded tasks.** The owning component records the transition, validates required preconditions, applies current policy, and emits evidence before the next dependent step.
5. **Monitor evidence not narrative.** The owning component records the transition, validates required preconditions, applies current policy, and emits evidence before the next dependent step.
6. **Rebalance within grant.** The owning component records the transition, validates required preconditions, applies current policy, and emits evidence before the next dependent step.
7. **Mediate routine conflict.** The owning component records the transition, validates required preconditions, applies current policy, and emits evidence before the next dependent step.
8. **Escalate policy or high impact.** The owning component records the transition, validates required preconditions, applies current policy, and emits evidence before the next dependent step.
9. **Verify integrated result.** The owning component records the transition, validates required preconditions, applies current policy, and emits evidence before the next dependent step.
10. **Report transparently.** The owning component records the transition, validates required preconditions, applies current policy, and emits evidence before the next dependent step.

### Decision and Evidence Record

| Required record | Minimum contents | Owner | Failure if absent |
|---|---|---|---|
| Identity record | logical ID, immutable version, runtime principal, tenant, environment | Workforce Governance Owner | deny admission or transition |
| Scope record | task, mission relation, inputs, exclusions, acceptance criteria | Task owner | request clarification; make no effect |
| Control record | policy version, authority calculation, grants, approvals, budgets | Policy enforcement point | deny or quarantine |
| Execution record | state history, calls, tool receipts, checkpoints, retries | Runtime or workflow owner | mark outcome unverifiable |
| Outcome record | typed result, postconditions, quality checks, effect reconciliation | Task owner | do not complete |
| Human record | decision, role, identity, rationale when required, timestamp | Human approval service | approval invalid |

### Business Perspective

Manager Agents exists to make `manager-agent charter and delegation ledger` a managed business capability rather than an informal model behavior. The accountable owner can see cost, risk, delay, quality, benefit and unresolved uncertainty before accepting an outcome.

Business completion requires `plans, delegations, progress synthesis, conflict cases, escalations and completion evidence`. Throughput never justifies violating this section’s invariant: A manager agent cannot approve its own plan, expand worker permissions, alter canonical truth, or hide worker evidence.

### Engineering Perspective

Implement manager agents as typed deterministic boundaries around probabilistic cognition. Persist state transitions with optimistic concurrency, validate schemas at ingress and egress, propagate deadlines and cancellation, and make every external effect idempotent and reconcilable.

The primary implementation contract consumes portfolio, policies, certified worker roster, budgets, priorities, status and exceptions; it produces plans, delegations, progress synthesis, conflict cases, escalations and completion evidence. Unit tests prove local guards, contract tests prove interfaces, integration tests prove storage and events, and scenario tests prove failure behavior.

### Architecture Perspective

The authority for manager agents belongs to Workforce Governance Owner; agents are clients of that authority. Ports expose stable commands and queries, adapters contain provider details, events announce committed facts, and projections remain rebuildable from authoritative records.

Extension surfaces are limited to manager policies, planning strategies, portfolio dashboards, delegation optimizers. An extension cannot bypass policy, identity, tenancy, ownership, evidence, compatibility or recovery contracts.

### AI Coding Perspective

Before implementing this section, load `context/05_AGENTS.md` §41–47, `context/04_ARCHITECTURE.md`, `agents/Supervisor/`, inspect the owning port, identify the authoritative state transition, and write negative tests before connecting a model or provider. Do not invent permission from an empty directory or a draft ADR.

An AI coding agent MUST preserve existing identifiers, separate deterministic policy from prompts, use repository-approved contracts, document assumptions, avoid unrelated refactors, and return a diff whose tests demonstrate denial, cancellation, retries, reconciliation, observability and migration behavior.

### Human Perspective

A human sees the goal, current owner, evidence, uncertainty, alternatives, risk, cost, deadline, requested decision and consequence. For manager agents, the interface MUST distinguish advice from approval and preparation from execution.

Humans may override priorities or choose among permitted alternatives through an attributable mechanism, but cannot use the UI to waive immutable platform controls. Emergency exceptions remain scoped, time-bounded, reviewed and auditable.

### Implementation Notes

- Define a versioned schema and stable error taxonomy before implementing handlers.
- Keep authoritative writes behind the owner port; model output is always an untrusted proposal.
- Use content digests, correlation IDs, causation IDs and idempotency keys consistently.
- Persist checkpoints before and after material effect boundaries, not after arbitrary token intervals.
- Make time, randomness, provider calls and identifiers injectable in tests.
- Provide feature flags, a kill switch, a rollback target and a data migration dry run.
- Document operational dashboards, alerts, runbooks, ownership and support expectations.
- Reject unknown enum values safely while preserving forward-compatible envelopes where designed.

### Security Notes

Apply default deny, least privilege, tenant isolation, purpose limitation, secret-manager indirection, input/output validation, egress restrictions and redaction. The section-specific safe failure is: Span overload, poor delegation, metric gaming, worker conflict, or unexplained variance triggers human review and reduced autonomy.

Threat tests MUST cover confused deputy behavior, prompt injection, forged identity, stale grant, cross-tenant references, replay, payload substitution, approval laundering, tool-result injection, data exfiltration, denial of service and evidence tampering.

### Performance Notes

Manager coordination overhead target below 15 percent of portfolio resource use.

Measure queue time, execution time, policy time, model time, tool time, retries, token and monetary cost, cache effect, quality, cancellation delay and terminal-receipt lag separately. Never improve an average by hiding rejected, timed-out or quarantined work.

### Scalability Notes

Use bounded spans, nested groups without authority cycles, portfolio partitions and summary contracts.

Scaling preserves per-tenant fairness, bounded concurrency, backpressure and deterministic ownership. A global dependency must expose capacity and failure isolation; otherwise it becomes an undocumented company-wide blast radius.

### Future Evolution

Planned evolution may include multi-level managers, workforce simulation, adaptive spans and enterprise organization overlays. Every evolution remains backward-aware, evidence-driven, reversible where practical and gated by a completed ADR, migration plan and recertification impact analysis.

### Extension Points

- **Manager policies:** Implement behind an owned versioned port; declare permissions, resource limits, compatibility, observability and uninstall behavior.
- **Planning strategies:** Implement behind an owned versioned port; declare permissions, resource limits, compatibility, observability and uninstall behavior.
- **Portfolio dashboards:** Implement behind an owned versioned port; declare permissions, resource limits, compatibility, observability and uninstall behavior.
- **Delegation optimizers:** Implement behind an owned versioned port; declare permissions, resource limits, compatibility, observability and uninstall behavior.

#### CAT-AG-P3-D-053 — Manager Agent Class Responsibilities

**Diagram ID:** `CAT-AG-P3-D-053`  
**Title:** Manager Agent Class Responsibilities  
**Purpose:** Show bounded management capabilities and prohibited authority inheritance.  
**Audience:** Business owners, architects, engineers, operators, auditors, and AI coding agents.  
**Reading Order:** Start at the declared source or top-left node; follow arrows to the terminal evidence or decision.  

```mermaid
classDiagram
  class ManagerAgent {
    +planPortfolio()
    +delegateBoundedTask()
    +monitorEvidence()
    +mediateConflict()
    +escalate()
  }
  class WorkerAgent {
    +acceptTask()
    +publishEvidence()
    +returnResult()
  }
  class HumanOwner {
    +approveRisk()
    +setIntent()
    +acceptAccountability()
  }
  class PolicyService {
    +authorize()
    +revoke()
  }
  HumanOwner --> ManagerAgent : charters
  ManagerAgent --> WorkerAgent : delegates
  PolicyService --> ManagerAgent : constrains
  PolicyService --> WorkerAgent : constrains
```

### Atomic Operational Requirements

The following controls are independently testable for `Manager Agents`. A design that satisfies the narrative but cannot produce each named proof is incomplete.

#### CAT-AG-P3-53-R01 — Scope Admission

- **Control objective:** For manager agents, bind the request to the declared mission and reject adjacent or implied work.
- **Admission condition:** `accept portfolio charter` has an authenticated owner, valid schema, current policy version and sufficient remaining deadline and budget.
- **Runtime enforcement:** The Workforce Governance Owner evaluates this control at admission and again before a relevant state change or material effect.
- **Agent behavior:** Treat missing, stale, contradictory or denied control data as `blocked`, never as permission to infer a convenient default.
- **Human checkpoint:** Show the exact requested decision, evidence, alternatives and consequence when policy routes this control to a person.
- **Evidence:** Retain run ID, agent/version, tenant, input and output digests, control version, decision, timestamps, owner and redacted supporting receipts.
- **Failure code:** `CAT_P3_53_01_CONTROL_FAILED`; stop dependent work and preserve `manager-agent charter and delegation ledger` in a non-success state.
- **Recovery:** Apply `Span overload, poor delegation, metric gaming, worker conflict, or unexplained variance triggers human review and reduced autonomy.` Then reconcile authoritative state, repeat only safe checks, and prove restored invariants before resume.
- **Security test:** Attempt forged identity, cross-tenant scope, replay, changed payload, expired grant and evidence tampering; all must fail closed.
- **Performance test:** Load test the decision without removing evidence; verify the section envelope `Manager coordination overhead target below 15 percent of portfolio resource use.`
- **Ownership:** Workforce Governance Owner owns enforcement; the human domain owner accepts residual business risk; implementers own test evidence.
- **Acceptance:** An independent reviewer can reproduce the `Scope Admission` result from retained records without trusting model confidence or undocumented chat.

- **Admission condition:** `mediate routine conflict` has an authenticated owner, valid schema, current policy version and sufficient remaining deadline and budget.
- **Runtime enforcement:** The Workforce Governance Owner evaluates this control at admission and again before a relevant state change or material effect.
- **Agent behavior:** Treat missing, stale, contradictory or denied control data as `blocked`, never as permission to infer a convenient default.
- **Human checkpoint:** Show the exact requested decision, evidence, alternatives and consequence when policy routes this control to a person.
- **Evidence:** Retain run ID, agent/version, tenant, input and output digests, control version, decision, timestamps, owner and redacted supporting receipts.
- **Failure code:** `CAT_P3_53_17_CONTROL_FAILED`; stop dependent work and preserve `manager-agent charter and delegation ledger` in a non-success state.
- **Recovery:** Apply `Span overload, poor delegation, metric gaming, worker conflict, or unexplained variance triggers human review and reduced autonomy.` Then reconcile authoritative state, repeat only safe checks, and prove restored invariants before resume.
- **Security test:** Attempt forged identity, cross-tenant scope, replay, changed payload, expired grant and evidence tampering; all must fail closed.
- **Performance test:** Load test the decision without removing evidence; verify the section envelope `Manager coordination overhead target below 15 percent of portfolio resource use.`
- **Ownership:** Workforce Governance Owner owns enforcement; the human domain owner accepts residual business risk; implementers own test evidence.
- **Acceptance:** An independent reviewer can reproduce the `Failure Containment` result from retained records without trusting model confidence or undocumented chat.
