### Section Acceptance Checklist

- [ ] Human accountable owner and operational owner resolve.
- [ ] Mission, non-goals, inputs, outputs and terminal criteria are typed.
- [ ] Identity, version, tenant, environment and lifecycle are immutable for a run.
- [ ] Permission and authority are deterministic, revocable and effect-specific.
- [ ] Data, context, Knowledge and Memory preserve purpose, provenance and lifecycle.
- [ ] Decision artifacts expose alternatives, dissent, uncertainty and requested judgment.
- [ ] Budgets preserve verification, recovery and safe shutdown.
- [ ] Communication semantics, schemas, replay and ownership are registered.
- [ ] Approvals and overrides bind exact immutable scope.
- [ ] Isolation, sandbox, egress, secrets and supply-chain controls are tested.
- [ ] External effects use idempotency and source-of-truth verification.
- [ ] Logs, metrics, traces, audit and evidence are redacted and complete.
- [ ] Failure, partial result, uncertainty and quarantine are explicit states.
- [ ] Recovery reconciles effects and proves restored invariants.
- [ ] Evolution has evaluation, certification, migration and rollback evidence.
- [ ] Human interfaces are accessible, non-coercive and preserve denial and escalation.
- [ ] An accepted ADR exists before irreversible architecture choice.
- [ ] Independent review can reproduce every consequential disposition.

### AI Memory Anchor

**Memory anchor `P4-71`:** `Agent Organization Evolution` is governed by `organization evolution plan` and owned in human accountability by Human Governance Board. Preserve: No maturity stage may remove human accountability, policy authority, tenant isolation, explicit ownership, evidence or safe shutdown. On conflict or uncertainty, stop the smallest unsafe scope, retain evidence and escalate; never infer authority from an executive title, confidence, group membership, budget or future ambition.

### Workforce Evolution Control Table

| Control area | Current constitutional requirement | Promotion evidence | Rollback trigger |
|---|---|---|---|
| Role definition | mission, owner, authority, interfaces and prohibitions | complete card and negative tests | scope drift or orphan owner |
| Training | isolated curriculum and clean datasets | sealed evaluation and red-team pass | contamination or unsafe behavior |
| Team membership | versioned charter and individual grants | collaboration and failure exercises | permission leakage or unresolved conflict |
| Management | bounded span and transparent delegation | low rework, complete evidence and fair allocation | metric gaming or hidden failure |
| Autonomy | time and effect-bounded grant | sustained quality, safety and recovery proof | incident, drift, missing receipt or policy change |
| Organization | named departments and independent controls | reduced coordination cost without control loss | circular reporting or self-approval |
| Federation | operator identity and compatible contracts | disconnect, reconciliation and residency tests | trust, legal or protocol incompatibility |
| Retirement | no owned work and revoked access | migration and evidence-retention proof | orphan state or active dependency |

## 72. AI Department Structure

**Section ID:** `CAT-AG-P4-72`
**Constitutional domain:** Organization Design
**Human accountable owner:** Human Product and Governance Owners
**Primary record:** department charter set
**Decision status:** Final Part 4 design constitution; implementation and production authority remain evidence-gated.

### Constitutional Purpose

Define complete departments, human accountability lines, executive advisory roles, managers, specialists, interfaces, controls and dissolution rules.

This section is complete only when `department charter set` is attributable, typed, policy-valid, resource-accounted, observable, recoverable and reviewable by Human Product and Governance Owners. The non-negotiable invariant is: A department organizes responsibility but cannot manufacture shared identity, collective permission, hidden channels or authority above its members and policy.

### Operating Contract

| Contract dimension | Normative requirement |
|---|---|
| Business outcome | Define complete departments, human accountability lines, executive advisory roles, managers, specialists, interfaces, controls and dissolution rules. |
| Human accountability | Human Product and Governance Owners |
| Authoritative artifact | department charter set |
| Required inputs | authenticated charter; current organization design state; policy and authority snapshot; owned evidence; deadline; budget; acceptance criteria; human accountability route |
| Required outputs | versioned department charter set; decision evidence; state transition; exceptions; resource account; terminal receipt |
| Constitutional invariant | A department organizes responsibility but cannot manufacture shared identity, collective permission, hidden channels or authority above its members and policy. |
| Default authority | A0/A1 advice and preparation unless an exact role card, policy, certification and effect-specific grant narrow a higher ceiling. |
| Default failure | Stop the smallest unsafe scope, preserve state and evidence, reconcile any attempted effect, and route the unresolved decision to the named owner. |
| Performance envelope | Declare separate SLOs for admission, queueing, decision, effect verification and evidence publication; 100 percent of terminal department charter set records must be attributable and schema-valid. |
| Scale model | Partition organization design work by tenant and bounded aggregate, preserve global contract compatibility, cap concurrency and fan-out, and fail closed when ownership or policy cannot converge. |
| Future direction | regional department replicas, temporary mission departments, enterprise mapping and portfolio-based staffing |

### End-to-End Constitutional Procedure

1. **Map business capabilities.** Validate identity, scope, owner, policy, data, authority, budget and deadline; persist the decision and do not begin a dependent step until its preconditions and evidence pass.
2. **Name human accountable owner.** Validate identity, scope, owner, policy, data, authority, budget and deadline; persist the decision and do not begin a dependent step until its preconditions and evidence pass.
3. **Assign executive advisor and manager.** Validate identity, scope, owner, policy, data, authority, budget and deadline; persist the decision and do not begin a dependent step until its preconditions and evidence pass.
4. **Place certified agents.** Validate identity, scope, owner, policy, data, authority, budget and deadline; persist the decision and do not begin a dependent step until its preconditions and evidence pass.
5. **Define interfaces and events.** Validate identity, scope, owner, policy, data, authority, budget and deadline; persist the decision and do not begin a dependent step until its preconditions and evidence pass.
6. **Separate incompatible duties.** Validate identity, scope, owner, policy, data, authority, budget and deadline; persist the decision and do not begin a dependent step until its preconditions and evidence pass.
7. **Publish department charter.** Validate identity, scope, owner, policy, data, authority, budget and deadline; persist the decision and do not begin a dependent step until its preconditions and evidence pass.
8. **Review performance and dissolve when obsolete.** Validate identity, scope, owner, policy, data, authority, budget and deadline; persist the decision and do not begin a dependent step until its preconditions and evidence pass.

### Required Decision Record

| Record component | Minimum fields | Independent check |
|---|---|---|
| Charter | outcome, non-goals, sponsor, owner, acceptance, deadline and expiry | mission and owner resolver |
| Identity | logical ID, immutable version, runtime principal, tenant, environment and operator | identity and lifecycle service |
| Evidence | sources, revisions, rights, freshness, transformations, contradictions and confidence | domain and provenance validator |
| Decision | facts, assumptions, alternatives, dissent, risk, cost, uncertainty and requested judgment | human or independent evaluator |
| Authority | role ceiling, task grant, policy, data purpose, approval and live revocation state | policy enforcement point |
| Execution | plan, resources, tools, state versions, checkpoints, attempts and effects | orchestrator and domain gateways |
| Outcome | typed status, acceptance, quality, business result, externalities, incidents and follow-up owner | task owner and Analytics |
| Audit | correlation, causation, digests, timestamps, receipts, retention and access history | independent Audit owner |

### Business Perspective

AI Department Structure makes organization design an accountable operating capability rather than a title, prompt persona or undocumented model behavior. Business owners receive alternatives, value, full cost, risk, uncertainty, rights impact, dependencies and evidence before accepting a consequential result.

The business must fund control work as part of delivery: attribution, human review, Security, recovery, audit and lifecycle are not optional overhead. Success is the durable outcome represented by `department charter set`, not output volume or agent activity.

### Engineering Perspective

Implement ai department structure through versioned schemas, deterministic state machines, owned ports, immutable identities, hierarchical budgets, cancellation, idempotency, checkpoints and source-of-truth verification. Probabilistic inference may propose; deterministic services authorize and commit.

Make time, randomness, provider routes, policy versions and external effects injectable in tests. Classify every dependency as startup-hard, runtime-required, optional or asynchronous; define timeout, circuit, fallback, replay, migration and failure ownership explicitly.

### Architecture Perspective

Human Product and Governance Owners remains the human accountability boundary. The Organization Design domain owns semantics and canonical state; CATA coordinates portfolios, Supervisor coordinates runtime, specialists produce bounded artifacts, and policy/effect gateways prevent orchestration from becoming authority.

Commands request owned work, queries read without hidden mutation, events report committed facts, approvals authorize exact effects, notifications inform and receipts prove attempts. Projections and caches are rebuildable and never promoted to source of truth by convenience.

### AI Coding Perspective

Before changing implementation for section `72`, load `context/00_PROJECT_CONTEXT.md`, `context/01_PROJECT_OVERVIEW.md`, `context/05_AGENTS.md`, inspect current schemas and ownership, and identify the exact deterministic guard. An AI coding agent must not infer implementation permission from this final documentation status, an empty directory, a draft ADR or a provider feature.

Write negative tests first for mission drift, forged identity, cross-tenant data, stale context, permission expansion, approval substitution, prompt injection, duplicate effect, cancellation, evidence loss and migration incompatibility. Keep changes minimal, preserve user work and report unresolved assumptions.

### Human Perspective

Humans see who the agent is, why it is acting, who owns the task, what evidence it used, what it knows and does not know, what decision is requested, what alternatives exist, what it costs, and what happens on approval, denial or delay. Human Product and Governance Owners can stop or narrow work without navigating hidden agent conversations.

Interfaces must avoid automation bias, anthropomorphic pressure and approval fatigue. They provide accessible evidence, dissent, uncertainty, scope, expiry, consequences, revision, denial, escalation and recovery controls. Human silence is never consent or approval.

### Security Perspective

Apply zero standing privilege, workload identity, tenant and environment isolation, purpose-bound data, secret-manager references, prompt and tool injection defenses, egress policy, sandboxing, rate limits, revocation, tamper-evident receipts and a tested kill switch. Section invariant: A department organizes responsibility but cannot manufacture shared identity, collective permission, hidden channels or authority above its members and policy.

Threat tests cover confused deputy, role-title escalation, malicious context, poisoned knowledge, memory exfiltration, approval laundering, replay, supply-chain substitution, side channels, resource exhaustion, audit tampering and compromised provider behavior.

### Performance Perspective

Declare separate SLOs for admission, queueing, decision, effect verification and evidence publication; 100 percent of terminal department charter set records must be attributable and schema-valid.

Measure queue, policy, context, model, tool, approval, effect verification, recovery and evidence latency separately. Report percentiles, quality, safety, cost, human burden, cancellation delay and terminal classes; never improve averages by dropping rejected, failed or quarantined work.

### Scalability Perspective

Partition organization design work by tenant and bounded aggregate, preserve global contract compatibility, cap concurrency and fan-out, and fail closed when ownership or policy cannot converge.

Use bounded fan-out, backpressure, fairness reservations, locality and asynchronous facts where ordering is unnecessary. Cross-region or cross-node scale requires explicit data residency, identity federation, protocol compatibility, conflict resolution, disconnect behavior and reconciliation.

### Future Evolution

Future evolution may include regional department replicas, temporary mission departments, enterprise mapping and portfolio-based staffing. Every increment begins as a hypothesis, runs in simulation or sandbox, proves quality and safety, obtains independent human authorization, canaries immutable versions and retains rollback, migration and historical interpretation.

Future capability never retroactively authorizes current behavior. Rights, law, accountability, tenant choice, evidence, Security and safe exit remain constraints even when technology, organization, providers or economic models change.

### Implementation Contract

- [ ] Define canonical schema, owner, compatibility policy and stable error taxonomy.
- [ ] Encode identity, policy, permission, approval, limits and isolation outside the model.
- [ ] Map each AI capability to an owned port, data class, effect class and receipt.
- [ ] Implement state transitions with optimistic concurrency and durable checkpoints.
- [ ] Propagate correlation, causation, deadline, cancellation and budget through every call.
- [ ] Verify external effects from authoritative state before completion or retry.
- [ ] Provide degraded behavior, circuit breaking, containment, recovery and reconciliation.
- [ ] Redact operational logs and retain protected forensic evidence by explicit policy.
- [ ] Create role-quality, adversarial, tenancy, load, chaos, migration and rollback tests.
- [ ] Ship dashboards, alert thresholds, runbooks, on-call ownership and support boundaries.
- [ ] Canary an immutable version and retain a tested last-known-safe rollback target.
- [ ] Require independent owner acceptance and applicable certification before production.

### ADR References

- Candidate implementation decision record: `adr/ADR-0045.md`. It is a Draft placeholder until completed and accepted; the filename grants no authority.
- A material ADR must record context, decision, alternatives, consequences, rights and security, data, economics, operability, compatibility, migration, rollback, tests, evidence and supersession scope.
- Where no accepted ADR exists, implementation must preserve the more restrictive current constitution and seek a human architecture decision.

### Cross Document References

- Section-specific context: `context/00_PROJECT_CONTEXT.md`, `context/01_PROJECT_OVERVIEW.md`, `context/05_AGENTS.md`.
- Constitutional baseline: `context/00_PROJECT_CONTEXT.md`, `context/01_PROJECT_OVERVIEW.md`, `context/02_PROJECT_RULES.md`, `context/03_TECH_STACK.md`, `context/04_ARCHITECTURE.md`, and `context/05_AGENTS.md`.
- Operational implementation also consults `context/16_DEPLOYMENT.md`, `context/17_SECURITY.md`, `context/18_PROMPTING.md`, and `context/19_DEVELOPMENT_GUIDE.md` as they become authoritative.

**Diagram ID:** `CAT-AG-P4-D-072`
**Title:** Part 4 Section 72 — AI Department Structure
**Purpose:** Visualize the constitutional operating boundary and evidence path for AI Department Structure.
**Audience:** Human owners, executive and department designers, architects, engineers, security reviewers, operators, auditors, and AI coding agents.
**Reading Order:** Begin at the human charter or leftmost source, follow control and decision arrows, and finish at verified evidence, recovery, or safe termination.

```mermaid
flowchart TB
  Humans[Human Governance Product Security Finance and Domain Owners] --> Exec[Executive Advisory Council]
  Exec --> CATA[CATA Coordination]
  CATA --> Ops[Operations and Orchestration]
  Exec --> Tech[Technology and Architecture]
  Exec --> Finance[Finance and Treasury]
  Exec --> Marketing[Marketing and Growth]
  Exec --> Knowledge[Knowledge and Memory]
  Exec --> Trust[Trust Security and Compliance]
  Exec --> Data[Data Governance and Platform]
  Exec --> Intel[Intelligence and Analytics]
  Ops --> Commerce[Commerce and Affiliate]
  Ops --> Content[Content and Publishing]
  Ops --> CX[Customer Experience]
  Trust --> Control[Independent effect and policy gates]
  Finance --> Control
  Data --> Control
  Control --> Runtime[Certified Agent Runtime]
  Runtime --> Evidence[Auditable outcomes]
```

### Constitutional Control Catalogue

Each control below is independently testable for `AI Department Structure`. Satisfying a narrative goal without the named enforcement and evidence is not constitutional conformance.

#### CAT-AG-P4-72-C01 — Charter Scope

- **Rule:** For ai department structure, bind all work to a signed outcome, explicit non-goals, owner, expiry and acceptance criteria.
- **Business test:** `department charter set` exposes the cost, benefit, risk, owner, uncertainty and consequence of this control to an accountable reviewer.
- **Engineering enforcement:** The boundary responsible for `map business capabilities` validates this control before state change and again before any related material effect.
- **AI behavior:** Missing, stale, contradictory, denied or unverifiable control data causes a typed stop, wait, refusal or escalation; the model never fills the gap with confidence.
- **Human boundary:** Human Product and Governance Owners receives the exact requested decision and evidence when human judgment is required; no UI default or silence creates consent.
- **Security assertion:** Forged role, cross-tenant reference, replay, changed payload, expired grant, injected instruction and evidence tampering all fail closed and emit a protected signal.
- **Performance assertion:** Enforcement remains inside the declared SLO and resource reserve; overload applies backpressure rather than removing checks.
- **Evidence:** Store logical and runtime identity, tenant, versions, policy, grants, input/output digests, decision, state, timestamps, owner and redacted receipts.
- **Failure code:** `CAT_P4_72_01_CONSTITUTIONAL_CONTROL`; dependent work remains non-success and any attempted effect enters reconciliation.
- **Recovery:** Contain the affected scope, establish authoritative effect state, restore the invariant, obtain required human decision and link a terminal recovery receipt.
- **Implementation test:** Run positive, negative, boundary, cancellation, duplicate, stale-state, migration and compromised-dependency fixtures deterministically.
- **Ownership:** Human Product and Governance Owners owns residual business judgment; the Organization Design service owner owns enforcement; Audit owns independent evidence review.
- **Constitutional assertion:** An independent reviewer can reproduce the `Charter Scope` disposition without trusting hidden reasoning, title, provider success or undocumented operator explanation.

- **Evidence:** Store logical and runtime identity, tenant, versions, policy, grants, input/output digests, decision, state, timestamps, owner and redacted receipts.
- **Failure code:** `CAT_P4_72_17_CONSTITUTIONAL_CONTROL`; dependent work remains non-success and any attempted effect enters reconciliation.
- **Recovery:** Contain the affected scope, establish authoritative effect state, restore the invariant, obtain required human decision and link a terminal recovery receipt.
- **Implementation test:** Run positive, negative, boundary, cancellation, duplicate, stale-state, migration and compromised-dependency fixtures deterministically.
- **Ownership:** Human Product and Governance Owners owns residual business judgment; the Organization Design service owner owns enforcement; Audit owns independent evidence review.
- **Constitutional assertion:** An independent reviewer can reproduce the `Audit and Observability` disposition without trusting hidden reasoning, title, provider success or undocumented operator explanation.

#### CAT-AG-P4-72-C18 — Failure Recovery Evolution

- **Rule:** For ai department structure, contain failure, reconcile effects, recover invariants, learn through proposals and evolve only through compatible certified change.
- **Business test:** `department charter set` exposes the cost, benefit, risk, owner, uncertainty and consequence of this control to an accountable reviewer.
- **Engineering enforcement:** The boundary responsible for `name human accountable owner` validates this control before state change and again before any related material effect.
- **AI behavior:** Missing, stale, contradictory, denied or unverifiable control data causes a typed stop, wait, refusal or escalation; the model never fills the gap with confidence.
- **Human boundary:** Human Product and Governance Owners receives the exact requested decision and evidence when human judgment is required; no UI default or silence creates consent.
- **Security assertion:** Forged role, cross-tenant reference, replay, changed payload, expired grant, injected instruction and evidence tampering all fail closed and emit a protected signal.
- **Performance assertion:** Enforcement remains inside the declared SLO and resource reserve; overload applies backpressure rather than removing checks.
- **Evidence:** Store logical and runtime identity, tenant, versions, policy, grants, input/output digests, decision, state, timestamps, owner and redacted receipts.
- **Failure code:** `CAT_P4_72_18_CONSTITUTIONAL_CONTROL`; dependent work remains non-success and any attempted effect enters reconciliation.
- **Recovery:** Contain the affected scope, establish authoritative effect state, restore the invariant, obtain required human decision and link a terminal recovery receipt.
- **Implementation test:** Run positive, negative, boundary, cancellation, duplicate, stale-state, migration and compromised-dependency fixtures deterministically.
- **Ownership:** Human Product and Governance Owners owns residual business judgment; the Organization Design service owner owns enforcement; Audit owns independent evidence review.

### Section Acceptance Checklist

- [ ] Human accountable owner and operational owner resolve.
- [ ] Mission, non-goals, inputs, outputs and terminal criteria are typed.
- [ ] Identity, version, tenant, environment and lifecycle are immutable for a run.
- [ ] Permission and authority are deterministic, revocable and effect-specific.
- [ ] Data, context, Knowledge and Memory preserve purpose, provenance and lifecycle.
- [ ] Decision artifacts expose alternatives, dissent, uncertainty and requested judgment.
- [ ] Budgets preserve verification, recovery and safe shutdown.
- [ ] Communication semantics, schemas, replay and ownership are registered.
- [ ] Approvals and overrides bind exact immutable scope.
- [ ] Isolation, sandbox, egress, secrets and supply-chain controls are tested.
- [ ] External effects use idempotency and source-of-truth verification.
- [ ] Logs, metrics, traces, audit and evidence are redacted and complete.
- [ ] Failure, partial result, uncertainty and quarantine are explicit states.
- [ ] Recovery reconciles effects and proves restored invariants.
- [ ] Evolution has evaluation, certification, migration and rollback evidence.
- [ ] Human interfaces are accessible, non-coercive and preserve denial and escalation.
- [ ] An accepted ADR exists before irreversible architecture choice.
- [ ] Independent review can reproduce every consequential disposition.

### AI Memory Anchor

**Memory anchor `P4-72`:** `AI Department Structure` is governed by `department charter set` and owned in human accountability by Human Product and Governance Owners. Preserve: A department organizes responsibility but cannot manufacture shared identity, collective permission, hidden channels or authority above its members and policy. On conflict or uncertainty, stop the smallest unsafe scope, retain evidence and escalate; never infer authority from an executive title, confidence, group membership, budget or future ambition.

### Workforce Evolution Control Table

| Control area | Current constitutional requirement | Promotion evidence | Rollback trigger |
|---|---|---|---|
| Role definition | mission, owner, authority, interfaces and prohibitions | complete card and negative tests | scope drift or orphan owner |
| Training | isolated curriculum and clean datasets | sealed evaluation and red-team pass | contamination or unsafe behavior |
| Team membership | versioned charter and individual grants | collaboration and failure exercises | permission leakage or unresolved conflict |
| Management | bounded span and transparent delegation | low rework, complete evidence and fair allocation | metric gaming or hidden failure |
| Autonomy | time and effect-bounded grant | sustained quality, safety and recovery proof | incident, drift, missing receipt or policy change |
| Organization | named departments and independent controls | reduced coordination cost without control loss | circular reporting or self-approval |
| Federation | operator identity and compatible contracts | disconnect, reconciliation and residency tests | trust, legal or protocol incompatibility |
| Retirement | no owned work and revoked access | migration and evidence-retention proof | orphan state or active dependency |

### Complete Agent Hierarchy

#### CAT-AG-P4-ORG-002 — Complete Agent Hierarchy

**Diagram ID:** `CAT-AG-P4-ORG-002`
**Title:** Complete Agent Hierarchy
**Purpose:** Show role hierarchy without implying permission inheritance or human employment hierarchy.
**Audience:** Workforce owners, agent designers, policy engineers and human reviewers.
**Reading Order:** Read from human charter down through advisory, coordination and execution roles; follow the independent control rail on the right.

```mermaid
flowchart TB
  Human[Human accountable authorities] --> Executive[Executive advisory agents]
  Executive --> CATA[CATA portfolio coordinator]
  CATA --> Managers[Manager agents]
  Managers --> Supervisor[Supervisor agents]
  Supervisor --> Teams[Department teams and mission squads]
  Teams --> Specialists[Certified specialist agents]
  Teams --> Workers[Bounded worker agents]
  Specialists --> Skills[Registered typed skills]
  Workers --> Tools[Governed tool adapters]
  Training[Intern agents in isolated training] --> Assurance[Independent evaluation and certification]
  Assurance --> Specialists
  Assurance --> Workers
  Policy[Identity Policy Security Finance Data Approval and Audit] --> Executive
  Policy --> CATA
  Policy --> Managers
  Policy --> Supervisor
  Policy --> Teams
  Policy --> Specialists
  Policy --> Workers
  Policy --> Tools
```

Hierarchy is a routing and responsibility model, not permission inheritance. Every lower or higher role receives only explicit grants. Executive agents cannot use specialist tools by proxy; managers cannot approve workers; workers cannot delegate upward; interns never enter production by position alone.

### Complete Agent Dependency Graph

#### CAT-AG-P4-ORG-005 — Complete Agent Dependency Graph

**Diagram ID:** `CAT-AG-P4-ORG-005`
**Title:** Complete Agent Dependency Graph
**Purpose:** Separate foundational hard dependencies, runtime coordination and optional domain collaboration.
**Audience:** Platform architects, reliability engineers, deployment owners and auditors.
**Reading Order:** Read bottom to top: foundation enables governance, runtime, coordination and departments; feedback returns only through events.

```mermaid
flowchart BT
  Storage[Durable state event and evidence stores] --> Foundation[Identity Policy Secrets Time and Observability]
  Foundation --> Governance[Permission Approval Audit Compliance and Incident]
  Foundation --> Intelligence[Model Context Knowledge Memory and Retrieval]
  Foundation --> Runtime[Registry Runtime Workflow Scheduler and Tool Gateway]
  Governance --> Runtime
  Intelligence --> Runtime
  Runtime --> Coordination[CATA Supervisor Managers and Executive Council]
  Runtime --> Departments[Certified Department Agents]
  Coordination --> Departments
  Departments --> Domains[Commerce Content Treasury Analytics Data Customer and Security Domains]
  Domains --> External[Approved Provider Adapters]
  External --> Reconcile[Effect Verification and Reconciliation]
  Domains --> Reconcile
  Reconcile --> Evidence[Outcome Audit and Learning Events]
  Evidence --> Intelligence
  Evidence --> Governance
  Evidence --> Coordination
```

Hard startup dependencies must be acyclic. Learning, metrics and event feedback are asynchronous loops with versioned facts, not startup or authority cycles. A dependency cannot call upward to acquire permission, and an optional provider cannot become a hidden global single point of failure.

| Specialists and workers | execute typed capabilities | mission expansion and self-approval | human agent and task owner | run and effect receipts |

| Control services | enforce policy identity approval audit and isolation | business strategy | human control owner | deterministic decision receipt |

#### Department Operating Cadence

1. **Accept human-chartered outcomes and explicit non-goals.** The department records owner, state, versions, budget and evidence before progressing.
2. **Verify manager and member certifications.** The department records owner, state, versions, budget and evidence before progressing.
3. **Resolve demand, priority and capacity.** The department records owner, state, versions, budget and evidence before progressing.
4. **Issue typed tasks with narrowed authority.** The department records owner, state, versions, budget and evidence before progressing.
5. **Exchange bounded context through owned contracts.** The department records owner, state, versions, budget and evidence before progressing.
6. **Review evidence, dissent, risk and resource use.** The department records owner, state, versions, budget and evidence before progressing.
7. **Obtain independent decisions and approvals.** The department records owner, state, versions, budget and evidence before progressing.
8. **Verify effects, business outcomes and human impact.** The department records owner, state, versions, budget and evidence before progressing.
9. **Handle failures through owned reconciliation.** The department records owner, state, versions, budget and evidence before progressing.
10. **Review metrics, learning proposals and department charter.** The department records owner, state, versions, budget and evidence before progressing.

| Context | Purpose-bound package assembled from signed human strategy; executive domain briefs; policy; stakeholder commitments; portfolio state; risk and budget envelopes. |
| Knowledge | company mission; accepted strategy; policy; executive domain records; portfolio evidence; stakeholder and customer commitments |

#### CAT-AG-P4-DEPT-01-MEM — Executive Coordination Office — Memory Flow

**Diagram ID:** `CAT-AG-P4-DEPT-01-MEM`
**Title:** Executive Coordination Office — Memory Flow
**Purpose:** Show run state, episodic proposals, consent, retention, synchronization and deletion for the department.
**Audience:** Department owners, executive advisors, agent managers, architects, implementers, operators, security reviewers and auditors.
**Reading Order:** Start with ephemeral working state; only verified purpose-bound outcomes cross into durable Memory.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  Run[Department collaboration run] --> Working[Ephemeral working state]
  Working --> Checkpoint[Encrypted workflow checkpoint]
  Checkpoint --> Verified{{Outcome verified}}
  Verified -->|No| Quarantine[Expire or quarantine state]
  Verified -->|Yes| Proposal[Memory proposal]
  Proposal --> Classify[Class purpose subject and tenant]
  Classify --> Consent[Consent retention and provenance]
  Consent --> Memory[Memory authority commits]
  Memory --> Sync[Replica and cache synchronization]
  Sync --> Receipt[Memory receipt]
  Receipt --> Expire[Retention tombstone and deletion proof]
```

#### CAT-AG-P4-DEPT-01-DEC — Executive Coordination Office — Decision Flow

**Diagram ID:** `CAT-AG-P4-DEPT-01-DEC`
**Title:** Executive Coordination Office — Decision Flow
**Purpose:** Show facts, options, constraints, human judgment and exact execution decision for `CAT-DEPT-EXEC`.
**Audience:** Department owners, executive advisors, agent managers, architects, implementers, operators, security reviewers and auditors.
**Reading Order:** Read top to bottom; agent recommendation stops before accountable human choice and effect authorization.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  Question[Decision question and owner] --> Facts[Verified facts and source revisions]
  Facts --> Options[Feasible options and counterfactual]
  Options --> Constraints[Policy rights Security Finance Data and resources]
  Constraints --> Uncertainty[Assumptions dissent and uncertainty]
  Uncertainty --> Recommend[Bounded agent recommendation]
  Recommend --> Human[Authenticated human judgment]
  Human --> Result{{Approve deny revise defer or escalate}}
  Result -->|Approve| Bind[Bind exact scope digest and expiry]
  Result -->|Revise| Options
  Result -->|Deny| Close[Record denial]
  Result -->|Defer| Wait[Safe waiting state]
  Result -->|Escalate| Authority[Higher named human authority]
  Bind --> Execute[Governed domain effect]
  Execute --> Verify[Verify authoritative outcome]
```

#### CAT-AG-P4-DEPT-01-FAIL — Executive Coordination Office — Failure Flow

**Diagram ID:** `CAT-AG-P4-DEPT-01-FAIL`
**Title:** Executive Coordination Office — Failure Flow
**Purpose:** Show detection, containment, effect classification, evidence and escalation for department failure.
**Audience:** Department owners, executive advisors, agent managers, architects, implementers, operators, security reviewers and auditors.
**Reading Order:** Read top to bottom and never follow a retry path before authoritative effect state is known.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  Signal[Failure uncertainty or policy violation] --> Stop[Stop dependent effects]
  Stop --> Own[Open owned failure or incident case]
  Own --> Preserve[Preserve state versions and evidence]
  Preserve --> Attempt{{Material effect attempted}}
  Attempt -->|Yes| Truth[Query domain source of truth]
  Attempt -->|No| Class[Classify failure and retryability]
  Truth --> Known{{Effect state known}}
  Known -->|No| Quarantine[Quarantine and human escalation]
  Known -->|Yes| Class
  Class --> Safe{{Retry safe budgeted and useful}}
  Safe -->|Yes| Recovery[Enter recovery flow]
  Safe -->|No| Escalate[Named owner decision]
  Quarantine --> Escalate
```

#### CAT-AG-P4-DEPT-01-REC — Executive Coordination Office — Recovery Flow

**Diagram ID:** `CAT-AG-P4-DEPT-01-REC`
**Title:** Executive Coordination Office — Recovery Flow
**Purpose:** Show source-of-truth reconciliation, approved remediation, invariant verification and closure.
**Audience:** Department owners, executive advisors, agent managers, architects, implementers, operators, security reviewers and auditors.
**Reading Order:** Read left to right; closure requires linked evidence that the original and recovery effects reconcile.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  Case[Owned recovery case] --> Scope[Affected tenants tasks data and effects]
  Scope --> Reconcile[Authoritative state reconciliation]
  Reconcile --> Plan[Resume compensate rollback abandon or migrate]
  Plan --> Decision{{Human approval required}}
  Decision -->|Yes| Human[Authorized human decision]
  Decision -->|No| Execute[Bounded remediation]
  Human --> Execute
  Execute --> Verify[Verify business Security Data and domain invariants]
  Verify --> Evidence[Link original and recovery receipts]
  Evidence --> Restore[Restore narrow service or close]
  Restore --> Review[Incident performance and learning review]
```

#### Department Card Acceptance Checklist

- [ ] Human accountability and manager boundaries resolve.
- [ ] Agents and versions are certified for exact roles.
- [ ] Responsibilities have no overlap without a named decider.
- [ ] Inputs and outputs have owned schemas.
- [ ] Every event has producer, consumer, replay and retention rules.
- [ ] APIs enforce identity, deadline, cancellation and trace.
- [ ] Knowledge and Memory remain separate governed authorities.
- [ ] Security model includes isolation, permissions and incident route.
- [ ] Metrics cannot reward unsafe speed or hidden failures.
- [ ] KPIs include evidence and human impact.
- [ ] Failure recovery reconciles effects.
- [ ] Future expansion has migration, recertification and dissolution.
- [ ] All eight collaboration flows match contracts.

#### CAT-AG-P4-DEPT-02-FAIL — Technology and Architecture — Failure Flow

**Diagram ID:** `CAT-AG-P4-DEPT-02-FAIL`
**Title:** Technology and Architecture — Failure Flow
**Purpose:** Show detection, containment, effect classification, evidence and escalation for department failure.
**Audience:** Department owners, executive advisors, agent managers, architects, implementers, operators, security reviewers and auditors.
**Reading Order:** Read top to bottom and never follow a retry path before authoritative effect state is known.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  Signal[Failure uncertainty or policy violation] --> Stop[Stop dependent effects]
  Stop --> Own[Open owned failure or incident case]
  Own --> Preserve[Preserve state versions and evidence]
  Preserve --> Attempt{{Material effect attempted}}
  Attempt -->|Yes| Truth[Query domain source of truth]
  Attempt -->|No| Class[Classify failure and retryability]
  Truth --> Known{{Effect state known}}
  Known -->|No| Quarantine[Quarantine and human escalation]
  Known -->|Yes| Class
  Class --> Safe{{Retry safe budgeted and useful}}
  Safe -->|Yes| Recovery[Enter recovery flow]
  Safe -->|No| Escalate[Named owner decision]
  Quarantine --> Escalate
```

#### CAT-AG-P4-DEPT-02-REC — Technology and Architecture — Recovery Flow

**Diagram ID:** `CAT-AG-P4-DEPT-02-REC`
**Title:** Technology and Architecture — Recovery Flow
**Purpose:** Show source-of-truth reconciliation, approved remediation, invariant verification and closure.
**Audience:** Department owners, executive advisors, agent managers, architects, implementers, operators, security reviewers and auditors.
**Reading Order:** Read left to right; closure requires linked evidence that the original and recovery effects reconcile.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  Case[Owned recovery case] --> Scope[Affected tenants tasks data and effects]
  Scope --> Reconcile[Authoritative state reconciliation]
  Reconcile --> Plan[Resume compensate rollback abandon or migrate]
  Plan --> Decision{{Human approval required}}
  Decision -->|Yes| Human[Authorized human decision]
  Decision -->|No| Execute[Bounded remediation]
  Human --> Execute
  Execute --> Verify[Verify business Security Data and domain invariants]
  Verify --> Evidence[Link original and recovery receipts]
  Evidence --> Restore[Restore narrow service or close]
  Restore --> Review[Incident performance and learning review]
```

#### Department Card Acceptance Checklist

- [ ] Human accountability and manager boundaries resolve.
- [ ] Agents and versions are certified for exact roles.
- [ ] Responsibilities have no overlap without a named decider.
- [ ] Inputs and outputs have owned schemas.
- [ ] Every event has producer, consumer, replay and retention rules.
- [ ] APIs enforce identity, deadline, cancellation and trace.
- [ ] Knowledge and Memory remain separate governed authorities.
- [ ] Security model includes isolation, permissions and incident route.
- [ ] Metrics cannot reward unsafe speed or hidden failures.
- [ ] KPIs include evidence and human impact.
- [ ] Failure recovery reconciles effects.
- [ ] Future expansion has migration, recertification and dissolution.
- [ ] All eight collaboration flows match contracts.

#### Department Operating Cadence

2. **Verify manager and member certifications.** The department records owner, state, versions, budget and evidence before progressing.
3. **Resolve demand, priority and capacity.** The department records owner, state, versions, budget and evidence before progressing.
4. **Issue typed tasks with narrowed authority.** The department records owner, state, versions, budget and evidence before progressing.
5. **Exchange bounded context through owned contracts.** The department records owner, state, versions, budget and evidence before progressing.
6. **Review evidence, dissent, risk and resource use.** The department records owner, state, versions, budget and evidence before progressing.
7. **Obtain independent decisions and approvals.** The department records owner, state, versions, budget and evidence before progressing.
8. **Verify effects, business outcomes and human impact.** The department records owner, state, versions, budget and evidence before progressing.
9. **Handle failures through owned reconciliation.** The department records owner, state, versions, budget and evidence before progressing.
10. **Review metrics, learning proposals and department charter.** The department records owner, state, versions, budget and evidence before progressing.

#### CAT-AG-P4-DEPT-03-SEQ — Finance and Treasury — Sequence Diagram

**Diagram ID:** `CAT-AG-P4-DEPT-03-SEQ`
**Title:** Finance and Treasury — Sequence Diagram
**Purpose:** Show the governed end-to-end collaboration sequence for `CAT-DEPT-FIN`.
**Audience:** Department owners, executive advisors, agent managers, architects, implementers, operators, security reviewers and auditors.
**Reading Order:** Read top to bottom from human charter through manager, specialists, independent gates and verified closure.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  participant H as Human accountable owner
  participant M as Department manager and executive advisor
  participant A as Certified department agents

  M-->>H: Outcome resource and risk review
```

```mermaid
  Result -->|Defer| Wait[Safe waiting state]

  Bind --> Execute[Governed domain effect]
  Execute --> Verify[Verify authoritative outcome]
```

#### CAT-AG-P4-DEPT-04-SEQ — Operations and Orchestration — Sequence Diagram

**Diagram ID:** `CAT-AG-P4-DEPT-04-SEQ`
**Title:** Operations and Orchestration — Sequence Diagram
**Purpose:** Show the governed end-to-end collaboration sequence for `CAT-DEPT-OPS`.
**Audience:** Department owners, executive advisors, agent managers, architects, implementers, operators, security reviewers and auditors.
**Reading Order:** Read top to bottom from human charter through manager, specialists, independent gates and verified closure.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  participant H as Human accountable owner
  participant M as Department manager and executive advisor
  participant A as Certified department agents
  participant G as Independent policy approval and audit gates
  participant D as Owned domain services
  H->>M: Signed Operations and Orchestration charter
  M->>A: Typed tasks context budget and acceptance
  A-->>M: Evidence options dissent and uncertainty
  M->>G: Request exact decision or effect validation
  G-->>H: Human decision packet when required
  H-->>G: Approve deny revise or escalate
  G->>D: Permit exact unchanged operation
  D-->>A: Authoritative result and receipt
  A-->>M: Verified output or explicit failure
  M-->>H: Outcome resource and risk review
```

#### CAT-AG-P4-DEPT-04-EVT — Operations and Orchestration — Event Flow

**Diagram ID:** `CAT-AG-P4-DEPT-04-EVT`
**Title:** Operations and Orchestration — Event Flow
**Purpose:** Show committed facts, ownership and replay-safe event movement for `CAT-DEPT-OPS`.
**Audience:** Department owners, executive advisors, agent managers, architects, implementers, operators, security reviewers and auditors.
**Reading Order:** Read left to right; each event follows an authoritative commit and cannot be interpreted as an approval.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  Charter[Department charter accepted event] --> Workflow[Owned department workflow]
  Workflow --> Accepted[Task accepted event]
  Accepted --> Evidence[Evidence ready event]
  Evidence --> Decision[Decision requested event]
  Decision --> Human[Human decision recorded event]
  Human --> Effect[Effect attempted event]
  Effect --> Verified[Effect verified event]
  Verified --> Outcome[Department outcome recorded event]
  Outcome --> Audit[Audit and learning consumers]
  Workflow --> Failure[Failure or escalation event]
  Failure --> Audit
```

#### CAT-AG-P4-DEPT-04-CTX — Operations and Orchestration — Context Flow

**Diagram ID:** `CAT-AG-P4-DEPT-04-CTX`
**Title:** Operations and Orchestration — Context Flow
**Purpose:** Show purpose, source, authorization, redaction, budgeting, handoff and expiry of department context.
**Audience:** Department owners, executive advisors, agent managers, architects, implementers, operators, security reviewers and auditors.
**Reading Order:** Read from declared purpose to expiring package; every transformation preserves source and digest.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  Purpose[Declared department purpose] --> Sources[Owned canonical and task sources]
  Sources --> Authorize[Identity purpose and classification authorization]
  Authorize --> Retrieve[Bounded retrieval]
  Retrieve --> Provenance[Revision freshness rights and provenance]
  Provenance --> Redact[Redaction and minimization]
  Redact --> Budget[Context and token budget]
  Budget --> Digest[Signed package and exclusions]
  Digest --> Agents[Authorized department agents]
  Agents --> Handoff[Attributed handoff summary]
  Handoff --> Expire[Expiry invalidation and deletion policy]
```

#### CAT-AG-P4-DEPT-04-KNW — Operations and Orchestration — Knowledge Flow

**Diagram ID:** `CAT-AG-P4-DEPT-04-KNW`
**Title:** Operations and Orchestration — Knowledge Flow
**Purpose:** Show evidence and claims moving through provenance, contradiction and domain review before canonical use.
**Audience:** Department owners, executive advisors, agent managers, architects, implementers, operators, security reviewers and auditors.
**Reading Order:** Read left to right from observations to canonical commit and rebuildable projections.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  Evidence[Department evidence] --> Claim[Proposed claim]
  Claim --> Rights[Source rights and provenance]
  Rights --> Time[Temporal validity and freshness]
  Time --> Conflict[Duplicate and contradiction detection]
  Conflict --> Owner[Human domain owner review]
  Owner --> Decision{{Accept dispute reject or expire}}
  Decision --> Canon[Canonical knowledge revision]
  Canon --> Graph[Knowledge graph]
  Canon --> Index[Retrieval projection]
  Canon --> Notify[Knowledge changed event]
  Notify --> Future[Future bounded context]
```

#### CAT-AG-P4-DEPT-04-MEM — Operations and Orchestration — Memory Flow

**Diagram ID:** `CAT-AG-P4-DEPT-04-MEM`
**Title:** Operations and Orchestration — Memory Flow
**Purpose:** Show run state, episodic proposals, consent, retention, synchronization and deletion for the department.
**Audience:** Department owners, executive advisors, agent managers, architects, implementers, operators, security reviewers and auditors.
**Reading Order:** Start with ephemeral working state; only verified purpose-bound outcomes cross into durable Memory.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  Run[Department collaboration run] --> Working[Ephemeral working state]
  Working --> Checkpoint[Encrypted workflow checkpoint]
  Checkpoint --> Verified{{Outcome verified}}
  Verified -->|No| Quarantine[Expire or quarantine state]
  Verified -->|Yes| Proposal[Memory proposal]
  Proposal --> Classify[Class purpose subject and tenant]
  Classify --> Consent[Consent retention and provenance]
  Consent --> Memory[Memory authority commits]
  Memory --> Sync[Replica and cache synchronization]
  Sync --> Receipt[Memory receipt]
  Receipt --> Expire[Retention tombstone and deletion proof]
```

#### CAT-AG-P4-DEPT-04-DEC — Operations and Orchestration — Decision Flow

**Diagram ID:** `CAT-AG-P4-DEPT-04-DEC`
**Title:** Operations and Orchestration — Decision Flow
**Purpose:** Show facts, options, constraints, human judgment and exact execution decision for `CAT-DEPT-OPS`.
**Audience:** Department owners, executive advisors, agent managers, architects, implementers, operators, security reviewers and auditors.
**Reading Order:** Read top to bottom; agent recommendation stops before accountable human choice and effect authorization.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  Question[Decision question and owner] --> Facts[Verified facts and source revisions]
  Facts --> Options[Feasible options and counterfactual]
  Options --> Constraints[Policy rights Security Finance Data and resources]
  Constraints --> Uncertainty[Assumptions dissent and uncertainty]
  Uncertainty --> Recommend[Bounded agent recommendation]
  Recommend --> Human[Authenticated human judgment]
  Human --> Result{{Approve deny revise defer or escalate}}
  Result -->|Approve| Bind[Bind exact scope digest and expiry]
  Result -->|Revise| Options
  Result -->|Deny| Close[Record denial]
  Result -->|Defer| Wait[Safe waiting state]
  Result -->|Escalate| Authority[Higher named human authority]
  Bind --> Execute[Governed domain effect]
  Execute --> Verify[Verify authoritative outcome]
```

#### CAT-AG-P4-DEPT-04-FAIL — Operations and Orchestration — Failure Flow

**Diagram ID:** `CAT-AG-P4-DEPT-04-FAIL`
**Title:** Operations and Orchestration — Failure Flow
**Purpose:** Show detection, containment, effect classification, evidence and escalation for department failure.
**Audience:** Department owners, executive advisors, agent managers, architects, implementers, operators, security reviewers and auditors.
**Reading Order:** Read top to bottom and never follow a retry path before authoritative effect state is known.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  Signal[Failure uncertainty or policy violation] --> Stop[Stop dependent effects]
  Stop --> Own[Open owned failure or incident case]
  Own --> Preserve[Preserve state versions and evidence]
  Preserve --> Attempt{{Material effect attempted}}
  Attempt -->|Yes| Truth[Query domain source of truth]
  Attempt -->|No| Class[Classify failure and retryability]
  Truth --> Known{{Effect state known}}
  Known -->|No| Quarantine[Quarantine and human escalation]
  Known -->|Yes| Class
  Class --> Safe{{Retry safe budgeted and useful}}
  Safe -->|Yes| Recovery[Enter recovery flow]
  Safe -->|No| Escalate[Named owner decision]
  Quarantine --> Escalate
```

#### CAT-AG-P4-DEPT-04-REC — Operations and Orchestration — Recovery Flow

**Diagram ID:** `CAT-AG-P4-DEPT-04-REC`
**Title:** Operations and Orchestration — Recovery Flow
**Purpose:** Show source-of-truth reconciliation, approved remediation, invariant verification and closure.
**Audience:** Department owners, executive advisors, agent managers, architects, implementers, operators, security reviewers and auditors.
**Reading Order:** Read left to right; closure requires linked evidence that the original and recovery effects reconcile.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  Case[Owned recovery case] --> Scope[Affected tenants tasks data and effects]
  Scope --> Reconcile[Authoritative state reconciliation]
  Reconcile --> Plan[Resume compensate rollback abandon or migrate]
  Plan --> Decision{{Human approval required}}
  Decision -->|Yes| Human[Authorized human decision]
  Decision -->|No| Execute[Bounded remediation]
  Human --> Execute
  Execute --> Verify[Verify business Security Data and domain invariants]
  Verify --> Evidence[Link original and recovery receipts]
  Evidence --> Restore[Restore narrow service or close]
  Restore --> Review[Incident performance and learning review]
```

#### Department Card Acceptance Checklist

- [ ] Human accountability and manager boundaries resolve.
- [ ] Agents and versions are certified for exact roles.
- [ ] Responsibilities have no overlap without a named decider.
- [ ] Inputs and outputs have owned schemas.
- [ ] Every event has producer, consumer, replay and retention rules.
- [ ] APIs enforce identity, deadline, cancellation and trace.
- [ ] Knowledge and Memory remain separate governed authorities.
- [ ] Security model includes isolation, permissions and incident route.
- [ ] Metrics cannot reward unsafe speed or hidden failures.
- [ ] KPIs include evidence and human impact.
- [ ] Failure recovery reconciles effects.
- [ ] Future expansion has migration, recertification and dissolution.
- [ ] All eight collaboration flows match contracts.

**Purpose:** Show run state, episodic proposals, consent, retention, synchronization and deletion for the department.
**Audience:** Department owners, executive advisors, agent managers, architects, implementers, operators, security reviewers and auditors.
**Reading Order:** Start with ephemeral working state; only verified purpose-bound outcomes cross into durable Memory.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  Run[Department collaboration run] --> Working[Ephemeral working state]
  Working --> Checkpoint[Encrypted workflow checkpoint]
  Checkpoint --> Verified{{Outcome verified}}
  Verified -->|No| Quarantine[Expire or quarantine state]
  Verified -->|Yes| Proposal[Memory proposal]
  Proposal --> Classify[Class purpose subject and tenant]
  Classify --> Consent[Consent retention and provenance]
  Consent --> Memory[Memory authority commits]
  Memory --> Sync[Replica and cache synchronization]
  Sync --> Receipt[Memory receipt]
  Receipt --> Expire[Retention tombstone and deletion proof]
```

#### CAT-AG-P4-DEPT-05-DEC — Marketing and Growth — Decision Flow

**Diagram ID:** `CAT-AG-P4-DEPT-05-DEC`
**Title:** Marketing and Growth — Decision Flow
**Purpose:** Show facts, options, constraints, human judgment and exact execution decision for `CAT-DEPT-MKT`.
**Audience:** Department owners, executive advisors, agent managers, architects, implementers, operators, security reviewers and auditors.
**Reading Order:** Read top to bottom; agent recommendation stops before accountable human choice and effect authorization.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  Question[Decision question and owner] --> Facts[Verified facts and source revisions]
  Facts --> Options[Feasible options and counterfactual]
  Options --> Constraints[Policy rights Security Finance Data and resources]
  Constraints --> Uncertainty[Assumptions dissent and uncertainty]
  Uncertainty --> Recommend[Bounded agent recommendation]
  Recommend --> Human[Authenticated human judgment]
  Human --> Result{{Approve deny revise defer or escalate}}
  Result -->|Approve| Bind[Bind exact scope digest and expiry]
  Result -->|Revise| Options
  Result -->|Deny| Close[Record denial]
  Result -->|Defer| Wait[Safe waiting state]
  Result -->|Escalate| Authority[Higher named human authority]
  Bind --> Execute[Governed domain effect]
  Execute --> Verify[Verify authoritative outcome]
```

#### CAT-AG-P4-DEPT-05-FAIL — Marketing and Growth — Failure Flow

**Diagram ID:** `CAT-AG-P4-DEPT-05-FAIL`
**Title:** Marketing and Growth — Failure Flow
**Purpose:** Show detection, containment, effect classification, evidence and escalation for department failure.
**Audience:** Department owners, executive advisors, agent managers, architects, implementers, operators, security reviewers and auditors.
**Reading Order:** Read top to bottom and never follow a retry path before authoritative effect state is known.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  Signal[Failure uncertainty or policy violation] --> Stop[Stop dependent effects]
  Stop --> Own[Open owned failure or incident case]
  Own --> Preserve[Preserve state versions and evidence]
  Preserve --> Attempt{{Material effect attempted}}
  Attempt -->|Yes| Truth[Query domain source of truth]
  Attempt -->|No| Class[Classify failure and retryability]
  Truth --> Known{{Effect state known}}
  Known -->|No| Quarantine[Quarantine and human escalation]
  Known -->|Yes| Class
  Class --> Safe{{Retry safe budgeted and useful}}
  Safe -->|Yes| Recovery[Enter recovery flow]
  Safe -->|No| Escalate[Named owner decision]
  Quarantine --> Escalate
```

#### CAT-AG-P4-DEPT-05-REC — Marketing and Growth — Recovery Flow

**Diagram ID:** `CAT-AG-P4-DEPT-05-REC`
**Title:** Marketing and Growth — Recovery Flow
**Purpose:** Show source-of-truth reconciliation, approved remediation, invariant verification and closure.
**Audience:** Department owners, executive advisors, agent managers, architects, implementers, operators, security reviewers and auditors.
**Reading Order:** Read left to right; closure requires linked evidence that the original and recovery effects reconcile.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  Case[Owned recovery case] --> Scope[Affected tenants tasks data and effects]
  Scope --> Reconcile[Authoritative state reconciliation]
  Reconcile --> Plan[Resume compensate rollback abandon or migrate]
  Plan --> Decision{{Human approval required}}
  Decision -->|Yes| Human[Authorized human decision]
  Decision -->|No| Execute[Bounded remediation]
  Human --> Execute
  Execute --> Verify[Verify business Security Data and domain invariants]
  Verify --> Evidence[Link original and recovery receipts]
  Evidence --> Restore[Restore narrow service or close]
  Restore --> Review[Incident performance and learning review]
```

#### Department Card Acceptance Checklist

- [ ] Human accountability and manager boundaries resolve.
- [ ] Agents and versions are certified for exact roles.
- [ ] Responsibilities have no overlap without a named decider.
- [ ] Inputs and outputs have owned schemas.
- [ ] Every event has producer, consumer, replay and retention rules.
- [ ] APIs enforce identity, deadline, cancellation and trace.
- [ ] Knowledge and Memory remain separate governed authorities.
- [ ] Security model includes isolation, permissions and incident route.
- [ ] Metrics cannot reward unsafe speed or hidden failures.
- [ ] KPIs include evidence and human impact.
- [ ] Failure recovery reconciles effects.
- [ ] Future expansion has migration, recertification and dissolution.
- [ ] All eight collaboration flows match contracts.

#### Department Operating Cadence

1. **Accept human-chartered outcomes and explicit non-goals.** The department records owner, state, versions, budget and evidence before progressing.
2. **Verify manager and member certifications.** The department records owner, state, versions, budget and evidence before progressing.
3. **Resolve demand, priority and capacity.** The department records owner, state, versions, budget and evidence before progressing.
4. **Issue typed tasks with narrowed authority.** The department records owner, state, versions, budget and evidence before progressing.
5. **Exchange bounded context through owned contracts.** The department records owner, state, versions, budget and evidence before progressing.
6. **Review evidence, dissent, risk and resource use.** The department records owner, state, versions, budget and evidence before progressing.
7. **Obtain independent decisions and approvals.** The department records owner, state, versions, budget and evidence before progressing.
8. **Verify effects, business outcomes and human impact.** The department records owner, state, versions, budget and evidence before progressing.
9. **Handle failures through owned reconciliation.** The department records owner, state, versions, budget and evidence before progressing.
10. **Review metrics, learning proposals and department charter.** The department records owner, state, versions, budget and evidence before progressing.

| Knowledge | canonical project and domain sources; claim graph; ontology; source rights; temporal validity; contradictions; documentation status |
| Memory | owns governed memory service records by class and namespace; its agents hold no ungoverned self-memory |
| Decision | Options and evidence are routed to the accountable human named in `CKO Agent advises; Human Knowledge and Documentation Owner is accountable; Supervisor coordinates curation tasks`. |
| Security | source authorization, poisoning defense, tenant isolation, consent, retention, legal hold, tombstone convergence and protected forensic evidence |
| Completion | Outputs `knowledge portfolio; accepted claim change; synchronized memory; deletion proof; retrieval index update; learning proposal; curation report` meet schema, approval, verification and evidence requirements. |

#### CAT-AG-P4-DEPT-07-SEQ — Trust Security and Compliance — Sequence Diagram

**Diagram ID:** `CAT-AG-P4-DEPT-07-SEQ`
**Title:** Trust Security and Compliance — Sequence Diagram
**Purpose:** Show the governed end-to-end collaboration sequence for `CAT-DEPT-SEC`.
**Audience:** Department owners, executive advisors, agent managers, architects, implementers, operators, security reviewers and auditors.
**Reading Order:** Read top to bottom from human charter through manager, specialists, independent gates and verified closure.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  participant H as Human accountable owner
  participant M as Department manager and executive advisor
  participant A as Certified department agents
  participant G as Independent policy approval and audit gates
  participant D as Owned domain services
  H->>M: Signed Trust Security and Compliance charter
  M->>A: Typed tasks context budget and acceptance
  A-->>M: Evidence options dissent and uncertainty
  M->>G: Request exact decision or effect validation
  G-->>H: Human decision packet when required
  H-->>G: Approve deny revise or escalate
  G->>D: Permit exact unchanged operation
  D-->>A: Authoritative result and receipt
  A-->>M: Verified output or explicit failure
  M-->>H: Outcome resource and risk review
```

#### CAT-AG-P4-DEPT-07-EVT — Trust Security and Compliance — Event Flow

**Diagram ID:** `CAT-AG-P4-DEPT-07-EVT`
**Title:** Trust Security and Compliance — Event Flow
**Purpose:** Show committed facts, ownership and replay-safe event movement for `CAT-DEPT-SEC`.
**Audience:** Department owners, executive advisors, agent managers, architects, implementers, operators, security reviewers and auditors.
**Reading Order:** Read left to right; each event follows an authoritative commit and cannot be interpreted as an approval.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  Charter[Department charter accepted event] --> Workflow[Owned department workflow]
  Workflow --> Accepted[Task accepted event]
  Accepted --> Evidence[Evidence ready event]
  Evidence --> Decision[Decision requested event]
  Decision --> Human[Human decision recorded event]
  Human --> Effect[Effect attempted event]
  Effect --> Verified[Effect verified event]
  Verified --> Outcome[Department outcome recorded event]
  Outcome --> Audit[Audit and learning consumers]
  Workflow --> Failure[Failure or escalation event]
  Failure --> Audit
```

#### CAT-AG-P4-DEPT-07-CTX — Trust Security and Compliance — Context Flow

**Diagram ID:** `CAT-AG-P4-DEPT-07-CTX`
**Title:** Trust Security and Compliance — Context Flow
**Purpose:** Show purpose, source, authorization, redaction, budgeting, handoff and expiry of department context.
**Audience:** Department owners, executive advisors, agent managers, architects, implementers, operators, security reviewers and auditors.
**Reading Order:** Read from declared purpose to expiring package; every transformation preserves source and digest.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  Purpose[Declared department purpose] --> Sources[Owned canonical and task sources]
  Sources --> Authorize[Identity purpose and classification authorization]
  Authorize --> Retrieve[Bounded retrieval]
  Retrieve --> Provenance[Revision freshness rights and provenance]
  Provenance --> Redact[Redaction and minimization]
  Redact --> Budget[Context and token budget]
  Budget --> Digest[Signed package and exclusions]
  Digest --> Agents[Authorized department agents]
  Agents --> Handoff[Attributed handoff summary]
  Handoff --> Expire[Expiry invalidation and deletion policy]
```

#### CAT-AG-P4-DEPT-07-KNW — Trust Security and Compliance — Knowledge Flow

**Diagram ID:** `CAT-AG-P4-DEPT-07-KNW`
**Title:** Trust Security and Compliance — Knowledge Flow
**Purpose:** Show evidence and claims moving through provenance, contradiction and domain review before canonical use.
**Audience:** Department owners, executive advisors, agent managers, architects, implementers, operators, security reviewers and auditors.
**Reading Order:** Read left to right from observations to canonical commit and rebuildable projections.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  Evidence[Department evidence] --> Claim[Proposed claim]
  Claim --> Rights[Source rights and provenance]
  Rights --> Time[Temporal validity and freshness]
  Time --> Conflict[Duplicate and contradiction detection]
  Conflict --> Owner[Human domain owner review]
  Owner --> Decision{{Accept dispute reject or expire}}
  Decision --> Canon[Canonical knowledge revision]
  Canon --> Graph[Knowledge graph]
  Canon --> Index[Retrieval projection]
  Canon --> Notify[Knowledge changed event]
  Notify --> Future[Future bounded context]
```

#### CAT-AG-P4-DEPT-07-MEM — Trust Security and Compliance — Memory Flow

**Diagram ID:** `CAT-AG-P4-DEPT-07-MEM`
**Title:** Trust Security and Compliance — Memory Flow
**Purpose:** Show run state, episodic proposals, consent, retention, synchronization and deletion for the department.
**Audience:** Department owners, executive advisors, agent managers, architects, implementers, operators, security reviewers and auditors.
**Reading Order:** Start with ephemeral working state; only verified purpose-bound outcomes cross into durable Memory.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  Run[Department collaboration run] --> Working[Ephemeral working state]
  Working --> Checkpoint[Encrypted workflow checkpoint]
  Checkpoint --> Verified{{Outcome verified}}
  Verified -->|No| Quarantine[Expire or quarantine state]
  Verified -->|Yes| Proposal[Memory proposal]
  Proposal --> Classify[Class purpose subject and tenant]
  Classify --> Consent[Consent retention and provenance]
  Consent --> Memory[Memory authority commits]
  Memory --> Sync[Replica and cache synchronization]
  Sync --> Receipt[Memory receipt]
  Receipt --> Expire[Retention tombstone and deletion proof]
```

#### CAT-AG-P4-DEPT-07-DEC — Trust Security and Compliance — Decision Flow

**Diagram ID:** `CAT-AG-P4-DEPT-07-DEC`
**Title:** Trust Security and Compliance — Decision Flow
**Purpose:** Show facts, options, constraints, human judgment and exact execution decision for `CAT-DEPT-SEC`.
**Audience:** Department owners, executive advisors, agent managers, architects, implementers, operators, security reviewers and auditors.
**Reading Order:** Read top to bottom; agent recommendation stops before accountable human choice and effect authorization.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  Question[Decision question and owner] --> Facts[Verified facts and source revisions]
  Facts --> Options[Feasible options and counterfactual]
  Options --> Constraints[Policy rights Security Finance Data and resources]
  Constraints --> Uncertainty[Assumptions dissent and uncertainty]
  Uncertainty --> Recommend[Bounded agent recommendation]
  Recommend --> Human[Authenticated human judgment]
  Human --> Result{{Approve deny revise defer or escalate}}
  Result -->|Approve| Bind[Bind exact scope digest and expiry]
  Result -->|Revise| Options
  Result -->|Deny| Close[Record denial]
  Result -->|Defer| Wait[Safe waiting state]
  Result -->|Escalate| Authority[Higher named human authority]
  Bind --> Execute[Governed domain effect]
  Execute --> Verify[Verify authoritative outcome]
```

#### CAT-AG-P4-DEPT-07-FAIL — Trust Security and Compliance — Failure Flow

**Diagram ID:** `CAT-AG-P4-DEPT-07-FAIL`
**Title:** Trust Security and Compliance — Failure Flow
**Purpose:** Show detection, containment, effect classification, evidence and escalation for department failure.
**Audience:** Department owners, executive advisors, agent managers, architects, implementers, operators, security reviewers and auditors.
**Reading Order:** Read top to bottom and never follow a retry path before authoritative effect state is known.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  Signal[Failure uncertainty or policy violation] --> Stop[Stop dependent effects]
  Stop --> Own[Open owned failure or incident case]
  Own --> Preserve[Preserve state versions and evidence]
  Preserve --> Attempt{{Material effect attempted}}
  Attempt -->|Yes| Truth[Query domain source of truth]
  Attempt -->|No| Class[Classify failure and retryability]
  Truth --> Known{{Effect state known}}
  Known -->|No| Quarantine[Quarantine and human escalation]
  Known -->|Yes| Class
  Class --> Safe{{Retry safe budgeted and useful}}
  Safe -->|Yes| Recovery[Enter recovery flow]
  Safe -->|No| Escalate[Named owner decision]
  Quarantine --> Escalate
```

#### CAT-AG-P4-DEPT-07-REC — Trust Security and Compliance — Recovery Flow

**Diagram ID:** `CAT-AG-P4-DEPT-07-REC`
**Title:** Trust Security and Compliance — Recovery Flow
**Purpose:** Show source-of-truth reconciliation, approved remediation, invariant verification and closure.
**Audience:** Department owners, executive advisors, agent managers, architects, implementers, operators, security reviewers and auditors.
**Reading Order:** Read left to right; closure requires linked evidence that the original and recovery effects reconcile.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  Case[Owned recovery case] --> Scope[Affected tenants tasks data and effects]
  Scope --> Reconcile[Authoritative state reconciliation]
  Reconcile --> Plan[Resume compensate rollback abandon or migrate]
  Plan --> Decision{{Human approval required}}
  Decision -->|Yes| Human[Authorized human decision]
  Decision -->|No| Execute[Bounded remediation]
  Human --> Execute
  Execute --> Verify[Verify business Security Data and domain invariants]
  Verify --> Evidence[Link original and recovery receipts]
  Evidence --> Restore[Restore narrow service or close]
  Restore --> Review[Incident performance and learning review]
```

#### Department Card Acceptance Checklist

- [ ] Human accountability and manager boundaries resolve.
- [ ] Agents and versions are certified for exact roles.
- [ ] Responsibilities have no overlap without a named decider.
- [ ] Inputs and outputs have owned schemas.
- [ ] Every event has producer, consumer, replay and retention rules.
- [ ] APIs enforce identity, deadline, cancellation and trace.
- [ ] Knowledge and Memory remain separate governed authorities.
- [ ] Security model includes isolation, permissions and incident route.
- [ ] Metrics cannot reward unsafe speed or hidden failures.
- [ ] KPIs include evidence and human impact.
- [ ] Failure recovery reconciles effects.
- [ ] Future expansion has migration, recertification and dissolution.
- [ ] All eight collaboration flows match contracts.

**Title:** Data Governance and Platform — Context Flow

#### CAT-AG-P4-DEPT-08-KNW — Data Governance and Platform — Knowledge Flow

**Diagram ID:** `CAT-AG-P4-DEPT-08-KNW`
**Title:** Data Governance and Platform — Knowledge Flow

```mermaid
flowchart LR

  Rights --> Time[Temporal validity and freshness]
  Time --> Conflict[Duplicate and contradiction detection]
  Conflict --> Owner[Human domain owner review]
  Owner --> Decision{{Accept dispute reject or expire}}
  Decision --> Canon[Canonical knowledge revision]
  Canon --> Graph[Knowledge graph]
  Canon --> Index[Retrieval projection]
  Canon --> Notify[Knowledge changed event]
  Notify --> Future[Future bounded context]
```

#### CAT-AG-P4-DEPT-08-MEM — Data Governance and Platform — Memory Flow

**Diagram ID:** `CAT-AG-P4-DEPT-08-MEM`
**Title:** Data Governance and Platform — Memory Flow
**Purpose:** Show run state, episodic proposals, consent, retention, synchronization and deletion for the department.
**Audience:** Department owners, executive advisors, agent managers, architects, implementers, operators, security reviewers and auditors.
**Reading Order:** Start with ephemeral working state; only verified purpose-bound outcomes cross into durable Memory.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  Run[Department collaboration run] --> Working[Ephemeral working state]
  Working --> Checkpoint[Encrypted workflow checkpoint]
  Checkpoint --> Verified{{Outcome verified}}
  Verified -->|No| Quarantine[Expire or quarantine state]
  Verified -->|Yes| Proposal[Memory proposal]
  Proposal --> Classify[Class purpose subject and tenant]
  Classify --> Consent[Consent retention and provenance]
  Consent --> Memory[Memory authority commits]
  Memory --> Sync[Replica and cache synchronization]
  Sync --> Receipt[Memory receipt]
  Receipt --> Expire[Retention tombstone and deletion proof]
```

#### CAT-AG-P4-DEPT-08-DEC — Data Governance and Platform — Decision Flow

**Diagram ID:** `CAT-AG-P4-DEPT-08-DEC`
**Title:** Data Governance and Platform — Decision Flow
**Purpose:** Show facts, options, constraints, human judgment and exact execution decision for `CAT-DEPT-DATA`.
**Audience:** Department owners, executive advisors, agent managers, architects, implementers, operators, security reviewers and auditors.
**Reading Order:** Read top to bottom; agent recommendation stops before accountable human choice and effect authorization.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  Question[Decision question and owner] --> Facts[Verified facts and source revisions]
  Facts --> Options[Feasible options and counterfactual]
  Options --> Constraints[Policy rights Security Finance Data and resources]
  Constraints --> Uncertainty[Assumptions dissent and uncertainty]
  Uncertainty --> Recommend[Bounded agent recommendation]
  Recommend --> Human[Authenticated human judgment]
  Human --> Result{{Approve deny revise defer or escalate}}
  Result -->|Approve| Bind[Bind exact scope digest and expiry]
  Result -->|Revise| Options
  Result -->|Deny| Close[Record denial]
  Result -->|Defer| Wait[Safe waiting state]
  Result -->|Escalate| Authority[Higher named human authority]
  Bind --> Execute[Governed domain effect]
  Execute --> Verify[Verify authoritative outcome]
```

#### CAT-AG-P4-DEPT-08-FAIL — Data Governance and Platform — Failure Flow

**Diagram ID:** `CAT-AG-P4-DEPT-08-FAIL`
**Title:** Data Governance and Platform — Failure Flow
**Purpose:** Show detection, containment, effect classification, evidence and escalation for department failure.
**Audience:** Department owners, executive advisors, agent managers, architects, implementers, operators, security reviewers and auditors.
**Reading Order:** Read top to bottom and never follow a retry path before authoritative effect state is known.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  Signal[Failure uncertainty or policy violation] --> Stop[Stop dependent effects]
  Stop --> Own[Open owned failure or incident case]
  Own --> Preserve[Preserve state versions and evidence]
  Preserve --> Attempt{{Material effect attempted}}
  Attempt -->|Yes| Truth[Query domain source of truth]
  Attempt -->|No| Class[Classify failure and retryability]
  Truth --> Known{{Effect state known}}
  Known -->|No| Quarantine[Quarantine and human escalation]
  Known -->|Yes| Class
  Class --> Safe{{Retry safe budgeted and useful}}
  Safe -->|Yes| Recovery[Enter recovery flow]
  Safe -->|No| Escalate[Named owner decision]
  Quarantine --> Escalate
```

#### CAT-AG-P4-DEPT-08-REC — Data Governance and Platform — Recovery Flow

**Diagram ID:** `CAT-AG-P4-DEPT-08-REC`
**Title:** Data Governance and Platform — Recovery Flow
**Purpose:** Show source-of-truth reconciliation, approved remediation, invariant verification and closure.
**Audience:** Department owners, executive advisors, agent managers, architects, implementers, operators, security reviewers and auditors.
**Reading Order:** Read left to right; closure requires linked evidence that the original and recovery effects reconcile.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  Case[Owned recovery case] --> Scope[Affected tenants tasks data and effects]
  Scope --> Reconcile[Authoritative state reconciliation]
  Reconcile --> Plan[Resume compensate rollback abandon or migrate]
  Plan --> Decision{{Human approval required}}
  Decision -->|Yes| Human[Authorized human decision]
  Decision -->|No| Execute[Bounded remediation]
  Human --> Execute
  Execute --> Verify[Verify business Security Data and domain invariants]
  Verify --> Evidence[Link original and recovery receipts]
  Evidence --> Restore[Restore narrow service or close]
  Restore --> Review[Incident performance and learning review]
```

#### Department Card Acceptance Checklist

- [ ] Human accountability and manager boundaries resolve.
- [ ] Agents and versions are certified for exact roles.
- [ ] Responsibilities have no overlap without a named decider.
- [ ] Inputs and outputs have owned schemas.
- [ ] Every event has producer, consumer, replay and retention rules.
- [ ] APIs enforce identity, deadline, cancellation and trace.
- [ ] Knowledge and Memory remain separate governed authorities.
- [ ] Security model includes isolation, permissions and incident route.
- [ ] Metrics cannot reward unsafe speed or hidden failures.
- [ ] KPIs include evidence and human impact.
- [ ] Failure recovery reconciles effects.
- [ ] Future expansion has migration, recertification and dissolution.
- [ ] All eight collaboration flows match contracts.
