#### Department Operating Cadence

1. **Accept human-chartered outcomes and explicit non-goals.** The department records owner, state, versions, budget and evidence before progressing.
2. **Verify manager and member certifications.** The department records owner, state, versions, budget and evidence before progressing.
3. **Resolve demand, priority and capacity.** The department records owner, state, versions, budget and evidence before progressing.
4. **Issue typed tasks with narrowed authority.** The department records owner, state, versions, budget and evidence before progressing.
5. **Exchange bounded context through owned contracts.** The department records owner, state, versions, budget and evidence before progressing.
6. **Review evidence, dissent, risk and resource use.** The department records owner, state, versions, budget and evidence before progressing.
7. **Obtain independent decisions and approvals.** The department records owner, state, versions, budget and evidence before progressing.
8. **Verify effects, business outcomes and human impact.** The department records owner, state, versions, budget and evidence before progressing.
9. **Handle failures through owned reconciliation.** The department records owner, state, versions, budget and evidence before progressing.
10. **Review metrics, learning proposals and department charter.** The department records owner, state, versions, budget and evidence before progressing.

| Memory | approved briefs, forecast scores and source-quality lessons; no prohibited surveillance or raw personal dossiers |
| Decision | Options and evidence are routed to the accountable human named in `CIO Agent advises; Human Research and Analytics Owners are accountable; Supervisor coordinates analysis tasks`. |
| Security | source allowlist and rights, egress controls, privacy thresholds, anti-poisoning, reproducible queries and no hidden collection |
| Completion | Outputs `research brief; source ledger; metric report; forecast; experiment result; contradiction report; intelligence decision packet` meet schema, approval, verification and evidence requirements. |

#### CAT-AG-P4-DEPT-10-SEQ — Commerce and Affiliate — Sequence Diagram

**Diagram ID:** `CAT-AG-P4-DEPT-10-SEQ`
**Title:** Commerce and Affiliate — Sequence Diagram
**Purpose:** Show the governed end-to-end collaboration sequence for `CAT-DEPT-COM`.
**Audience:** Department owners, executive advisors, agent managers, architects, implementers, operators, security reviewers and auditors.
**Reading Order:** Read top to bottom from human charter through manager, specialists, independent gates and verified closure.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  participant H as Human accountable owner
  participant M as Department manager and executive advisor
  participant A as Certified department agents
  participant G as Independent policy approval and audit gates
  participant D as Owned domain services
  H->>M: Signed Commerce and Affiliate charter
  M->>A: Typed tasks context budget and acceptance
  A-->>M: Evidence options dissent and uncertainty
  M->>G: Request exact decision or effect validation
  G-->>H: Human decision packet when required
  H-->>G: Approve deny revise or escalate
  G->>D: Permit exact unchanged operation
  D-->>A: Authoritative result and receipt
  A-->>M: Verified output or explicit failure
  M-->>H: Outcome resource and risk review
```

**Diagram ID:** `CAT-AG-P4-DEPT-10-EVT`

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  Charter[Department charter accepted event] --> Workflow[Owned department workflow]

  Accepted --> Evidence[Evidence ready event]
  Evidence --> Decision[Decision requested event]
  Decision --> Human[Human decision recorded event]
  Human --> Effect[Effect attempted event]
  Effect --> Verified[Effect verified event]
  Verified --> Outcome[Department outcome recorded event]
  Outcome --> Audit[Audit and learning consumers]
  Workflow --> Failure[Failure or escalation event]
  Failure --> Audit
```

#### CAT-AG-P4-DEPT-10-CTX — Commerce and Affiliate — Context Flow

**Diagram ID:** `CAT-AG-P4-DEPT-10-CTX`
**Title:** Commerce and Affiliate — Context Flow

```mermaid
flowchart LR

  Retrieve --> Provenance[Revision freshness rights and provenance]

  Redact --> Budget[Context and token budget]

```

#### CAT-AG-P4-DEPT-10-KNW — Commerce and Affiliate — Knowledge Flow

**Title:** Commerce and Affiliate — Knowledge Flow

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  Evidence[Department evidence] --> Claim[Proposed claim]

```

#### CAT-AG-P4-DEPT-10-MEM — Commerce and Affiliate — Memory Flow

**Diagram ID:** `CAT-AG-P4-DEPT-10-MEM`
**Title:** Commerce and Affiliate — Memory Flow
**Purpose:** Show run state, episodic proposals, consent, retention, synchronization and deletion for the department.
**Audience:** Department owners, executive advisors, agent managers, architects, implementers, operators, security reviewers and auditors.
**Reading Order:** Start with ephemeral working state; only verified purpose-bound outcomes cross into durable Memory.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  Run[Department collaboration run] --> Working[Ephemeral working state]
  Working --> Checkpoint[Encrypted workflow checkpoint]
  Checkpoint --> Verified{{Outcome verified}}
  Verified -->|No| Quarantine[Expire or quarantine state]
  Verified -->|Yes| Proposal[Memory proposal]
  Proposal --> Classify[Class purpose subject and tenant]
  Classify --> Consent[Consent retention and provenance]
  Consent --> Memory[Memory authority commits]
  Memory --> Sync[Replica and cache synchronization]
  Sync --> Receipt[Memory receipt]
  Receipt --> Expire[Retention tombstone and deletion proof]
```

#### CAT-AG-P4-DEPT-10-DEC — Commerce and Affiliate — Decision Flow

**Diagram ID:** `CAT-AG-P4-DEPT-10-DEC`
**Title:** Commerce and Affiliate — Decision Flow
**Purpose:** Show facts, options, constraints, human judgment and exact execution decision for `CAT-DEPT-COM`.
**Audience:** Department owners, executive advisors, agent managers, architects, implementers, operators, security reviewers and auditors.
**Reading Order:** Read top to bottom; agent recommendation stops before accountable human choice and effect authorization.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  Question[Decision question and owner] --> Facts[Verified facts and source revisions]
  Facts --> Options[Feasible options and counterfactual]
  Options --> Constraints[Policy rights Security Finance Data and resources]
  Constraints --> Uncertainty[Assumptions dissent and uncertainty]
  Uncertainty --> Recommend[Bounded agent recommendation]
  Recommend --> Human[Authenticated human judgment]
  Human --> Result{{Approve deny revise defer or escalate}}
  Result -->|Approve| Bind[Bind exact scope digest and expiry]
  Result -->|Revise| Options
  Result -->|Deny| Close[Record denial]
  Result -->|Defer| Wait[Safe waiting state]
  Result -->|Escalate| Authority[Higher named human authority]
  Bind --> Execute[Governed domain effect]
  Execute --> Verify[Verify authoritative outcome]
```

#### CAT-AG-P4-DEPT-10-FAIL — Commerce and Affiliate — Failure Flow

**Diagram ID:** `CAT-AG-P4-DEPT-10-FAIL`
**Title:** Commerce and Affiliate — Failure Flow
**Purpose:** Show detection, containment, effect classification, evidence and escalation for department failure.
**Audience:** Department owners, executive advisors, agent managers, architects, implementers, operators, security reviewers and auditors.
**Reading Order:** Read top to bottom and never follow a retry path before authoritative effect state is known.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  Signal[Failure uncertainty or policy violation] --> Stop[Stop dependent effects]
  Stop --> Own[Open owned failure or incident case]
  Own --> Preserve[Preserve state versions and evidence]
  Preserve --> Attempt{{Material effect attempted}}
  Attempt -->|Yes| Truth[Query domain source of truth]
  Attempt -->|No| Class[Classify failure and retryability]
  Truth --> Known{{Effect state known}}
  Known -->|No| Quarantine[Quarantine and human escalation]
  Known -->|Yes| Class
  Class --> Safe{{Retry safe budgeted and useful}}
  Safe -->|Yes| Recovery[Enter recovery flow]
  Safe -->|No| Escalate[Named owner decision]
  Quarantine --> Escalate
```

#### CAT-AG-P4-DEPT-10-REC — Commerce and Affiliate — Recovery Flow

**Diagram ID:** `CAT-AG-P4-DEPT-10-REC`
**Title:** Commerce and Affiliate — Recovery Flow
**Purpose:** Show source-of-truth reconciliation, approved remediation, invariant verification and closure.
**Audience:** Department owners, executive advisors, agent managers, architects, implementers, operators, security reviewers and auditors.
**Reading Order:** Read left to right; closure requires linked evidence that the original and recovery effects reconcile.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  Case[Owned recovery case] --> Scope[Affected tenants tasks data and effects]
  Scope --> Reconcile[Authoritative state reconciliation]
  Reconcile --> Plan[Resume compensate rollback abandon or migrate]
  Plan --> Decision{{Human approval required}}
  Decision -->|Yes| Human[Authorized human decision]
  Decision -->|No| Execute[Bounded remediation]
  Human --> Execute
  Execute --> Verify[Verify business Security Data and domain invariants]
  Verify --> Evidence[Link original and recovery receipts]
  Evidence --> Restore[Restore narrow service or close]
  Restore --> Review[Incident performance and learning review]
```

#### Department Card Acceptance Checklist

- [ ] Human accountability and manager boundaries resolve.
- [ ] Agents and versions are certified for exact roles.
- [ ] Responsibilities have no overlap without a named decider.
- [ ] Inputs and outputs have owned schemas.
- [ ] Every event has producer, consumer, replay and retention rules.
- [ ] APIs enforce identity, deadline, cancellation and trace.
- [ ] Knowledge and Memory remain separate governed authorities.
- [ ] Security model includes isolation, permissions and incident route.
- [ ] Metrics cannot reward unsafe speed or hidden failures.
- [ ] KPIs include evidence and human impact.
- [ ] Failure recovery reconciles effects.
- [ ] Future expansion has migration, recertification and dissolution.
- [ ] All eight collaboration flows match contracts.

#### CAT-AG-P4-DEPT-11-DEC — Content and Publishing — Decision Flow

```mermaid
flowchart TD
```

#### CAT-AG-P4-DEPT-11-FAIL — Content and Publishing — Failure Flow

**Diagram ID:** `CAT-AG-P4-DEPT-11-FAIL`
**Title:** Content and Publishing — Failure Flow
**Purpose:** Show detection, containment, effect classification, evidence and escalation for department failure.
**Audience:** Department owners, executive advisors, agent managers, architects, implementers, operators, security reviewers and auditors.
**Reading Order:** Read top to bottom and never follow a retry path before authoritative effect state is known.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  Signal[Failure uncertainty or policy violation] --> Stop[Stop dependent effects]
  Stop --> Own[Open owned failure or incident case]
  Own --> Preserve[Preserve state versions and evidence]
  Preserve --> Attempt{{Material effect attempted}}
  Attempt -->|Yes| Truth[Query domain source of truth]
  Attempt -->|No| Class[Classify failure and retryability]
  Truth --> Known{{Effect state known}}
  Known -->|No| Quarantine[Quarantine and human escalation]
  Known -->|Yes| Class
  Class --> Safe{{Retry safe budgeted and useful}}
  Safe -->|Yes| Recovery[Enter recovery flow]
  Safe -->|No| Escalate[Named owner decision]
  Quarantine --> Escalate
```

#### CAT-AG-P4-DEPT-11-REC — Content and Publishing — Recovery Flow

**Diagram ID:** `CAT-AG-P4-DEPT-11-REC`
**Title:** Content and Publishing — Recovery Flow
**Purpose:** Show source-of-truth reconciliation, approved remediation, invariant verification and closure.
**Audience:** Department owners, executive advisors, agent managers, architects, implementers, operators, security reviewers and auditors.
**Reading Order:** Read left to right; closure requires linked evidence that the original and recovery effects reconcile.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  Case[Owned recovery case] --> Scope[Affected tenants tasks data and effects]
  Scope --> Reconcile[Authoritative state reconciliation]
  Reconcile --> Plan[Resume compensate rollback abandon or migrate]
  Plan --> Decision{{Human approval required}}
  Decision -->|Yes| Human[Authorized human decision]
  Decision -->|No| Execute[Bounded remediation]
  Human --> Execute
  Execute --> Verify[Verify business Security Data and domain invariants]
  Verify --> Evidence[Link original and recovery receipts]
  Evidence --> Restore[Restore narrow service or close]
  Restore --> Review[Incident performance and learning review]
```

#### Department Card Acceptance Checklist

- [ ] Human accountability and manager boundaries resolve.
- [ ] Agents and versions are certified for exact roles.
- [ ] Responsibilities have no overlap without a named decider.
- [ ] Inputs and outputs have owned schemas.
- [ ] Every event has producer, consumer, replay and retention rules.
- [ ] APIs enforce identity, deadline, cancellation and trace.
- [ ] Knowledge and Memory remain separate governed authorities.
- [ ] Security model includes isolation, permissions and incident route.
- [ ] Metrics cannot reward unsafe speed or hidden failures.
- [ ] KPIs include evidence and human impact.
- [ ] Failure recovery reconciles effects.
- [ ] Future expansion has migration, recertification and dissolution.
- [ ] All eight collaboration flows match contracts.

#### Department Operating Cadence

1. **Accept human-chartered outcomes and explicit non-goals.** The department records owner, state, versions, budget and evidence before progressing.
2. **Verify manager and member certifications.** The department records owner, state, versions, budget and evidence before progressing.
3. **Resolve demand, priority and capacity.** The department records owner, state, versions, budget and evidence before progressing.
4. **Issue typed tasks with narrowed authority.** The department records owner, state, versions, budget and evidence before progressing.
5. **Exchange bounded context through owned contracts.** The department records owner, state, versions, budget and evidence before progressing.
6. **Review evidence, dissent, risk and resource use.** The department records owner, state, versions, budget and evidence before progressing.
7. **Obtain independent decisions and approvals.** The department records owner, state, versions, budget and evidence before progressing.
8. **Verify effects, business outcomes and human impact.** The department records owner, state, versions, budget and evidence before progressing.
9. **Handle failures through owned reconciliation.** The department records owner, state, versions, budget and evidence before progressing.
10. **Review metrics, learning proposals and department charter.** The department records owner, state, versions, budget and evidence before progressing.

#### Department Collaboration Contract

| Dimension | Requirement |
|---|---|
| Human sponsor | CEO and COO Agents advise; Human Customer Experience Owner is accountable; Supervisor coordinates delegated work |
| Participating agents | KATA human-facing boundary; CATA coordinator; authorized specialists; no independent KATA execution authority |
| Context | Purpose-bound package assembled from customer request; authenticated context; consent; policy; knowledge; account state; support history; urgency and accessibility preferences. |
| Knowledge | approved product and policy knowledge; account and service state by purpose; accessibility and communication guidance |
| Memory | consent-governed preferences and reviewed interaction episodes; no hidden emotional profiling or unrelated conversation retention |
| Decision | Options and evidence are routed to the accountable human named in `CEO and COO Agents advise; Human Customer Experience Owner is accountable; Supervisor coordinates delegated work`. |
| Security | customer identity, consent, data minimization, redaction, anti-impersonation, no silent approval, accessibility and safe human handoff |
| Completion | Outputs `clear answer; evidence and uncertainty; consent or approval request; reversible service action; escalation; customer confirmation; feedback` meet schema, approval, verification and evidence requirements. |

```mermaid
  Decision -->|Yes| Human[Authorized human decision]
  Decision -->|No| Execute[Bounded remediation]
  Human --> Execute
  Execute --> Verify[Verify business Security Data and domain invariants]
  Verify --> Evidence[Link original and recovery receipts]
  Evidence --> Restore[Restore narrow service or close]
  Restore --> Review[Incident performance and learning review]
```

#### Department Card Acceptance Checklist

- [ ] Human accountability and manager boundaries resolve.
- [ ] Agents and versions are certified for exact roles.
- [ ] Responsibilities have no overlap without a named decider.
- [ ] Inputs and outputs have owned schemas.
- [ ] Every event has producer, consumer, replay and retention rules.
- [ ] APIs enforce identity, deadline, cancellation and trace.
- [ ] Knowledge and Memory remain separate governed authorities.
- [ ] Security model includes isolation, permissions and incident route.
- [ ] Metrics cannot reward unsafe speed or hidden failures.
- [ ] KPIs include evidence and human impact.
- [ ] Failure recovery reconciles effects.
- [ ] Future expansion has migration, recertification and dissolution.
- [ ] All eight collaboration flows match contracts.

## 73. Agent Teams

**Section ID:** `CAT-AG-P4-73`
**Constitutional domain:** Workforce Collaboration
**Human accountable owner:** Human Team Sponsor
**Primary record:** team charter
**Decision status:** Final Part 4 design constitution; implementation and production authority remain evidence-gated.

### Constitutional Purpose

Define durable or time-bounded teams with one mission, explicit roles, shared service levels, governed context and measurable outcomes.

This section is complete only when `team charter` is attributable, typed, policy-valid, resource-accounted, observable, recoverable and reviewable by Human Team Sponsor. The non-negotiable invariant is: Team membership never creates shared credentials, pooled hidden memory, majority-rule policy or ambiguous accountability.

### Operating Contract

| Contract dimension | Normative requirement |
|---|---|
| Business outcome | Define durable or time-bounded teams with one mission, explicit roles, shared service levels, governed context and measurable outcomes. |
| Human accountability | Human Team Sponsor |
| Authoritative artifact | team charter |
| Required inputs | authenticated charter; current workforce collaboration state; policy and authority snapshot; owned evidence; deadline; budget; acceptance criteria; human accountability route |
| Required outputs | versioned team charter; decision evidence; state transition; exceptions; resource account; terminal receipt |
| Constitutional invariant | Team membership never creates shared credentials, pooled hidden memory, majority-rule policy or ambiguous accountability. |
| Default authority | A0/A1 advice and preparation unless an exact role card, policy, certification and effect-specific grant narrow a higher ceiling. |
| Default failure | Stop the smallest unsafe scope, preserve state and evidence, reconcile any attempted effect, and route the unresolved decision to the named owner. |
| Performance envelope | Declare separate SLOs for admission, queueing, decision, effect verification and evidence publication; 100 percent of terminal team charter records must be attributable and schema-valid. |
| Scale model | Partition workforce collaboration work by tenant and bounded aggregate, preserve global contract compatibility, cap concurrency and fan-out, and fail closed when ownership or policy cannot converge. |
| Future direction | dynamic capability teams, follow-the-sun teams, enterprise collaboration and outcome-based staffing |

### End-to-End Constitutional Procedure

1. **State measurable team mission.** Validate identity, scope, owner, policy, data, authority, budget and deadline; persist the decision and do not begin a dependent step until its preconditions and evidence pass.
2. **Appoint human sponsor and lead.** Validate identity, scope, owner, policy, data, authority, budget and deadline; persist the decision and do not begin a dependent step until its preconditions and evidence pass.
3. **Select certified members.** Validate identity, scope, owner, policy, data, authority, budget and deadline; persist the decision and do not begin a dependent step until its preconditions and evidence pass.
4. **Calculate bounded authority.** Validate identity, scope, owner, policy, data, authority, budget and deadline; persist the decision and do not begin a dependent step until its preconditions and evidence pass.
5. **Provision scoped workspace.** Validate identity, scope, owner, policy, data, authority, budget and deadline; persist the decision and do not begin a dependent step until its preconditions and evidence pass.
6. **Execute typed collaboration.** Validate identity, scope, owner, policy, data, authority, budget and deadline; persist the decision and do not begin a dependent step until its preconditions and evidence pass.
7. **Review team health.** Validate identity, scope, owner, policy, data, authority, budget and deadline; persist the decision and do not begin a dependent step until its preconditions and evidence pass.
8. **Dissolve and revoke access.** Validate identity, scope, owner, policy, data, authority, budget and deadline; persist the decision and do not begin a dependent step until its preconditions and evidence pass.

### Required Decision Record

| Record component | Minimum fields | Independent check |
|---|---|---|
| Charter | outcome, non-goals, sponsor, owner, acceptance, deadline and expiry | mission and owner resolver |
| Identity | logical ID, immutable version, runtime principal, tenant, environment and operator | identity and lifecycle service |
| Evidence | sources, revisions, rights, freshness, transformations, contradictions and confidence | domain and provenance validator |
| Decision | facts, assumptions, alternatives, dissent, risk, cost, uncertainty and requested judgment | human or independent evaluator |
| Authority | role ceiling, task grant, policy, data purpose, approval and live revocation state | policy enforcement point |
| Execution | plan, resources, tools, state versions, checkpoints, attempts and effects | orchestrator and domain gateways |
| Outcome | typed status, acceptance, quality, business result, externalities, incidents and follow-up owner | task owner and Analytics |
| Audit | correlation, causation, digests, timestamps, receipts, retention and access history | independent Audit owner |

### Business Perspective

Agent Teams makes workforce collaboration an accountable operating capability rather than a title, prompt persona or undocumented model behavior. Business owners receive alternatives, value, full cost, risk, uncertainty, rights impact, dependencies and evidence before accepting a consequential result.

The business must fund control work as part of delivery: attribution, human review, Security, recovery, audit and lifecycle are not optional overhead. Success is the durable outcome represented by `team charter`, not output volume or agent activity.

### Engineering Perspective

Implement agent teams through versioned schemas, deterministic state machines, owned ports, immutable identities, hierarchical budgets, cancellation, idempotency, checkpoints and source-of-truth verification. Probabilistic inference may propose; deterministic services authorize and commit.

Make time, randomness, provider routes, policy versions and external effects injectable in tests. Classify every dependency as startup-hard, runtime-required, optional or asynchronous; define timeout, circuit, fallback, replay, migration and failure ownership explicitly.

### Architecture Perspective

Human Team Sponsor remains the human accountability boundary. The Workforce Collaboration domain owns semantics and canonical state; CATA coordinates portfolios, Supervisor coordinates runtime, specialists produce bounded artifacts, and policy/effect gateways prevent orchestration from becoming authority.

Commands request owned work, queries read without hidden mutation, events report committed facts, approvals authorize exact effects, notifications inform and receipts prove attempts. Projections and caches are rebuildable and never promoted to source of truth by convenience.

### AI Coding Perspective

Before changing implementation for section `73`, load `context/05_AGENTS.md`, `context/00_PROJECT_CONTEXT.md`, `architecture/Agent_Communication.md`, inspect current schemas and ownership, and identify the exact deterministic guard. An AI coding agent must not infer implementation permission from this final documentation status, an empty directory, a draft ADR or a provider feature.

Write negative tests first for mission drift, forged identity, cross-tenant data, stale context, permission expansion, approval substitution, prompt injection, duplicate effect, cancellation, evidence loss and migration incompatibility. Keep changes minimal, preserve user work and report unresolved assumptions.

### Human Perspective

Humans see who the agent is, why it is acting, who owns the task, what evidence it used, what it knows and does not know, what decision is requested, what alternatives exist, what it costs, and what happens on approval, denial or delay. Human Team Sponsor can stop or narrow work without navigating hidden agent conversations.

Interfaces must avoid automation bias, anthropomorphic pressure and approval fatigue. They provide accessible evidence, dissent, uncertainty, scope, expiry, consequences, revision, denial, escalation and recovery controls. Human silence is never consent or approval.

### Security Perspective

Apply zero standing privilege, workload identity, tenant and environment isolation, purpose-bound data, secret-manager references, prompt and tool injection defenses, egress policy, sandboxing, rate limits, revocation, tamper-evident receipts and a tested kill switch. Section invariant: Team membership never creates shared credentials, pooled hidden memory, majority-rule policy or ambiguous accountability.

Threat tests cover confused deputy, role-title escalation, malicious context, poisoned knowledge, memory exfiltration, approval laundering, replay, supply-chain substitution, side channels, resource exhaustion, audit tampering and compromised provider behavior.

### Performance Perspective

Declare separate SLOs for admission, queueing, decision, effect verification and evidence publication; 100 percent of terminal team charter records must be attributable and schema-valid.

Measure queue, policy, context, model, tool, approval, effect verification, recovery and evidence latency separately. Report percentiles, quality, safety, cost, human burden, cancellation delay and terminal classes; never improve averages by dropping rejected, failed or quarantined work.

### Scalability Perspective

Partition workforce collaboration work by tenant and bounded aggregate, preserve global contract compatibility, cap concurrency and fan-out, and fail closed when ownership or policy cannot converge.

Use bounded fan-out, backpressure, fairness reservations, locality and asynchronous facts where ordering is unnecessary. Cross-region or cross-node scale requires explicit data residency, identity federation, protocol compatibility, conflict resolution, disconnect behavior and reconciliation.

### Future Evolution

Future evolution may include dynamic capability teams, follow-the-sun teams, enterprise collaboration and outcome-based staffing. Every increment begins as a hypothesis, runs in simulation or sandbox, proves quality and safety, obtains independent human authorization, canaries immutable versions and retains rollback, migration and historical interpretation.

Future capability never retroactively authorizes current behavior. Rights, law, accountability, tenant choice, evidence, Security and safe exit remain constraints even when technology, organization, providers or economic models change.

### Implementation Contract

- [ ] Define canonical schema, owner, compatibility policy and stable error taxonomy.
- [ ] Encode identity, policy, permission, approval, limits and isolation outside the model.
- [ ] Map each AI capability to an owned port, data class, effect class and receipt.
- [ ] Implement state transitions with optimistic concurrency and durable checkpoints.
- [ ] Propagate correlation, causation, deadline, cancellation and budget through every call.
- [ ] Verify external effects from authoritative state before completion or retry.
- [ ] Provide degraded behavior, circuit breaking, containment, recovery and reconciliation.
- [ ] Redact operational logs and retain protected forensic evidence by explicit policy.
- [ ] Create role-quality, adversarial, tenancy, load, chaos, migration and rollback tests.
- [ ] Ship dashboards, alert thresholds, runbooks, on-call ownership and support boundaries.
- [ ] Canary an immutable version and retain a tested last-known-safe rollback target.
- [ ] Require independent owner acceptance and applicable certification before production.

### ADR References

- Candidate implementation decision record: `adr/ADR-0046.md`. It is a Draft placeholder until completed and accepted; the filename grants no authority.
- A material ADR must record context, decision, alternatives, consequences, rights and security, data, economics, operability, compatibility, migration, rollback, tests, evidence and supersession scope.
- Where no accepted ADR exists, implementation must preserve the more restrictive current constitution and seek a human architecture decision.

### Constitutional Control Catalogue

#### CAT-AG-P4-73-C01 — Charter Scope

- **Rule:** For agent teams, bind all work to a signed outcome, explicit non-goals, owner, expiry and acceptance criteria.
- **Business test:** `team charter` exposes the cost, benefit, risk, owner, uncertainty and consequence of this control to an accountable reviewer.
- **Engineering enforcement:** The boundary responsible for `state measurable team mission` validates this control before state change and again before any related material effect.
- **AI behavior:** Missing, stale, contradictory, denied or unverifiable control data causes a typed stop, wait, refusal or escalation; the model never fills the gap with confidence.
- **Human boundary:** Human Team Sponsor receives the exact requested decision and evidence when human judgment is required; no UI default or silence creates consent.
- **Security assertion:** Forged role, cross-tenant reference, replay, changed payload, expired grant, injected instruction and evidence tampering all fail closed and emit a protected signal.
- **Performance assertion:** Enforcement remains inside the declared SLO and resource reserve; overload applies backpressure rather than removing checks.
- **Evidence:** Store logical and runtime identity, tenant, versions, policy, grants, input/output digests, decision, state, timestamps, owner and redacted receipts.
- **Failure code:** `CAT_P4_73_01_CONSTITUTIONAL_CONTROL`; dependent work remains non-success and any attempted effect enters reconciliation.
- **Recovery:** Contain the affected scope, establish authoritative effect state, restore the invariant, obtain required human decision and link a terminal recovery receipt.
- **Implementation test:** Run positive, negative, boundary, cancellation, duplicate, stale-state, migration and compromised-dependency fixtures deterministically.
- **Ownership:** Human Team Sponsor owns residual business judgment; the Workforce Collaboration service owner owns enforcement; Audit owns independent evidence review.
- **Constitutional assertion:** An independent reviewer can reproduce the `Charter Scope` disposition without trusting hidden reasoning, title, provider success or undocumented operator explanation.

- [ ] Approvals and overrides bind exact immutable scope.
- [ ] Isolation, sandbox, egress, secrets and supply-chain controls are tested.
- [ ] External effects use idempotency and source-of-truth verification.
- [ ] Logs, metrics, traces, audit and evidence are redacted and complete.
- [ ] Failure, partial result, uncertainty and quarantine are explicit states.
- [ ] Recovery reconciles effects and proves restored invariants.
- [ ] Evolution has evaluation, certification, migration and rollback evidence.
- [ ] Human interfaces are accessible, non-coercive and preserve denial and escalation.
- [ ] An accepted ADR exists before irreversible architecture choice.
- [ ] Independent review can reproduce every consequential disposition.

### AI Memory Anchor

**Memory anchor `P4-73`:** `Agent Teams` is governed by `team charter` and owned in human accountability by Human Team Sponsor. Preserve: Team membership never creates shared credentials, pooled hidden memory, majority-rule policy or ambiguous accountability. On conflict or uncertainty, stop the smallest unsafe scope, retain evidence and escalate; never infer authority from an executive title, confidence, group membership, budget or future ambition.

### Workforce Evolution Control Table

| Control area | Current constitutional requirement | Promotion evidence | Rollback trigger |
|---|---|---|---|
| Role definition | mission, owner, authority, interfaces and prohibitions | complete card and negative tests | scope drift or orphan owner |
| Training | isolated curriculum and clean datasets | sealed evaluation and red-team pass | contamination or unsafe behavior |
| Team membership | versioned charter and individual grants | collaboration and failure exercises | permission leakage or unresolved conflict |
| Management | bounded span and transparent delegation | low rework, complete evidence and fair allocation | metric gaming or hidden failure |
| Autonomy | time and effect-bounded grant | sustained quality, safety and recovery proof | incident, drift, missing receipt or policy change |
| Organization | named departments and independent controls | reduced coordination cost without control loss | circular reporting or self-approval |
| Federation | operator identity and compatible contracts | disconnect, reconciliation and residency tests | trust, legal or protocol incompatibility |
| Retirement | no owned work and revoked access | migration and evidence-retention proof | orphan state or active dependency |

## 74. Agent Squads

**Section ID:** `CAT-AG-P4-74`
**Constitutional domain:** Mission Execution
**Human accountable owner:** Human Mission Sponsor
**Primary record:** squad mission record
**Decision status:** Final Part 4 design constitution; implementation and production authority remain evidence-gated.

### Constitutional Purpose

Define small cross-functional mission squads optimized for one outcome, short feedback loops and explicit handoffs.

This section is complete only when `squad mission record` is attributable, typed, policy-valid, resource-accounted, observable, recoverable and reviewable by Human Mission Sponsor. The non-negotiable invariant is: A squad cannot become a bypass around department owners, approval chains, resource ceilings or independent Security and Finance review.

### Operating Contract

| Contract dimension | Normative requirement |
|---|---|
| Business outcome | Define small cross-functional mission squads optimized for one outcome, short feedback loops and explicit handoffs. |
| Human accountability | Human Mission Sponsor |
| Authoritative artifact | squad mission record |
| Required inputs | authenticated charter; current mission execution state; policy and authority snapshot; owned evidence; deadline; budget; acceptance criteria; human accountability route |
| Required outputs | versioned squad mission record; decision evidence; state transition; exceptions; resource account; terminal receipt |
| Constitutional invariant | A squad cannot become a bypass around department owners, approval chains, resource ceilings or independent Security and Finance review. |
| Default authority | A0/A1 advice and preparation unless an exact role card, policy, certification and effect-specific grant narrow a higher ceiling. |
| Default failure | Stop the smallest unsafe scope, preserve state and evidence, reconcile any attempted effect, and route the unresolved decision to the named owner. |
| Performance envelope | Declare separate SLOs for admission, queueing, decision, effect verification and evidence publication; 100 percent of terminal squad mission record records must be attributable and schema-valid. |
| Scale model | Partition mission execution work by tenant and bounded aggregate, preserve global contract compatibility, cap concurrency and fan-out, and fail closed when ownership or policy cannot converge. |
| Future direction | automatically assembled squads, regional launch squads and reusable mission templates |

### End-to-End Constitutional Procedure

1. **Receive approved mission.** Validate identity, scope, owner, policy, data, authority, budget and deadline; persist the decision and do not begin a dependent step until its preconditions and evidence pass.
2. **Select minimum roles.** Validate identity, scope, owner, policy, data, authority, budget and deadline; persist the decision and do not begin a dependent step until its preconditions and evidence pass.
3. **Bind squad budget and deadline.** Validate identity, scope, owner, policy, data, authority, budget and deadline; persist the decision and do not begin a dependent step until its preconditions and evidence pass.
4. **Declare decision and approval map.** Validate identity, scope, owner, policy, data, authority, budget and deadline; persist the decision and do not begin a dependent step until its preconditions and evidence pass.
5. **Execute short bounded iterations.** Validate identity, scope, owner, policy, data, authority, budget and deadline; persist the decision and do not begin a dependent step until its preconditions and evidence pass.
6. **Demonstrate increment with evidence.** Validate identity, scope, owner, policy, data, authority, budget and deadline; persist the decision and do not begin a dependent step until its preconditions and evidence pass.
7. **Replan within charter.** Validate identity, scope, owner, policy, data, authority, budget and deadline; persist the decision and do not begin a dependent step until its preconditions and evidence pass.
8. **Close and return resources.** Validate identity, scope, owner, policy, data, authority, budget and deadline; persist the decision and do not begin a dependent step until its preconditions and evidence pass.

### Required Decision Record

| Record component | Minimum fields | Independent check |
|---|---|---|
| Charter | outcome, non-goals, sponsor, owner, acceptance, deadline and expiry | mission and owner resolver |
| Identity | logical ID, immutable version, runtime principal, tenant, environment and operator | identity and lifecycle service |
| Evidence | sources, revisions, rights, freshness, transformations, contradictions and confidence | domain and provenance validator |
| Decision | facts, assumptions, alternatives, dissent, risk, cost, uncertainty and requested judgment | human or independent evaluator |
| Authority | role ceiling, task grant, policy, data purpose, approval and live revocation state | policy enforcement point |
| Execution | plan, resources, tools, state versions, checkpoints, attempts and effects | orchestrator and domain gateways |
| Outcome | typed status, acceptance, quality, business result, externalities, incidents and follow-up owner | task owner and Analytics |
| Audit | correlation, causation, digests, timestamps, receipts, retention and access history | independent Audit owner |

### Business Perspective

Agent Squads makes mission execution an accountable operating capability rather than a title, prompt persona or undocumented model behavior. Business owners receive alternatives, value, full cost, risk, uncertainty, rights impact, dependencies and evidence before accepting a consequential result.

The business must fund control work as part of delivery: attribution, human review, Security, recovery, audit and lifecycle are not optional overhead. Success is the durable outcome represented by `squad mission record`, not output volume or agent activity.

### Engineering Perspective

Implement agent squads through versioned schemas, deterministic state machines, owned ports, immutable identities, hierarchical budgets, cancellation, idempotency, checkpoints and source-of-truth verification. Probabilistic inference may propose; deterministic services authorize and commit.

Make time, randomness, provider routes, policy versions and external effects injectable in tests. Classify every dependency as startup-hard, runtime-required, optional or asynchronous; define timeout, circuit, fallback, replay, migration and failure ownership explicitly.

### Architecture Perspective

Human Mission Sponsor remains the human accountability boundary. The Mission Execution domain owns semantics and canonical state; CATA coordinates portfolios, Supervisor coordinates runtime, specialists produce bounded artifacts, and policy/effect gateways prevent orchestration from becoming authority.

Commands request owned work, queries read without hidden mutation, events report committed facts, approvals authorize exact effects, notifications inform and receipts prove attempts. Projections and caches are rebuildable and never promoted to source of truth by convenience.

### AI Coding Perspective

Before changing implementation for section `74`, load `context/05_AGENTS.md`, `context/04_ARCHITECTURE.md`, inspect current schemas and ownership, and identify the exact deterministic guard. An AI coding agent must not infer implementation permission from this final documentation status, an empty directory, a draft ADR or a provider feature.

Write negative tests first for mission drift, forged identity, cross-tenant data, stale context, permission expansion, approval substitution, prompt injection, duplicate effect, cancellation, evidence loss and migration incompatibility. Keep changes minimal, preserve user work and report unresolved assumptions.

### Human Perspective

Humans see who the agent is, why it is acting, who owns the task, what evidence it used, what it knows and does not know, what decision is requested, what alternatives exist, what it costs, and what happens on approval, denial or delay. Human Mission Sponsor can stop or narrow work without navigating hidden agent conversations.

Interfaces must avoid automation bias, anthropomorphic pressure and approval fatigue. They provide accessible evidence, dissent, uncertainty, scope, expiry, consequences, revision, denial, escalation and recovery controls. Human silence is never consent or approval.

### Security Perspective

Apply zero standing privilege, workload identity, tenant and environment isolation, purpose-bound data, secret-manager references, prompt and tool injection defenses, egress policy, sandboxing, rate limits, revocation, tamper-evident receipts and a tested kill switch. Section invariant: A squad cannot become a bypass around department owners, approval chains, resource ceilings or independent Security and Finance review.

Threat tests cover confused deputy, role-title escalation, malicious context, poisoned knowledge, memory exfiltration, approval laundering, replay, supply-chain substitution, side channels, resource exhaustion, audit tampering and compromised provider behavior.

### Performance Perspective

Declare separate SLOs for admission, queueing, decision, effect verification and evidence publication; 100 percent of terminal squad mission record records must be attributable and schema-valid.

Measure queue, policy, context, model, tool, approval, effect verification, recovery and evidence latency separately. Report percentiles, quality, safety, cost, human burden, cancellation delay and terminal classes; never improve averages by dropping rejected, failed or quarantined work.

### Scalability Perspective

Partition mission execution work by tenant and bounded aggregate, preserve global contract compatibility, cap concurrency and fan-out, and fail closed when ownership or policy cannot converge.

Use bounded fan-out, backpressure, fairness reservations, locality and asynchronous facts where ordering is unnecessary. Cross-region or cross-node scale requires explicit data residency, identity federation, protocol compatibility, conflict resolution, disconnect behavior and reconciliation.

### Future Evolution

Future evolution may include automatically assembled squads, regional launch squads and reusable mission templates. Every increment begins as a hypothesis, runs in simulation or sandbox, proves quality and safety, obtains independent human authorization, canaries immutable versions and retains rollback, migration and historical interpretation.

Future capability never retroactively authorizes current behavior. Rights, law, accountability, tenant choice, evidence, Security and safe exit remain constraints even when technology, organization, providers or economic models change.

### Implementation Contract

- [ ] Define canonical schema, owner, compatibility policy and stable error taxonomy.
- [ ] Encode identity, policy, permission, approval, limits and isolation outside the model.
- [ ] Map each AI capability to an owned port, data class, effect class and receipt.
- [ ] Implement state transitions with optimistic concurrency and durable checkpoints.
- [ ] Propagate correlation, causation, deadline, cancellation and budget through every call.
- [ ] Verify external effects from authoritative state before completion or retry.
- [ ] Provide degraded behavior, circuit breaking, containment, recovery and reconciliation.
- [ ] Redact operational logs and retain protected forensic evidence by explicit policy.
- [ ] Create role-quality, adversarial, tenancy, load, chaos, migration and rollback tests.
- [ ] Ship dashboards, alert thresholds, runbooks, on-call ownership and support boundaries.
- [ ] Canary an immutable version and retain a tested last-known-safe rollback target.
- [ ] Require independent owner acceptance and applicable certification before production.

### ADR References

- Candidate implementation decision record: `adr/ADR-0047.md`. It is a Draft placeholder until completed and accepted; the filename grants no authority.
- A material ADR must record context, decision, alternatives, consequences, rights and security, data, economics, operability, compatibility, migration, rollback, tests, evidence and supersession scope.
- Where no accepted ADR exists, implementation must preserve the more restrictive current constitution and seek a human architecture decision.

### Section Acceptance Checklist

- [ ] Human accountable owner and operational owner resolve.
- [ ] Mission, non-goals, inputs, outputs and terminal criteria are typed.
- [ ] Identity, version, tenant, environment and lifecycle are immutable for a run.
- [ ] Permission and authority are deterministic, revocable and effect-specific.
- [ ] Data, context, Knowledge and Memory preserve purpose, provenance and lifecycle.
- [ ] Decision artifacts expose alternatives, dissent, uncertainty and requested judgment.
- [ ] Budgets preserve verification, recovery and safe shutdown.
- [ ] Communication semantics, schemas, replay and ownership are registered.
- [ ] Approvals and overrides bind exact immutable scope.
- [ ] Isolation, sandbox, egress, secrets and supply-chain controls are tested.
- [ ] External effects use idempotency and source-of-truth verification.
- [ ] Logs, metrics, traces, audit and evidence are redacted and complete.
- [ ] Failure, partial result, uncertainty and quarantine are explicit states.
- [ ] Recovery reconciles effects and proves restored invariants.
- [ ] Evolution has evaluation, certification, migration and rollback evidence.
- [ ] Human interfaces are accessible, non-coercive and preserve denial and escalation.
- [ ] An accepted ADR exists before irreversible architecture choice.
- [ ] Independent review can reproduce every consequential disposition.

### AI Memory Anchor

**Memory anchor `P4-74`:** `Agent Squads` is governed by `squad mission record` and owned in human accountability by Human Mission Sponsor. Preserve: A squad cannot become a bypass around department owners, approval chains, resource ceilings or independent Security and Finance review. On conflict or uncertainty, stop the smallest unsafe scope, retain evidence and escalate; never infer authority from an executive title, confidence, group membership, budget or future ambition.

### Workforce Evolution Control Table

| Control area | Current constitutional requirement | Promotion evidence | Rollback trigger |
|---|---|---|---|
| Role definition | mission, owner, authority, interfaces and prohibitions | complete card and negative tests | scope drift or orphan owner |
| Training | isolated curriculum and clean datasets | sealed evaluation and red-team pass | contamination or unsafe behavior |
| Team membership | versioned charter and individual grants | collaboration and failure exercises | permission leakage or unresolved conflict |
| Management | bounded span and transparent delegation | low rework, complete evidence and fair allocation | metric gaming or hidden failure |
| Autonomy | time and effect-bounded grant | sustained quality, safety and recovery proof | incident, drift, missing receipt or policy change |
| Organization | named departments and independent controls | reduced coordination cost without control loss | circular reporting or self-approval |
| Federation | operator identity and compatible contracts | disconnect, reconciliation and residency tests | trust, legal or protocol incompatibility |
| Retirement | no owned work and revoked access | migration and evidence-retention proof | orphan state or active dependency |

## 75. Agent Managers

**Section ID:** `CAT-AG-P4-75`
**Constitutional domain:** Workforce Management
**Human accountable owner:** Human Workforce Owner
**Primary record:** manager portfolio record
**Decision status:** Final Part 4 design constitution; implementation and production authority remain evidence-gated.

### Constitutional Purpose

Define manager agents that plan, delegate, monitor, integrate, coach through proposals and escalate without becoming domain or approval authorities.

This section is complete only when `manager portfolio record` is attributable, typed, policy-valid, resource-accounted, observable, recoverable and reviewable by Human Workforce Owner. The non-negotiable invariant is: Managers cannot grant permissions, hide worker evidence, optimize appearances, self-approve portfolios or transfer accountability to workers.

### Operating Contract

| Contract dimension | Normative requirement |
|---|---|
| Business outcome | Define manager agents that plan, delegate, monitor, integrate, coach through proposals and escalate without becoming domain or approval authorities. |
| Human accountability | Human Workforce Owner |
| Authoritative artifact | manager portfolio record |
| Required inputs | authenticated charter; current workforce management state; policy and authority snapshot; owned evidence; deadline; budget; acceptance criteria; human accountability route |
| Required outputs | versioned manager portfolio record; decision evidence; state transition; exceptions; resource account; terminal receipt |
| Constitutional invariant | Managers cannot grant permissions, hide worker evidence, optimize appearances, self-approve portfolios or transfer accountability to workers. |
| Default authority | A0/A1 advice and preparation unless an exact role card, policy, certification and effect-specific grant narrow a higher ceiling. |
| Default failure | Stop the smallest unsafe scope, preserve state and evidence, reconcile any attempted effect, and route the unresolved decision to the named owner. |
| Performance envelope | Declare separate SLOs for admission, queueing, decision, effect verification and evidence publication; 100 percent of terminal manager portfolio record records must be attributable and schema-valid. |
| Scale model | Partition workforce management work by tenant and bounded aggregate, preserve global contract compatibility, cap concurrency and fan-out, and fail closed when ownership or policy cannot converge. |
| Future direction | adaptive spans, manager evaluation, regional management cells and simulated workforce planning |

### End-to-End Constitutional Procedure

1. **Accept bounded portfolio.** Validate identity, scope, owner, policy, data, authority, budget and deadline; persist the decision and do not begin a dependent step until its preconditions and evidence pass.
2. **Verify worker eligibility.** Validate identity, scope, owner, policy, data, authority, budget and deadline; persist the decision and do not begin a dependent step until its preconditions and evidence pass.
3. **Decompose outcomes.** Validate identity, scope, owner, policy, data, authority, budget and deadline; persist the decision and do not begin a dependent step until its preconditions and evidence pass.
4. **Delegate narrowed tasks.** Validate identity, scope, owner, policy, data, authority, budget and deadline; persist the decision and do not begin a dependent step until its preconditions and evidence pass.
5. **Monitor receipts and health.** Validate identity, scope, owner, policy, data, authority, budget and deadline; persist the decision and do not begin a dependent step until its preconditions and evidence pass.
6. **Mediate routine conflicts.** Validate identity, scope, owner, policy, data, authority, budget and deadline; persist the decision and do not begin a dependent step until its preconditions and evidence pass.
7. **Integrate verified results.** Validate identity, scope, owner, policy, data, authority, budget and deadline; persist the decision and do not begin a dependent step until its preconditions and evidence pass.
8. **Escalate and report honestly.** Validate identity, scope, owner, policy, data, authority, budget and deadline; persist the decision and do not begin a dependent step until its preconditions and evidence pass.

### Required Decision Record

| Record component | Minimum fields | Independent check |
|---|---|---|
| Charter | outcome, non-goals, sponsor, owner, acceptance, deadline and expiry | mission and owner resolver |
| Identity | logical ID, immutable version, runtime principal, tenant, environment and operator | identity and lifecycle service |
| Evidence | sources, revisions, rights, freshness, transformations, contradictions and confidence | domain and provenance validator |
| Decision | facts, assumptions, alternatives, dissent, risk, cost, uncertainty and requested judgment | human or independent evaluator |
| Authority | role ceiling, task grant, policy, data purpose, approval and live revocation state | policy enforcement point |
| Execution | plan, resources, tools, state versions, checkpoints, attempts and effects | orchestrator and domain gateways |
| Outcome | typed status, acceptance, quality, business result, externalities, incidents and follow-up owner | task owner and Analytics |
| Audit | correlation, causation, digests, timestamps, receipts, retention and access history | independent Audit owner |

### Business Perspective

Agent Managers makes workforce management an accountable operating capability rather than a title, prompt persona or undocumented model behavior. Business owners receive alternatives, value, full cost, risk, uncertainty, rights impact, dependencies and evidence before accepting a consequential result.

The business must fund control work as part of delivery: attribution, human review, Security, recovery, audit and lifecycle are not optional overhead. Success is the durable outcome represented by `manager portfolio record`, not output volume or agent activity.

### Engineering Perspective

Implement agent managers through versioned schemas, deterministic state machines, owned ports, immutable identities, hierarchical budgets, cancellation, idempotency, checkpoints and source-of-truth verification. Probabilistic inference may propose; deterministic services authorize and commit.

Make time, randomness, provider routes, policy versions and external effects injectable in tests. Classify every dependency as startup-hard, runtime-required, optional or asynchronous; define timeout, circuit, fallback, replay, migration and failure ownership explicitly.

### Architecture Perspective

Human Workforce Owner remains the human accountability boundary. The Workforce Management domain owns semantics and canonical state; CATA coordinates portfolios, Supervisor coordinates runtime, specialists produce bounded artifacts, and policy/effect gateways prevent orchestration from becoming authority.

Commands request owned work, queries read without hidden mutation, events report committed facts, approvals authorize exact effects, notifications inform and receipts prove attempts. Projections and caches are rebuildable and never promoted to source of truth by convenience.

### AI Coding Perspective

Before changing implementation for section `75`, load `context/05_AGENTS.md`, `context/00_PROJECT_CONTEXT.md`, inspect current schemas and ownership, and identify the exact deterministic guard. An AI coding agent must not infer implementation permission from this final documentation status, an empty directory, a draft ADR or a provider feature.

Write negative tests first for mission drift, forged identity, cross-tenant data, stale context, permission expansion, approval substitution, prompt injection, duplicate effect, cancellation, evidence loss and migration incompatibility. Keep changes minimal, preserve user work and report unresolved assumptions.

### Human Perspective

Humans see who the agent is, why it is acting, who owns the task, what evidence it used, what it knows and does not know, what decision is requested, what alternatives exist, what it costs, and what happens on approval, denial or delay. Human Workforce Owner can stop or narrow work without navigating hidden agent conversations.

Interfaces must avoid automation bias, anthropomorphic pressure and approval fatigue. They provide accessible evidence, dissent, uncertainty, scope, expiry, consequences, revision, denial, escalation and recovery controls. Human silence is never consent or approval.

### Security Perspective

Apply zero standing privilege, workload identity, tenant and environment isolation, purpose-bound data, secret-manager references, prompt and tool injection defenses, egress policy, sandboxing, rate limits, revocation, tamper-evident receipts and a tested kill switch. Section invariant: Managers cannot grant permissions, hide worker evidence, optimize appearances, self-approve portfolios or transfer accountability to workers.

Threat tests cover confused deputy, role-title escalation, malicious context, poisoned knowledge, memory exfiltration, approval laundering, replay, supply-chain substitution, side channels, resource exhaustion, audit tampering and compromised provider behavior.

### Performance Perspective

Declare separate SLOs for admission, queueing, decision, effect verification and evidence publication; 100 percent of terminal manager portfolio record records must be attributable and schema-valid.

Measure queue, policy, context, model, tool, approval, effect verification, recovery and evidence latency separately. Report percentiles, quality, safety, cost, human burden, cancellation delay and terminal classes; never improve averages by dropping rejected, failed or quarantined work.

### Scalability Perspective

Partition workforce management work by tenant and bounded aggregate, preserve global contract compatibility, cap concurrency and fan-out, and fail closed when ownership or policy cannot converge.

Use bounded fan-out, backpressure, fairness reservations, locality and asynchronous facts where ordering is unnecessary. Cross-region or cross-node scale requires explicit data residency, identity federation, protocol compatibility, conflict resolution, disconnect behavior and reconciliation.

### Future Evolution

Future evolution may include adaptive spans, manager evaluation, regional management cells and simulated workforce planning. Every increment begins as a hypothesis, runs in simulation or sandbox, proves quality and safety, obtains independent human authorization, canaries immutable versions and retains rollback, migration and historical interpretation.

Future capability never retroactively authorizes current behavior. Rights, law, accountability, tenant choice, evidence, Security and safe exit remain constraints even when technology, organization, providers or economic models change.

### Implementation Contract

- [ ] Define canonical schema, owner, compatibility policy and stable error taxonomy.
- [ ] Encode identity, policy, permission, approval, limits and isolation outside the model.
- [ ] Map each AI capability to an owned port, data class, effect class and receipt.
- [ ] Implement state transitions with optimistic concurrency and durable checkpoints.
- [ ] Propagate correlation, causation, deadline, cancellation and budget through every call.
- [ ] Verify external effects from authoritative state before completion or retry.
- [ ] Provide degraded behavior, circuit breaking, containment, recovery and reconciliation.
- [ ] Redact operational logs and retain protected forensic evidence by explicit policy.
- [ ] Create role-quality, adversarial, tenancy, load, chaos, migration and rollback tests.
- [ ] Ship dashboards, alert thresholds, runbooks, on-call ownership and support boundaries.
- [ ] Canary an immutable version and retain a tested last-known-safe rollback target.
- [ ] Require independent owner acceptance and applicable certification before production.

### ADR References

- Candidate implementation decision record: `adr/ADR-0048.md`. It is a Draft placeholder until completed and accepted; the filename grants no authority.
- A material ADR must record context, decision, alternatives, consequences, rights and security, data, economics, operability, compatibility, migration, rollback, tests, evidence and supersession scope.
- Where no accepted ADR exists, implementation must preserve the more restrictive current constitution and seek a human architecture decision.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
```

#### CAT-AG-P4-75-C01 — Charter Scope

- **Rule:** For agent managers, bind all work to a signed outcome, explicit non-goals, owner, expiry and acceptance criteria.
- **Business test:** `manager portfolio record` exposes the cost, benefit, risk, owner, uncertainty and consequence of this control to an accountable reviewer.
- **Engineering enforcement:** The boundary responsible for `accept bounded portfolio` validates this control before state change and again before any related material effect.
- **AI behavior:** Missing, stale, contradictory, denied or unverifiable control data causes a typed stop, wait, refusal or escalation; the model never fills the gap with confidence.
- **Human boundary:** Human Workforce Owner receives the exact requested decision and evidence when human judgment is required; no UI default or silence creates consent.
- **Security assertion:** Forged role, cross-tenant reference, replay, changed payload, expired grant, injected instruction and evidence tampering all fail closed and emit a protected signal.
- **Performance assertion:** Enforcement remains inside the declared SLO and resource reserve; overload applies backpressure rather than removing checks.
- **Evidence:** Store logical and runtime identity, tenant, versions, policy, grants, input/output digests, decision, state, timestamps, owner and redacted receipts.
- **Failure code:** `CAT_P4_75_01_CONSTITUTIONAL_CONTROL`; dependent work remains non-success and any attempted effect enters reconciliation.
- **Recovery:** Contain the affected scope, establish authoritative effect state, restore the invariant, obtain required human decision and link a terminal recovery receipt.
- **Implementation test:** Run positive, negative, boundary, cancellation, duplicate, stale-state, migration and compromised-dependency fixtures deterministically.
- **Ownership:** Human Workforce Owner owns residual business judgment; the Workforce Management service owner owns enforcement; Audit owns independent evidence review.
- **Constitutional assertion:** An independent reviewer can reproduce the `Charter Scope` disposition without trusting hidden reasoning, title, provider success or undocumented operator explanation.

### AI Memory Anchor

**Memory anchor `P4-75`:** `Agent Managers` is governed by `manager portfolio record` and owned in human accountability by Human Workforce Owner. Preserve: Managers cannot grant permissions, hide worker evidence, optimize appearances, self-approve portfolios or transfer accountability to workers. On conflict or uncertainty, stop the smallest unsafe scope, retain evidence and escalate; never infer authority from an executive title, confidence, group membership, budget or future ambition.

### Workforce Evolution Control Table

| Control area | Current constitutional requirement | Promotion evidence | Rollback trigger |
|---|---|---|---|
| Role definition | mission, owner, authority, interfaces and prohibitions | complete card and negative tests | scope drift or orphan owner |
| Training | isolated curriculum and clean datasets | sealed evaluation and red-team pass | contamination or unsafe behavior |
| Team membership | versioned charter and individual grants | collaboration and failure exercises | permission leakage or unresolved conflict |
| Management | bounded span and transparent delegation | low rework, complete evidence and fair allocation | metric gaming or hidden failure |
| Autonomy | time and effect-bounded grant | sustained quality, safety and recovery proof | incident, drift, missing receipt or policy change |
| Organization | named departments and independent controls | reduced coordination cost without control loss | circular reporting or self-approval |
| Federation | operator identity and compatible contracts | disconnect, reconciliation and residency tests | trust, legal or protocol incompatibility |
| Retirement | no owned work and revoked access | migration and evidence-retention proof | orphan state or active dependency |

## 76. Agent Supervisors

**Section ID:** `CAT-AG-P4-76`
**Constitutional domain:** Runtime Supervision
**Human accountable owner:** Human Operations Owner
**Primary record:** supervision case record
**Decision status:** Final Part 4 design constitution; implementation and production authority remain evidence-gated.

### Constitutional Purpose

Define supervisors as runtime safety and progress coordinators for state, ownership, cancellation, retries, failures and recovery.

This section is complete only when `supervision case record` is attributable, typed, policy-valid, resource-accounted, observable, recoverable and reviewable by Human Operations Owner. The non-negotiable invariant is: Supervisors cannot reinterpret business intent, approve effects, mutate domain truth or use supervised agents as confused deputies.

### Operating Contract

| Contract dimension | Normative requirement |
|---|---|
| Business outcome | Define supervisors as runtime safety and progress coordinators for state, ownership, cancellation, retries, failures and recovery. |
| Human accountability | Human Operations Owner |
| Authoritative artifact | supervision case record |
| Required inputs | authenticated charter; current runtime supervision state; policy and authority snapshot; owned evidence; deadline; budget; acceptance criteria; human accountability route |
| Required outputs | versioned supervision case record; decision evidence; state transition; exceptions; resource account; terminal receipt |
| Constitutional invariant | Supervisors cannot reinterpret business intent, approve effects, mutate domain truth or use supervised agents as confused deputies. |
| Default authority | A0/A1 advice and preparation unless an exact role card, policy, certification and effect-specific grant narrow a higher ceiling. |
| Default failure | Stop the smallest unsafe scope, preserve state and evidence, reconcile any attempted effect, and route the unresolved decision to the named owner. |
| Performance envelope | Declare separate SLOs for admission, queueing, decision, effect verification and evidence publication; 100 percent of terminal supervision case record records must be attributable and schema-valid. |
| Scale model | Partition runtime supervision work by tenant and bounded aggregate, preserve global contract compatibility, cap concurrency and fan-out, and fail closed when ownership or policy cannot converge. |
| Future direction | hierarchical supervision, predictive incident prevention and cross-region lease recovery |

### End-to-End Constitutional Procedure

1. **Observe admitted run state.** Validate identity, scope, owner, policy, data, authority, budget and deadline; persist the decision and do not begin a dependent step until its preconditions and evidence pass.
2. **Verify ownership and heartbeat.** Validate identity, scope, owner, policy, data, authority, budget and deadline; persist the decision and do not begin a dependent step until its preconditions and evidence pass.
3. **Enforce deadline and budget.** Validate identity, scope, owner, policy, data, authority, budget and deadline; persist the decision and do not begin a dependent step until its preconditions and evidence pass.
4. **Contain unhealthy execution.** Validate identity, scope, owner, policy, data, authority, budget and deadline; persist the decision and do not begin a dependent step until its preconditions and evidence pass.
5. **Classify blocked or failed work.** Validate identity, scope, owner, policy, data, authority, budget and deadline; persist the decision and do not begin a dependent step until its preconditions and evidence pass.
6. **Coordinate reconciliation.** Validate identity, scope, owner, policy, data, authority, budget and deadline; persist the decision and do not begin a dependent step until its preconditions and evidence pass.
7. **Request human or domain decision.** Validate identity, scope, owner, policy, data, authority, budget and deadline; persist the decision and do not begin a dependent step until its preconditions and evidence pass.
8. **Verify terminal evidence.** Validate identity, scope, owner, policy, data, authority, budget and deadline; persist the decision and do not begin a dependent step until its preconditions and evidence pass.

### Required Decision Record

| Record component | Minimum fields | Independent check |
|---|---|---|
| Charter | outcome, non-goals, sponsor, owner, acceptance, deadline and expiry | mission and owner resolver |
| Identity | logical ID, immutable version, runtime principal, tenant, environment and operator | identity and lifecycle service |
| Evidence | sources, revisions, rights, freshness, transformations, contradictions and confidence | domain and provenance validator |
| Decision | facts, assumptions, alternatives, dissent, risk, cost, uncertainty and requested judgment | human or independent evaluator |
| Authority | role ceiling, task grant, policy, data purpose, approval and live revocation state | policy enforcement point |
| Execution | plan, resources, tools, state versions, checkpoints, attempts and effects | orchestrator and domain gateways |
| Outcome | typed status, acceptance, quality, business result, externalities, incidents and follow-up owner | task owner and Analytics |
| Audit | correlation, causation, digests, timestamps, receipts, retention and access history | independent Audit owner |

### Business Perspective

Agent Supervisors makes runtime supervision an accountable operating capability rather than a title, prompt persona or undocumented model behavior. Business owners receive alternatives, value, full cost, risk, uncertainty, rights impact, dependencies and evidence before accepting a consequential result.

The business must fund control work as part of delivery: attribution, human review, Security, recovery, audit and lifecycle are not optional overhead. Success is the durable outcome represented by `supervision case record`, not output volume or agent activity.

### Engineering Perspective

Implement agent supervisors through versioned schemas, deterministic state machines, owned ports, immutable identities, hierarchical budgets, cancellation, idempotency, checkpoints and source-of-truth verification. Probabilistic inference may propose; deterministic services authorize and commit.

Make time, randomness, provider routes, policy versions and external effects injectable in tests. Classify every dependency as startup-hard, runtime-required, optional or asynchronous; define timeout, circuit, fallback, replay, migration and failure ownership explicitly.

### Architecture Perspective

Human Operations Owner remains the human accountability boundary. The Runtime Supervision domain owns semantics and canonical state; CATA coordinates portfolios, Supervisor coordinates runtime, specialists produce bounded artifacts, and policy/effect gateways prevent orchestration from becoming authority.

Commands request owned work, queries read without hidden mutation, events report committed facts, approvals authorize exact effects, notifications inform and receipts prove attempts. Projections and caches are rebuildable and never promoted to source of truth by convenience.

### AI Coding Perspective

Before changing implementation for section `76`, load `context/05_AGENTS.md`, `context/04_ARCHITECTURE.md`, `context/16_DEPLOYMENT.md`, inspect current schemas and ownership, and identify the exact deterministic guard. An AI coding agent must not infer implementation permission from this final documentation status, an empty directory, a draft ADR or a provider feature.

Write negative tests first for mission drift, forged identity, cross-tenant data, stale context, permission expansion, approval substitution, prompt injection, duplicate effect, cancellation, evidence loss and migration incompatibility. Keep changes minimal, preserve user work and report unresolved assumptions.

### Human Perspective

Humans see who the agent is, why it is acting, who owns the task, what evidence it used, what it knows and does not know, what decision is requested, what alternatives exist, what it costs, and what happens on approval, denial or delay. Human Operations Owner can stop or narrow work without navigating hidden agent conversations.

Interfaces must avoid automation bias, anthropomorphic pressure and approval fatigue. They provide accessible evidence, dissent, uncertainty, scope, expiry, consequences, revision, denial, escalation and recovery controls. Human silence is never consent or approval.

### Security Perspective

Apply zero standing privilege, workload identity, tenant and environment isolation, purpose-bound data, secret-manager references, prompt and tool injection defenses, egress policy, sandboxing, rate limits, revocation, tamper-evident receipts and a tested kill switch. Section invariant: Supervisors cannot reinterpret business intent, approve effects, mutate domain truth or use supervised agents as confused deputies.

Threat tests cover confused deputy, role-title escalation, malicious context, poisoned knowledge, memory exfiltration, approval laundering, replay, supply-chain substitution, side channels, resource exhaustion, audit tampering and compromised provider behavior.

### Performance Perspective

Declare separate SLOs for admission, queueing, decision, effect verification and evidence publication; 100 percent of terminal supervision case record records must be attributable and schema-valid.

Measure queue, policy, context, model, tool, approval, effect verification, recovery and evidence latency separately. Report percentiles, quality, safety, cost, human burden, cancellation delay and terminal classes; never improve averages by dropping rejected, failed or quarantined work.

### Scalability Perspective

Partition runtime supervision work by tenant and bounded aggregate, preserve global contract compatibility, cap concurrency and fan-out, and fail closed when ownership or policy cannot converge.

Use bounded fan-out, backpressure, fairness reservations, locality and asynchronous facts where ordering is unnecessary. Cross-region or cross-node scale requires explicit data residency, identity federation, protocol compatibility, conflict resolution, disconnect behavior and reconciliation.

### Future Evolution

Future evolution may include hierarchical supervision, predictive incident prevention and cross-region lease recovery. Every increment begins as a hypothesis, runs in simulation or sandbox, proves quality and safety, obtains independent human authorization, canaries immutable versions and retains rollback, migration and historical interpretation.

Future capability never retroactively authorizes current behavior. Rights, law, accountability, tenant choice, evidence, Security and safe exit remain constraints even when technology, organization, providers or economic models change.

### Implementation Contract

- [ ] Define canonical schema, owner, compatibility policy and stable error taxonomy.
- [ ] Encode identity, policy, permission, approval, limits and isolation outside the model.
- [ ] Map each AI capability to an owned port, data class, effect class and receipt.
- [ ] Implement state transitions with optimistic concurrency and durable checkpoints.
- [ ] Propagate correlation, causation, deadline, cancellation and budget through every call.
- [ ] Verify external effects from authoritative state before completion or retry.
- [ ] Provide degraded behavior, circuit breaking, containment, recovery and reconciliation.
- [ ] Redact operational logs and retain protected forensic evidence by explicit policy.
- [ ] Create role-quality, adversarial, tenancy, load, chaos, migration and rollback tests.
- [ ] Ship dashboards, alert thresholds, runbooks, on-call ownership and support boundaries.
- [ ] Canary an immutable version and retain a tested last-known-safe rollback target.
- [ ] Require independent owner acceptance and applicable certification before production.

### ADR References

- Candidate implementation decision record: `adr/ADR-0049.md`. It is a Draft placeholder until completed and accepted; the filename grants no authority.
- A material ADR must record context, decision, alternatives, consequences, rights and security, data, economics, operability, compatibility, migration, rollback, tests, evidence and supersession scope.
- Where no accepted ADR exists, implementation must preserve the more restrictive current constitution and seek a human architecture decision.

- Constitutional baseline: `context/00_PROJECT_CONTEXT.md`, `context/01_PROJECT_OVERVIEW.md`, `context/02_PROJECT_RULES.md`, `context/03_TECH_STACK.md`, `context/04_ARCHITECTURE.md`, and `context/05_AGENTS.md`.
