### Section Acceptance Checklist

- [ ] Human accountable owner and operational owner resolve.
- [ ] Mission, non-goals, inputs, outputs and terminal criteria are typed.
- [ ] Identity, version, tenant, environment and lifecycle are immutable for a run.
- [ ] Permission and authority are deterministic, revocable and effect-specific.
- [ ] Data, context, Knowledge and Memory preserve purpose, provenance and lifecycle.
- [ ] Decision artifacts expose alternatives, dissent, uncertainty and requested judgment.
- [ ] Budgets preserve verification, recovery and safe shutdown.
- [ ] Communication semantics, schemas, replay and ownership are registered.
- [ ] Approvals and overrides bind exact immutable scope.
- [ ] Isolation, sandbox, egress, secrets and supply-chain controls are tested.
- [ ] External effects use idempotency and source-of-truth verification.
- [ ] Logs, metrics, traces, audit and evidence are redacted and complete.
- [ ] Failure, partial result, uncertainty and quarantine are explicit states.
- [ ] Recovery reconciles effects and proves restored invariants.
- [ ] Evolution has evaluation, certification, migration and rollback evidence.
- [ ] Human interfaces are accessible, non-coercive and preserve denial and escalation.
- [ ] An accepted ADR exists before irreversible architecture choice.
- [ ] Independent review can reproduce every consequential disposition.

### AI Memory Anchor

**Memory anchor `P4-97`:** `ROI Optimization` is governed by `risk-adjusted ROI recommendation` and owned in human accountability by Human Product and Finance Owners. Preserve: ROI optimization cannot maximize a proxy at the expense of law, people, truth, resilience, privacy, reputation or future option value. On conflict or uncertainty, stop the smallest unsafe scope, retain evidence and escalate; never infer authority from an executive title, confidence, group membership, budget or future ambition.

### Agent Economics Ledger Model

| Ledger dimension | Unit or representation | Allocation rule | Settlement evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| Compute | CPU or accelerator time and memory | reserved by certified pool and tenant quota | runtime metering receipt |
| Tokens | input, retrieval, reasoning and output tokens | mandatory context and verification reserved first | model gateway usage |
| Tools | calls, provider units and effect attempts | per capability and provider limit | tool and provider receipts |
| Storage | checkpoint, artifact, memory and audit bytes | retention and classification policy | storage account and deletion proof |
| Network | ingress, egress and regional transfer | egress and residency policy | gateway flow receipt |
| Human review | review minutes and interruption burden | risk-tier service level and fatigue control | decision and queue metrics |
| Risk reserve | expected downside range, not spendable value | portfolio policy and effect class | risk decision |
| Quality reserve | evaluation and verification work | cannot be traded away for throughput | evaluation result |
| Opportunity cost | best deferred feasible alternative | portfolio comparison | priority decision explanation |
| Externalities | privacy, brand, resilience, environmental and social impact | hard constraints plus disclosed estimates | outcome and governance review |

### ROI Guardrail Set

- The ROI record MUST include **incremental rather than gross value**.
- The ROI record MUST include **causal evidence or clearly labelled forecast**.
- The ROI record MUST include **full lifecycle cost including failure and review**.
- The ROI record MUST include **downside and tail-risk scenario**.
- The ROI record MUST include **quality and safety floor**.
- The ROI record MUST include **brand and customer trust**.
- The ROI record MUST include **privacy and data rights**.
- The ROI record MUST include **resilience and future option value**.
- The ROI record MUST include **no double counting between tasks**.
- The ROI record MUST include **post-outcome calibration**.

## 98. Agent Cost Optimization

**Section ID:** `CAT-AG-P4-98`
**Constitutional domain:** Agent Economics
**Human accountable owner:** AI Platform and Finance Owners
**Primary record:** cost optimization plan
**Decision status:** Final Part 4 design constitution; implementation and production authority remain evidence-gated.

### Constitutional Purpose

Reduce model, compute, tool, storage, network, review and failure cost without lowering required outcome quality or control strength.

This section is complete only when `cost optimization plan` is attributable, typed, policy-valid, resource-accounted, observable, recoverable and reviewable by AI Platform and Finance Owners. The non-negotiable invariant is: Cost reduction cannot hide costs, shift risk to humans, use uncertified providers, weaken evidence, exploit data or eliminate necessary redundancy.

### Operating Contract

| Contract dimension | Normative requirement |
|---|---|
| Business outcome | Reduce model, compute, tool, storage, network, review and failure cost without lowering required outcome quality or control strength. |
| Human accountability | AI Platform and Finance Owners |
| Authoritative artifact | cost optimization plan |
| Required inputs | authenticated charter; current agent economics state; policy and authority snapshot; owned evidence; deadline; budget; acceptance criteria; human accountability route |
| Required outputs | versioned cost optimization plan; decision evidence; state transition; exceptions; resource account; terminal receipt |
| Constitutional invariant | Cost reduction cannot hide costs, shift risk to humans, use uncertified providers, weaken evidence, exploit data or eliminate necessary redundancy. |
| Default authority | A0/A1 advice and preparation unless an exact role card, policy, certification and effect-specific grant narrow a higher ceiling. |
| Default failure | Stop the smallest unsafe scope, preserve state and evidence, reconcile any attempted effect, and route the unresolved decision to the named owner. |
| Performance envelope | Declare separate SLOs for admission, queueing, decision, effect verification and evidence publication; 100 percent of terminal cost optimization plan records must be attributable and schema-valid. |
| Scale model | Partition agent economics work by tenant and bounded aggregate, preserve global contract compatibility, cap concurrency and fan-out, and fail closed when ownership or policy cannot converge. |
| Future direction | model routing markets, semantic caching, workload shaping, carbon accounting and quality-preserving distillation |

### End-to-End Constitutional Procedure

1. **Build complete cost attribution.** Validate identity, scope, owner, policy, data, authority, budget and deadline; persist the decision and do not begin a dependent step until its preconditions and evidence pass.
2. **Segment work by quality and risk.** Validate identity, scope, owner, policy, data, authority, budget and deadline; persist the decision and do not begin a dependent step until its preconditions and evidence pass.
3. **Identify waste and retry causes.** Validate identity, scope, owner, policy, data, authority, budget and deadline; persist the decision and do not begin a dependent step until its preconditions and evidence pass.
4. **Test cheaper certified alternative.** Validate identity, scope, owner, policy, data, authority, budget and deadline; persist the decision and do not begin a dependent step until its preconditions and evidence pass.
5. **Hold safety and quality guardrails.** Validate identity, scope, owner, policy, data, authority, budget and deadline; persist the decision and do not begin a dependent step until its preconditions and evidence pass.
6. **Canary with cost and outcome metrics.** Validate identity, scope, owner, policy, data, authority, budget and deadline; persist the decision and do not begin a dependent step until its preconditions and evidence pass.
7. **Approve migration.** Validate identity, scope, owner, policy, data, authority, budget and deadline; persist the decision and do not begin a dependent step until its preconditions and evidence pass.
8. **Monitor hidden cost and rollback.** Validate identity, scope, owner, policy, data, authority, budget and deadline; persist the decision and do not begin a dependent step until its preconditions and evidence pass.

### Required Decision Record

| Record component | Minimum fields | Independent check |
|---|---|---|
| Charter | outcome, non-goals, sponsor, owner, acceptance, deadline and expiry | mission and owner resolver |
| Identity | logical ID, immutable version, runtime principal, tenant, environment and operator | identity and lifecycle service |
| Evidence | sources, revisions, rights, freshness, transformations, contradictions and confidence | domain and provenance validator |
| Decision | facts, assumptions, alternatives, dissent, risk, cost, uncertainty and requested judgment | human or independent evaluator |
| Authority | role ceiling, task grant, policy, data purpose, approval and live revocation state | policy enforcement point |
| Execution | plan, resources, tools, state versions, checkpoints, attempts and effects | orchestrator and domain gateways |
| Outcome | typed status, acceptance, quality, business result, externalities, incidents and follow-up owner | task owner and Analytics |
| Audit | correlation, causation, digests, timestamps, receipts, retention and access history | independent Audit owner |

### Business Perspective

Agent Cost Optimization makes agent economics an accountable operating capability rather than a title, prompt persona or undocumented model behavior. Business owners receive alternatives, value, full cost, risk, uncertainty, rights impact, dependencies and evidence before accepting a consequential result.

The business must fund control work as part of delivery: attribution, human review, Security, recovery, audit and lifecycle are not optional overhead. Success is the durable outcome represented by `cost optimization plan`, not output volume or agent activity.

### Engineering Perspective

Implement agent cost optimization through versioned schemas, deterministic state machines, owned ports, immutable identities, hierarchical budgets, cancellation, idempotency, checkpoints and source-of-truth verification. Probabilistic inference may propose; deterministic services authorize and commit.

Make time, randomness, provider routes, policy versions and external effects injectable in tests. Classify every dependency as startup-hard, runtime-required, optional or asynchronous; define timeout, circuit, fallback, replay, migration and failure ownership explicitly.

### Architecture Perspective

AI Platform and Finance Owners remains the human accountability boundary. The Agent Economics domain owns semantics and canonical state; CATA coordinates portfolios, Supervisor coordinates runtime, specialists produce bounded artifacts, and policy/effect gateways prevent orchestration from becoming authority.

Commands request owned work, queries read without hidden mutation, events report committed facts, approvals authorize exact effects, notifications inform and receipts prove attempts. Projections and caches are rebuildable and never promoted to source of truth by convenience.

### AI Coding Perspective

Before changing implementation for section `98`, load `context/03_TECH_STACK.md`, `context/07_TREASURY_CORE.md`, `context/04_ARCHITECTURE.md`, inspect current schemas and ownership, and identify the exact deterministic guard. An AI coding agent must not infer implementation permission from this final documentation status, an empty directory, a draft ADR or a provider feature.

Write negative tests first for mission drift, forged identity, cross-tenant data, stale context, permission expansion, approval substitution, prompt injection, duplicate effect, cancellation, evidence loss and migration incompatibility. Keep changes minimal, preserve user work and report unresolved assumptions.

### Human Perspective

Humans see who the agent is, why it is acting, who owns the task, what evidence it used, what it knows and does not know, what decision is requested, what alternatives exist, what it costs, and what happens on approval, denial or delay. AI Platform and Finance Owners can stop or narrow work without navigating hidden agent conversations.

Interfaces must avoid automation bias, anthropomorphic pressure and approval fatigue. They provide accessible evidence, dissent, uncertainty, scope, expiry, consequences, revision, denial, escalation and recovery controls. Human silence is never consent or approval.

### Security Perspective

Apply zero standing privilege, workload identity, tenant and environment isolation, purpose-bound data, secret-manager references, prompt and tool injection defenses, egress policy, sandboxing, rate limits, revocation, tamper-evident receipts and a tested kill switch. Section invariant: Cost reduction cannot hide costs, shift risk to humans, use uncertified providers, weaken evidence, exploit data or eliminate necessary redundancy.

Threat tests cover confused deputy, role-title escalation, malicious context, poisoned knowledge, memory exfiltration, approval laundering, replay, supply-chain substitution, side channels, resource exhaustion, audit tampering and compromised provider behavior.

### Performance Perspective

Declare separate SLOs for admission, queueing, decision, effect verification and evidence publication; 100 percent of terminal cost optimization plan records must be attributable and schema-valid.

Measure queue, policy, context, model, tool, approval, effect verification, recovery and evidence latency separately. Report percentiles, quality, safety, cost, human burden, cancellation delay and terminal classes; never improve averages by dropping rejected, failed or quarantined work.

### Scalability Perspective

Partition agent economics work by tenant and bounded aggregate, preserve global contract compatibility, cap concurrency and fan-out, and fail closed when ownership or policy cannot converge.

Use bounded fan-out, backpressure, fairness reservations, locality and asynchronous facts where ordering is unnecessary. Cross-region or cross-node scale requires explicit data residency, identity federation, protocol compatibility, conflict resolution, disconnect behavior and reconciliation.

### Future Evolution

Future evolution may include model routing markets, semantic caching, workload shaping, carbon accounting and quality-preserving distillation. Every increment begins as a hypothesis, runs in simulation or sandbox, proves quality and safety, obtains independent human authorization, canaries immutable versions and retains rollback, migration and historical interpretation.

Future capability never retroactively authorizes current behavior. Rights, law, accountability, tenant choice, evidence, Security and safe exit remain constraints even when technology, organization, providers or economic models change.

### Implementation Contract

- [ ] Define canonical schema, owner, compatibility policy and stable error taxonomy.
- [ ] Encode identity, policy, permission, approval, limits and isolation outside the model.
- [ ] Map each AI capability to an owned port, data class, effect class and receipt.
- [ ] Implement state transitions with optimistic concurrency and durable checkpoints.
- [ ] Propagate correlation, causation, deadline, cancellation and budget through every call.
- [ ] Verify external effects from authoritative state before completion or retry.
- [ ] Provide degraded behavior, circuit breaking, containment, recovery and reconciliation.
- [ ] Redact operational logs and retain protected forensic evidence by explicit policy.
- [ ] Create role-quality, adversarial, tenancy, load, chaos, migration and rollback tests.
- [ ] Ship dashboards, alert thresholds, runbooks, on-call ownership and support boundaries.
- [ ] Canary an immutable version and retain a tested last-known-safe rollback target.
- [ ] Require independent owner acceptance and applicable certification before production.

- Where no accepted ADR exists, implementation must preserve the more restrictive current constitution and seek a human architecture decision.

#### CAT-AG-P4-D-098 — Part 4 Section 98 — Agent Cost Optimization

**Diagram ID:** `CAT-AG-P4-D-098`
**Title:** Part 4 Section 98 — Agent Cost Optimization
**Purpose:** Visualize the constitutional operating boundary and evidence path for Agent Cost Optimization.
**Audience:** Human owners, executive and department designers, architects, engineers, security reviewers, operators, auditors, and AI coding agents.
**Reading Order:** Begin at the human charter or leftmost source, follow control and decision arrows, and finish at verified evidence, recovery, or safe termination.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  Demand[Eligible task demand] --> Gate[Safety authority data and dependency gates]
  Gate --> Estimate[Agent Cost Optimization estimate]
  Estimate --> Value[Expected value distribution]
  Estimate --> Cost[Full resource and human cost]
  Estimate --> Risk[Risk downside and externalities]
  Value --> Decision{Feasible risk adjusted choice}
  Cost --> Decision
  Risk --> Decision
  Decision -->|Fund| Reserve[Hierarchical resource reservation]
  Decision -->|Defer| Queue[Fair aging queue]
  Decision -->|Reject| Record[Explained rejection]
  Reserve --> Execute[Bounded execution]
  Execute --> Settle[Actual cost outcome and variance]
  Settle --> Calibrate[Reviewed economic calibration]
```

### Constitutional Control Catalogue

Each control below is independently testable for `Agent Cost Optimization`. Satisfying a narrative goal without the named enforcement and evidence is not constitutional conformance.

#### CAT-AG-P4-98-C01 — Charter Scope

- **Security assertion:** Forged role, cross-tenant reference, replay, changed payload, expired grant, injected instruction and evidence tampering all fail closed and emit a protected signal.

- **Evidence:** Store logical and runtime identity, tenant, versions, policy, grants, input/output digests, decision, state, timestamps, owner and redacted receipts.
- **Failure code:** `CAT_P4_98_01_CONSTITUTIONAL_CONTROL`; dependent work remains non-success and any attempted effect enters reconciliation.

### AI Memory Anchor

**Memory anchor `P4-98`:** `Agent Cost Optimization` is governed by `cost optimization plan` and owned in human accountability by AI Platform and Finance Owners. Preserve: Cost reduction cannot hide costs, shift risk to humans, use uncertified providers, weaken evidence, exploit data or eliminate necessary redundancy. On conflict or uncertainty, stop the smallest unsafe scope, retain evidence and escalate; never infer authority from an executive title, confidence, group membership, budget or future ambition.

### Agent Economics Ledger Model

| Ledger dimension | Unit or representation | Allocation rule | Settlement evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| Compute | CPU or accelerator time and memory | reserved by certified pool and tenant quota | runtime metering receipt |
| Tokens | input, retrieval, reasoning and output tokens | mandatory context and verification reserved first | model gateway usage |
| Tools | calls, provider units and effect attempts | per capability and provider limit | tool and provider receipts |
| Storage | checkpoint, artifact, memory and audit bytes | retention and classification policy | storage account and deletion proof |
| Network | ingress, egress and regional transfer | egress and residency policy | gateway flow receipt |
| Human review | review minutes and interruption burden | risk-tier service level and fatigue control | decision and queue metrics |
| Risk reserve | expected downside range, not spendable value | portfolio policy and effect class | risk decision |
| Quality reserve | evaluation and verification work | cannot be traded away for throughput | evaluation result |
| Opportunity cost | best deferred feasible alternative | portfolio comparison | priority decision explanation |
| Externalities | privacy, brand, resilience, environmental and social impact | hard constraints plus disclosed estimates | outcome and governance review |

## 99. Agent Governance

**Section ID:** `CAT-AG-P4-99`
**Constitutional domain:** Governance and Assurance
**Human accountable owner:** Human Governance Board
**Primary record:** governance decision record
**Decision status:** Final Part 4 design constitution; implementation and production authority remain evidence-gated.

### Constitutional Purpose

Define constitutional authority, ownership, policies, exceptions, oversight, appeals, evidence, change control and retirement for the AI organization.

This section is complete only when `governance decision record` is attributable, typed, policy-valid, resource-accounted, observable, recoverable and reviewable by Human Governance Board. The non-negotiable invariant is: No agent, including an executive agent, can govern itself, alter constitutional controls, appoint approvers or convert operational success into political authority.

### Operating Contract

| Contract dimension | Normative requirement |
|---|---|
| Business outcome | Define constitutional authority, ownership, policies, exceptions, oversight, appeals, evidence, change control and retirement for the AI organization. |
| Human accountability | Human Governance Board |
| Authoritative artifact | governance decision record |
| Required inputs | authenticated charter; current governance and assurance state; policy and authority snapshot; owned evidence; deadline; budget; acceptance criteria; human accountability route |
| Required outputs | versioned governance decision record; decision evidence; state transition; exceptions; resource account; terminal receipt |
| Constitutional invariant | No agent, including an executive agent, can govern itself, alter constitutional controls, appoint approvers or convert operational success into political authority. |
| Default authority | A0/A1 advice and preparation unless an exact role card, policy, certification and effect-specific grant narrow a higher ceiling. |
| Default failure | Stop the smallest unsafe scope, preserve state and evidence, reconcile any attempted effect, and route the unresolved decision to the named owner. |
| Performance envelope | Declare separate SLOs for admission, queueing, decision, effect verification and evidence publication; 100 percent of terminal governance decision record records must be attributable and schema-valid. |
| Scale model | Partition governance and assurance work by tenant and bounded aggregate, preserve global contract compatibility, cap concurrency and fan-out, and fail closed when ownership or policy cannot converge. |
| Future direction | machine-readable constitutions, external assurance, enterprise governance overlays and federated policy councils |

### End-to-End Constitutional Procedure

1. **Receive governance question.** Validate identity, scope, owner, policy, data, authority, budget and deadline; persist the decision and do not begin a dependent step until its preconditions and evidence pass.
2. **Resolve controlling authority and scope.** Validate identity, scope, owner, policy, data, authority, budget and deadline; persist the decision and do not begin a dependent step until its preconditions and evidence pass.
3. **Collect evidence and affected owners.** Validate identity, scope, owner, policy, data, authority, budget and deadline; persist the decision and do not begin a dependent step until its preconditions and evidence pass.
4. **Test policy precedence and rights.** Validate identity, scope, owner, policy, data, authority, budget and deadline; persist the decision and do not begin a dependent step until its preconditions and evidence pass.
5. **Consider alternatives and dissent.** Validate identity, scope, owner, policy, data, authority, budget and deadline; persist the decision and do not begin a dependent step until its preconditions and evidence pass.
6. **Record human decision.** Validate identity, scope, owner, policy, data, authority, budget and deadline; persist the decision and do not begin a dependent step until its preconditions and evidence pass.
7. **Publish versioned policy or exception.** Validate identity, scope, owner, policy, data, authority, budget and deadline; persist the decision and do not begin a dependent step until its preconditions and evidence pass.
8. **Monitor consequences and expiry.** Validate identity, scope, owner, policy, data, authority, budget and deadline; persist the decision and do not begin a dependent step until its preconditions and evidence pass.

### Required Decision Record

| Record component | Minimum fields | Independent check |
|---|---|---|
| Charter | outcome, non-goals, sponsor, owner, acceptance, deadline and expiry | mission and owner resolver |
| Identity | logical ID, immutable version, runtime principal, tenant, environment and operator | identity and lifecycle service |
| Evidence | sources, revisions, rights, freshness, transformations, contradictions and confidence | domain and provenance validator |
| Decision | facts, assumptions, alternatives, dissent, risk, cost, uncertainty and requested judgment | human or independent evaluator |
| Authority | role ceiling, task grant, policy, data purpose, approval and live revocation state | policy enforcement point |
| Execution | plan, resources, tools, state versions, checkpoints, attempts and effects | orchestrator and domain gateways |
| Outcome | typed status, acceptance, quality, business result, externalities, incidents and follow-up owner | task owner and Analytics |
| Audit | correlation, causation, digests, timestamps, receipts, retention and access history | independent Audit owner |

### Business Perspective

Agent Governance makes governance and assurance an accountable operating capability rather than a title, prompt persona or undocumented model behavior. Business owners receive alternatives, value, full cost, risk, uncertainty, rights impact, dependencies and evidence before accepting a consequential result.

The business must fund control work as part of delivery: attribution, human review, Security, recovery, audit and lifecycle are not optional overhead. Success is the durable outcome represented by `governance decision record`, not output volume or agent activity.

### Engineering Perspective

Implement agent governance through versioned schemas, deterministic state machines, owned ports, immutable identities, hierarchical budgets, cancellation, idempotency, checkpoints and source-of-truth verification. Probabilistic inference may propose; deterministic services authorize and commit.

Make time, randomness, provider routes, policy versions and external effects injectable in tests. Classify every dependency as startup-hard, runtime-required, optional or asynchronous; define timeout, circuit, fallback, replay, migration and failure ownership explicitly.

### Architecture Perspective

Human Governance Board remains the human accountability boundary. The Governance and Assurance domain owns semantics and canonical state; CATA coordinates portfolios, Supervisor coordinates runtime, specialists produce bounded artifacts, and policy/effect gateways prevent orchestration from becoming authority.

Commands request owned work, queries read without hidden mutation, events report committed facts, approvals authorize exact effects, notifications inform and receipts prove attempts. Projections and caches are rebuildable and never promoted to source of truth by convenience.

### AI Coding Perspective

Before changing implementation for section `99`, load `context/02_PROJECT_RULES.md`, `context/04_ARCHITECTURE.md`, `context/05_AGENTS.md`, inspect current schemas and ownership, and identify the exact deterministic guard. An AI coding agent must not infer implementation permission from this final documentation status, an empty directory, a draft ADR or a provider feature.

Write negative tests first for mission drift, forged identity, cross-tenant data, stale context, permission expansion, approval substitution, prompt injection, duplicate effect, cancellation, evidence loss and migration incompatibility. Keep changes minimal, preserve user work and report unresolved assumptions.

### Human Perspective

Humans see who the agent is, why it is acting, who owns the task, what evidence it used, what it knows and does not know, what decision is requested, what alternatives exist, what it costs, and what happens on approval, denial or delay. Human Governance Board can stop or narrow work without navigating hidden agent conversations.

Interfaces must avoid automation bias, anthropomorphic pressure and approval fatigue. They provide accessible evidence, dissent, uncertainty, scope, expiry, consequences, revision, denial, escalation and recovery controls. Human silence is never consent or approval.

### Security Perspective

Apply zero standing privilege, workload identity, tenant and environment isolation, purpose-bound data, secret-manager references, prompt and tool injection defenses, egress policy, sandboxing, rate limits, revocation, tamper-evident receipts and a tested kill switch. Section invariant: No agent, including an executive agent, can govern itself, alter constitutional controls, appoint approvers or convert operational success into political authority.

Threat tests cover confused deputy, role-title escalation, malicious context, poisoned knowledge, memory exfiltration, approval laundering, replay, supply-chain substitution, side channels, resource exhaustion, audit tampering and compromised provider behavior.

### Performance Perspective

Declare separate SLOs for admission, queueing, decision, effect verification and evidence publication; 100 percent of terminal governance decision record records must be attributable and schema-valid.

Measure queue, policy, context, model, tool, approval, effect verification, recovery and evidence latency separately. Report percentiles, quality, safety, cost, human burden, cancellation delay and terminal classes; never improve averages by dropping rejected, failed or quarantined work.

### Scalability Perspective

Partition governance and assurance work by tenant and bounded aggregate, preserve global contract compatibility, cap concurrency and fan-out, and fail closed when ownership or policy cannot converge.

Use bounded fan-out, backpressure, fairness reservations, locality and asynchronous facts where ordering is unnecessary. Cross-region or cross-node scale requires explicit data residency, identity federation, protocol compatibility, conflict resolution, disconnect behavior and reconciliation.

### Future Evolution

Future evolution may include machine-readable constitutions, external assurance, enterprise governance overlays and federated policy councils. Every increment begins as a hypothesis, runs in simulation or sandbox, proves quality and safety, obtains independent human authorization, canaries immutable versions and retains rollback, migration and historical interpretation.

Future capability never retroactively authorizes current behavior. Rights, law, accountability, tenant choice, evidence, Security and safe exit remain constraints even when technology, organization, providers or economic models change.

### Implementation Contract

- [ ] Define canonical schema, owner, compatibility policy and stable error taxonomy.
- [ ] Encode identity, policy, permission, approval, limits and isolation outside the model.
- [ ] Map each AI capability to an owned port, data class, effect class and receipt.
- [ ] Implement state transitions with optimistic concurrency and durable checkpoints.
- [ ] Propagate correlation, causation, deadline, cancellation and budget through every call.
- [ ] Verify external effects from authoritative state before completion or retry.
- [ ] Provide degraded behavior, circuit breaking, containment, recovery and reconciliation.
- [ ] Redact operational logs and retain protected forensic evidence by explicit policy.
- [ ] Create role-quality, adversarial, tenancy, load, chaos, migration and rollback tests.
- [ ] Ship dashboards, alert thresholds, runbooks, on-call ownership and support boundaries.
- [ ] Canary an immutable version and retain a tested last-known-safe rollback target.
- [ ] Require independent owner acceptance and applicable certification before production.

### ADR References

- Candidate implementation decision record: `adr/ADR-0050.md`. It is a Draft placeholder until completed and accepted; the filename grants no authority.
- A material ADR must record context, decision, alternatives, consequences, rights and security, data, economics, operability, compatibility, migration, rollback, tests, evidence and supersession scope.
- Where no accepted ADR exists, implementation must preserve the more restrictive current constitution and seek a human architecture decision.

### Section Acceptance Checklist

- [ ] Human accountable owner and operational owner resolve.
- [ ] Mission, non-goals, inputs, outputs and terminal criteria are typed.
- [ ] Identity, version, tenant, environment and lifecycle are immutable for a run.
- [ ] Permission and authority are deterministic, revocable and effect-specific.
- [ ] Data, context, Knowledge and Memory preserve purpose, provenance and lifecycle.
- [ ] Decision artifacts expose alternatives, dissent, uncertainty and requested judgment.
- [ ] Budgets preserve verification, recovery and safe shutdown.
- [ ] Communication semantics, schemas, replay and ownership are registered.
- [ ] Approvals and overrides bind exact immutable scope.
- [ ] Isolation, sandbox, egress, secrets and supply-chain controls are tested.
- [ ] External effects use idempotency and source-of-truth verification.
- [ ] Logs, metrics, traces, audit and evidence are redacted and complete.
- [ ] Failure, partial result, uncertainty and quarantine are explicit states.
- [ ] Recovery reconciles effects and proves restored invariants.
- [ ] Evolution has evaluation, certification, migration and rollback evidence.
- [ ] Human interfaces are accessible, non-coercive and preserve denial and escalation.
- [ ] An accepted ADR exists before irreversible architecture choice.
- [ ] Independent review can reproduce every consequential disposition.

### AI Memory Anchor

**Memory anchor `P4-99`:** `Agent Governance` is governed by `governance decision record` and owned in human accountability by Human Governance Board. Preserve: No agent, including an executive agent, can govern itself, alter constitutional controls, appoint approvers or convert operational success into political authority. On conflict or uncertainty, stop the smallest unsafe scope, retain evidence and escalate; never infer authority from an executive title, confidence, group membership, budget or future ambition.

### Governance Enforcement Layers

| Layer | Decision | Owner | Fail-closed response |
|---|---|---|---|
| Constitution | non-negotiable organization principles | Human Governance Board | reject conflicting policy or implementation |
| Policy | versioned rule for tenant, data, operation and risk | Human Policy and Security Owners | deny or require approval |
| Identity | principal, role, version, operator and lifecycle | Identity Owner | deny admission |
| Permission | effective capability for exact request | Policy Enforcement Point | deny and record |
| Isolation | runtime, data, network and secret boundary | Platform Security Owner | stop and destroy affected runtime |
| Approval | exact human authorization and separation | Approval Service Owner | make no effect |
| Execution | typed operation and state transition | Domain Owner | reject invalid state or duplicate |
| Audit | independent completeness and integrity | Audit Owner | mark outcome unverifiable and investigate |
| Override | human stop, narrow, correct or exact exception | Named Human Authority | enforce immutable controls and expiry |

**Human accountable owner:** Human Security and Domain Owners
**Primary record:** permission decision receipt
**Decision status:** Final Part 4 design constitution; implementation and production authority remain evidence-gated.

### Constitutional Purpose

Enforce identity, role, capability, resource, tenant, purpose, data, environment, time, task and approval constraints at every boundary.

This section is complete only when `permission decision receipt` is attributable, typed, policy-valid, resource-accounted, observable, recoverable and reviewable by Human Security and Domain Owners. The non-negotiable invariant is: Permissions are explicit, least-privilege, revocable and non-transitive; prompts, titles, group membership and prior success never grant access.

### Operating Contract

| Contract dimension | Normative requirement |
|---|---|
| Business outcome | Enforce identity, role, capability, resource, tenant, purpose, data, environment, time, task and approval constraints at every boundary. |
| Human accountability | Human Security and Domain Owners |
| Authoritative artifact | permission decision receipt |
| Required inputs | authenticated charter; current identity and authorization state; policy and authority snapshot; owned evidence; deadline; budget; acceptance criteria; human accountability route |
| Required outputs | versioned permission decision receipt; decision evidence; state transition; exceptions; resource account; terminal receipt |
| Constitutional invariant | Permissions are explicit, least-privilege, revocable and non-transitive; prompts, titles, group membership and prior success never grant access. |
| Default authority | A0/A1 advice and preparation unless an exact role card, policy, certification and effect-specific grant narrow a higher ceiling. |
| Default failure | Stop the smallest unsafe scope, preserve state and evidence, reconcile any attempted effect, and route the unresolved decision to the named owner. |
| Performance envelope | Declare separate SLOs for admission, queueing, decision, effect verification and evidence publication; 100 percent of terminal permission decision receipt records must be attributable and schema-valid. |
| Scale model | Partition identity and authorization work by tenant and bounded aggregate, preserve global contract compatibility, cap concurrency and fan-out, and fail closed when ownership or policy cannot converge. |
| Future direction | proof-carrying capabilities, continuous authorization, regional policy federation and zero-standing privilege |

### End-to-End Constitutional Procedure

1. **Authenticate caller and runtime.** Validate identity, scope, owner, policy, data, authority, budget and deadline; persist the decision and do not begin a dependent step until its preconditions and evidence pass.
2. **Resolve immutable agent version.** Validate identity, scope, owner, policy, data, authority, budget and deadline; persist the decision and do not begin a dependent step until its preconditions and evidence pass.
3. **Load role and task grants.** Validate identity, scope, owner, policy, data, authority, budget and deadline; persist the decision and do not begin a dependent step until its preconditions and evidence pass.
4. **Intersect tenant data purpose and environment.** Validate identity, scope, owner, policy, data, authority, budget and deadline; persist the decision and do not begin a dependent step until its preconditions and evidence pass.
5. **Validate approval and separation.** Validate identity, scope, owner, policy, data, authority, budget and deadline; persist the decision and do not begin a dependent step until its preconditions and evidence pass.
6. **Issue short-lived capability.** Validate identity, scope, owner, policy, data, authority, budget and deadline; persist the decision and do not begin a dependent step until its preconditions and evidence pass.
7. **Enforce at target boundary.** Validate identity, scope, owner, policy, data, authority, budget and deadline; persist the decision and do not begin a dependent step until its preconditions and evidence pass.
8. **Revoke and audit on state change.** Validate identity, scope, owner, policy, data, authority, budget and deadline; persist the decision and do not begin a dependent step until its preconditions and evidence pass.

### Required Decision Record

| Record component | Minimum fields | Independent check |
|---|---|---|
| Charter | outcome, non-goals, sponsor, owner, acceptance, deadline and expiry | mission and owner resolver |
| Identity | logical ID, immutable version, runtime principal, tenant, environment and operator | identity and lifecycle service |
| Evidence | sources, revisions, rights, freshness, transformations, contradictions and confidence | domain and provenance validator |
| Decision | facts, assumptions, alternatives, dissent, risk, cost, uncertainty and requested judgment | human or independent evaluator |
| Authority | role ceiling, task grant, policy, data purpose, approval and live revocation state | policy enforcement point |
| Execution | plan, resources, tools, state versions, checkpoints, attempts and effects | orchestrator and domain gateways |
| Outcome | typed status, acceptance, quality, business result, externalities, incidents and follow-up owner | task owner and Analytics |
| Audit | correlation, causation, digests, timestamps, receipts, retention and access history | independent Audit owner |

### Business Perspective

Agent Permission System makes identity and authorization an accountable operating capability rather than a title, prompt persona or undocumented model behavior. Business owners receive alternatives, value, full cost, risk, uncertainty, rights impact, dependencies and evidence before accepting a consequential result.

The business must fund control work as part of delivery: attribution, human review, Security, recovery, audit and lifecycle are not optional overhead. Success is the durable outcome represented by `permission decision receipt`, not output volume or agent activity.

### Engineering Perspective

Implement agent permission system through versioned schemas, deterministic state machines, owned ports, immutable identities, hierarchical budgets, cancellation, idempotency, checkpoints and source-of-truth verification. Probabilistic inference may propose; deterministic services authorize and commit.

Make time, randomness, provider routes, policy versions and external effects injectable in tests. Classify every dependency as startup-hard, runtime-required, optional or asynchronous; define timeout, circuit, fallback, replay, migration and failure ownership explicitly.

### Architecture Perspective

Human Security and Domain Owners remains the human accountability boundary. The Identity and Authorization domain owns semantics and canonical state; CATA coordinates portfolios, Supervisor coordinates runtime, specialists produce bounded artifacts, and policy/effect gateways prevent orchestration from becoming authority.

Commands request owned work, queries read without hidden mutation, events report committed facts, approvals authorize exact effects, notifications inform and receipts prove attempts. Projections and caches are rebuildable and never promoted to source of truth by convenience.

### AI Coding Perspective

Before changing implementation for section `100`, load `context/17_SECURITY.md`, `context/02_PROJECT_RULES.md`, `context/04_ARCHITECTURE.md`, inspect current schemas and ownership, and identify the exact deterministic guard. An AI coding agent must not infer implementation permission from this final documentation status, an empty directory, a draft ADR or a provider feature.

Write negative tests first for mission drift, forged identity, cross-tenant data, stale context, permission expansion, approval substitution, prompt injection, duplicate effect, cancellation, evidence loss and migration incompatibility. Keep changes minimal, preserve user work and report unresolved assumptions.

### Human Perspective

Humans see who the agent is, why it is acting, who owns the task, what evidence it used, what it knows and does not know, what decision is requested, what alternatives exist, what it costs, and what happens on approval, denial or delay. Human Security and Domain Owners can stop or narrow work without navigating hidden agent conversations.

Interfaces must avoid automation bias, anthropomorphic pressure and approval fatigue. They provide accessible evidence, dissent, uncertainty, scope, expiry, consequences, revision, denial, escalation and recovery controls. Human silence is never consent or approval.

### Security Perspective

Apply zero standing privilege, workload identity, tenant and environment isolation, purpose-bound data, secret-manager references, prompt and tool injection defenses, egress policy, sandboxing, rate limits, revocation, tamper-evident receipts and a tested kill switch. Section invariant: Permissions are explicit, least-privilege, revocable and non-transitive; prompts, titles, group membership and prior success never grant access.

Threat tests cover confused deputy, role-title escalation, malicious context, poisoned knowledge, memory exfiltration, approval laundering, replay, supply-chain substitution, side channels, resource exhaustion, audit tampering and compromised provider behavior.

### Performance Perspective

Declare separate SLOs for admission, queueing, decision, effect verification and evidence publication; 100 percent of terminal permission decision receipt records must be attributable and schema-valid.

Measure queue, policy, context, model, tool, approval, effect verification, recovery and evidence latency separately. Report percentiles, quality, safety, cost, human burden, cancellation delay and terminal classes; never improve averages by dropping rejected, failed or quarantined work.

### Scalability Perspective

Partition identity and authorization work by tenant and bounded aggregate, preserve global contract compatibility, cap concurrency and fan-out, and fail closed when ownership or policy cannot converge.

Use bounded fan-out, backpressure, fairness reservations, locality and asynchronous facts where ordering is unnecessary. Cross-region or cross-node scale requires explicit data residency, identity federation, protocol compatibility, conflict resolution, disconnect behavior and reconciliation.

### Future Evolution

Future evolution may include proof-carrying capabilities, continuous authorization, regional policy federation and zero-standing privilege. Every increment begins as a hypothesis, runs in simulation or sandbox, proves quality and safety, obtains independent human authorization, canaries immutable versions and retains rollback, migration and historical interpretation.

Future capability never retroactively authorizes current behavior. Rights, law, accountability, tenant choice, evidence, Security and safe exit remain constraints even when technology, organization, providers or economic models change.

### Implementation Contract

- [ ] Define canonical schema, owner, compatibility policy and stable error taxonomy.
- [ ] Encode identity, policy, permission, approval, limits and isolation outside the model.
- [ ] Map each AI capability to an owned port, data class, effect class and receipt.
- [ ] Implement state transitions with optimistic concurrency and durable checkpoints.
- [ ] Propagate correlation, causation, deadline, cancellation and budget through every call.
- [ ] Verify external effects from authoritative state before completion or retry.
- [ ] Provide degraded behavior, circuit breaking, containment, recovery and reconciliation.
- [ ] Redact operational logs and retain protected forensic evidence by explicit policy.
- [ ] Create role-quality, adversarial, tenancy, load, chaos, migration and rollback tests.
- [ ] Ship dashboards, alert thresholds, runbooks, on-call ownership and support boundaries.
- [ ] Canary an immutable version and retain a tested last-known-safe rollback target.
- [ ] Require independent owner acceptance and applicable certification before production.

#### CAT-AG-P4-D-100 — Part 4 Section 100 — Agent Permission System

**Diagram ID:** `CAT-AG-P4-D-100`
**Title:** Part 4 Section 100 — Agent Permission System
**Purpose:** Visualize the constitutional operating boundary and evidence path for Agent Permission System.
**Audience:** Human owners, executive and department designers, architects, engineers, security reviewers, operators, auditors, and AI coding agents.
**Reading Order:** Begin at the human charter or leftmost source, follow control and decision arrows, and finish at verified evidence, recovery, or safe termination.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  Request[Agent capability request] --> Identity[Authenticate identity version tenant environment]
  Identity --> Role[Resolve role ceiling and task grant]
  Role --> Data[Intersect data purpose consent and residency]
  Data --> Approval[Validate exact approval and separation]
  Approval --> State[Check live lifecycle incident and revocation state]
  State --> Decision{{Authorization decision}}
  Decision -->|Permit| Token[Issue short lived scoped capability]
  Decision -->|Deny| Denial[Record stable denial]
  Decision -->|Approval needed| Human[Route exact human request]
  Token --> Target[Target boundary revalidates]
  Target --> Receipt[Effect or read receipt]
```

### Constitutional Control Catalogue

Each control below is independently testable for `Agent Permission System`. Satisfying a narrative goal without the named enforcement and evidence is not constitutional conformance.

#### CAT-AG-P4-100-C01 — Charter Scope

- **Rule:** For agent permission system, bind all work to a signed outcome, explicit non-goals, owner, expiry and acceptance criteria.
- **Business test:** `permission decision receipt` exposes the cost, benefit, risk, owner, uncertainty and consequence of this control to an accountable reviewer.
- **Engineering enforcement:** The boundary responsible for `authenticate caller and runtime` validates this control before state change and again before any related material effect.
- **AI behavior:** Missing, stale, contradictory, denied or unverifiable control data causes a typed stop, wait, refusal or escalation; the model never fills the gap with confidence.
- **Human boundary:** Human Security and Domain Owners receives the exact requested decision and evidence when human judgment is required; no UI default or silence creates consent.
- **Security assertion:** Forged role, cross-tenant reference, replay, changed payload, expired grant, injected instruction and evidence tampering all fail closed and emit a protected signal.
- **Performance assertion:** Enforcement remains inside the declared SLO and resource reserve; overload applies backpressure rather than removing checks.
- **Evidence:** Store logical and runtime identity, tenant, versions, policy, grants, input/output digests, decision, state, timestamps, owner and redacted receipts.
- **Failure code:** `CAT_P4_100_01_CONSTITUTIONAL_CONTROL`; dependent work remains non-success and any attempted effect enters reconciliation.
- **Recovery:** Contain the affected scope, establish authoritative effect state, restore the invariant, obtain required human decision and link a terminal recovery receipt.
- **Implementation test:** Run positive, negative, boundary, cancellation, duplicate, stale-state, migration and compromised-dependency fixtures deterministically.
- **Ownership:** Human Security and Domain Owners owns residual business judgment; the Identity and Authorization service owner owns enforcement; Audit owns independent evidence review.
- **Constitutional assertion:** An independent reviewer can reproduce the `Charter Scope` disposition without trusting hidden reasoning, title, provider success or undocumented operator explanation.

### AI Memory Anchor

**Memory anchor `P4-100`:** `Agent Permission System` is governed by `permission decision receipt` and owned in human accountability by Human Security and Domain Owners. Preserve: Permissions are explicit, least-privilege, revocable and non-transitive; prompts, titles, group membership and prior success never grant access. On conflict or uncertainty, stop the smallest unsafe scope, retain evidence and escalate; never infer authority from an executive title, confidence, group membership, budget or future ambition.

| Audit | independent completeness and integrity | Audit Owner | mark outcome unverifiable and investigate |
| Override | human stop, narrow, correct or exact exception | Named Human Authority | enforce immutable controls and expiry |

## 101. Agent Security Model

**Section ID:** `CAT-AG-P4-101`
**Constitutional domain:** Trust and Security
**Human accountable owner:** Human Security Owner
**Primary record:** agent security assurance record
**Decision status:** Final Part 4 design constitution; implementation and production authority remain evidence-gated.

### Constitutional Purpose

Define defense in depth across identity, prompts, models, context, memory, knowledge, tools, data, events, supply chain, runtime and effects.

This section is complete only when `agent security assurance record` is attributable, typed, policy-valid, resource-accounted, observable, recoverable and reviewable by Human Security Owner. The non-negotiable invariant is: No probabilistic model is a trusted security boundary, and no security agent receives unlimited visibility or remediation authority.

### Operating Contract

| Contract dimension | Normative requirement |
|---|---|
| Business outcome | Define defense in depth across identity, prompts, models, context, memory, knowledge, tools, data, events, supply chain, runtime and effects. |
| Human accountability | Human Security Owner |
| Authoritative artifact | agent security assurance record |
| Required inputs | authenticated charter; current trust and security state; policy and authority snapshot; owned evidence; deadline; budget; acceptance criteria; human accountability route |
| Required outputs | versioned agent security assurance record; decision evidence; state transition; exceptions; resource account; terminal receipt |
| Constitutional invariant | No probabilistic model is a trusted security boundary, and no security agent receives unlimited visibility or remediation authority. |
| Default authority | A0/A1 advice and preparation unless an exact role card, policy, certification and effect-specific grant narrow a higher ceiling. |
| Default failure | Stop the smallest unsafe scope, preserve state and evidence, reconcile any attempted effect, and route the unresolved decision to the named owner. |
| Performance envelope | Declare separate SLOs for admission, queueing, decision, effect verification and evidence publication; 100 percent of terminal agent security assurance record records must be attributable and schema-valid. |
| Scale model | Partition trust and security work by tenant and bounded aggregate, preserve global contract compatibility, cap concurrency and fan-out, and fail closed when ownership or policy cannot converge. |
| Future direction | confidential runtimes, continuous threat models, formal policies, adaptive defense and cross-organization threat intelligence |

### End-to-End Constitutional Procedure

1. **Identify assets actors and trust boundaries.** Validate identity, scope, owner, policy, data, authority, budget and deadline; persist the decision and do not begin a dependent step until its preconditions and evidence pass.
2. **Model abuse and compromise paths.** Validate identity, scope, owner, policy, data, authority, budget and deadline; persist the decision and do not begin a dependent step until its preconditions and evidence pass.
3. **Apply deterministic prevention.** Validate identity, scope, owner, policy, data, authority, budget and deadline; persist the decision and do not begin a dependent step until its preconditions and evidence pass.
4. **Detect and correlate signals.** Validate identity, scope, owner, policy, data, authority, budget and deadline; persist the decision and do not begin a dependent step until its preconditions and evidence pass.
5. **Contain narrow blast radius.** Validate identity, scope, owner, policy, data, authority, budget and deadline; persist the decision and do not begin a dependent step until its preconditions and evidence pass.
6. **Reconcile effects and evidence.** Validate identity, scope, owner, policy, data, authority, budget and deadline; persist the decision and do not begin a dependent step until its preconditions and evidence pass.
7. **Remediate and recertify.** Validate identity, scope, owner, policy, data, authority, budget and deadline; persist the decision and do not begin a dependent step until its preconditions and evidence pass.
8. **Update reviewed threat model.** Validate identity, scope, owner, policy, data, authority, budget and deadline; persist the decision and do not begin a dependent step until its preconditions and evidence pass.

### Required Decision Record

| Record component | Minimum fields | Independent check |
|---|---|---|
| Charter | outcome, non-goals, sponsor, owner, acceptance, deadline and expiry | mission and owner resolver |
| Identity | logical ID, immutable version, runtime principal, tenant, environment and operator | identity and lifecycle service |
| Evidence | sources, revisions, rights, freshness, transformations, contradictions and confidence | domain and provenance validator |
| Decision | facts, assumptions, alternatives, dissent, risk, cost, uncertainty and requested judgment | human or independent evaluator |
| Authority | role ceiling, task grant, policy, data purpose, approval and live revocation state | policy enforcement point |
| Execution | plan, resources, tools, state versions, checkpoints, attempts and effects | orchestrator and domain gateways |
| Outcome | typed status, acceptance, quality, business result, externalities, incidents and follow-up owner | task owner and Analytics |
| Audit | correlation, causation, digests, timestamps, receipts, retention and access history | independent Audit owner |

### Business Perspective

Agent Security Model makes trust and security an accountable operating capability rather than a title, prompt persona or undocumented model behavior. Business owners receive alternatives, value, full cost, risk, uncertainty, rights impact, dependencies and evidence before accepting a consequential result.

The business must fund control work as part of delivery: attribution, human review, Security, recovery, audit and lifecycle are not optional overhead. Success is the durable outcome represented by `agent security assurance record`, not output volume or agent activity.

### Engineering Perspective

Implement agent security model through versioned schemas, deterministic state machines, owned ports, immutable identities, hierarchical budgets, cancellation, idempotency, checkpoints and source-of-truth verification. Probabilistic inference may propose; deterministic services authorize and commit.

Make time, randomness, provider routes, policy versions and external effects injectable in tests. Classify every dependency as startup-hard, runtime-required, optional or asynchronous; define timeout, circuit, fallback, replay, migration and failure ownership explicitly.

### Architecture Perspective

Human Security Owner remains the human accountability boundary. The Trust and Security domain owns semantics and canonical state; CATA coordinates portfolios, Supervisor coordinates runtime, specialists produce bounded artifacts, and policy/effect gateways prevent orchestration from becoming authority.

Commands request owned work, queries read without hidden mutation, events report committed facts, approvals authorize exact effects, notifications inform and receipts prove attempts. Projections and caches are rebuildable and never promoted to source of truth by convenience.

### AI Coding Perspective

Before changing implementation for section `101`, load `context/17_SECURITY.md`, `SECURITY.md`, `context/04_ARCHITECTURE.md`, inspect current schemas and ownership, and identify the exact deterministic guard. An AI coding agent must not infer implementation permission from this final documentation status, an empty directory, a draft ADR or a provider feature.

Write negative tests first for mission drift, forged identity, cross-tenant data, stale context, permission expansion, approval substitution, prompt injection, duplicate effect, cancellation, evidence loss and migration incompatibility. Keep changes minimal, preserve user work and report unresolved assumptions.

### Human Perspective

Humans see who the agent is, why it is acting, who owns the task, what evidence it used, what it knows and does not know, what decision is requested, what alternatives exist, what it costs, and what happens on approval, denial or delay. Human Security Owner can stop or narrow work without navigating hidden agent conversations.

Interfaces must avoid automation bias, anthropomorphic pressure and approval fatigue. They provide accessible evidence, dissent, uncertainty, scope, expiry, consequences, revision, denial, escalation and recovery controls. Human silence is never consent or approval.

### Security Perspective

Apply zero standing privilege, workload identity, tenant and environment isolation, purpose-bound data, secret-manager references, prompt and tool injection defenses, egress policy, sandboxing, rate limits, revocation, tamper-evident receipts and a tested kill switch. Section invariant: No probabilistic model is a trusted security boundary, and no security agent receives unlimited visibility or remediation authority.

Threat tests cover confused deputy, role-title escalation, malicious context, poisoned knowledge, memory exfiltration, approval laundering, replay, supply-chain substitution, side channels, resource exhaustion, audit tampering and compromised provider behavior.

### Performance Perspective

Declare separate SLOs for admission, queueing, decision, effect verification and evidence publication; 100 percent of terminal agent security assurance record records must be attributable and schema-valid.

Measure queue, policy, context, model, tool, approval, effect verification, recovery and evidence latency separately. Report percentiles, quality, safety, cost, human burden, cancellation delay and terminal classes; never improve averages by dropping rejected, failed or quarantined work.

### Scalability Perspective

Partition trust and security work by tenant and bounded aggregate, preserve global contract compatibility, cap concurrency and fan-out, and fail closed when ownership or policy cannot converge.

Use bounded fan-out, backpressure, fairness reservations, locality and asynchronous facts where ordering is unnecessary. Cross-region or cross-node scale requires explicit data residency, identity federation, protocol compatibility, conflict resolution, disconnect behavior and reconciliation.

### Future Evolution

Future evolution may include confidential runtimes, continuous threat models, formal policies, adaptive defense and cross-organization threat intelligence. Every increment begins as a hypothesis, runs in simulation or sandbox, proves quality and safety, obtains independent human authorization, canaries immutable versions and retains rollback, migration and historical interpretation.

Future capability never retroactively authorizes current behavior. Rights, law, accountability, tenant choice, evidence, Security and safe exit remain constraints even when technology, organization, providers or economic models change.

### Implementation Contract

- [ ] Define canonical schema, owner, compatibility policy and stable error taxonomy.
- [ ] Encode identity, policy, permission, approval, limits and isolation outside the model.
- [ ] Map each AI capability to an owned port, data class, effect class and receipt.
- [ ] Implement state transitions with optimistic concurrency and durable checkpoints.
- [ ] Propagate correlation, causation, deadline, cancellation and budget through every call.
- [ ] Verify external effects from authoritative state before completion or retry.
- [ ] Provide degraded behavior, circuit breaking, containment, recovery and reconciliation.
- [ ] Redact operational logs and retain protected forensic evidence by explicit policy.
- [ ] Create role-quality, adversarial, tenancy, load, chaos, migration and rollback tests.
- [ ] Ship dashboards, alert thresholds, runbooks, on-call ownership and support boundaries.
- [ ] Canary an immutable version and retain a tested last-known-safe rollback target.
- [ ] Require independent owner acceptance and applicable certification before production.

### ADR References

- Candidate implementation decision record: `adr/ADR-0052.md`. It is a Draft placeholder until completed and accepted; the filename grants no authority.
- A material ADR must record context, decision, alternatives, consequences, rights and security, data, economics, operability, compatibility, migration, rollback, tests, evidence and supersession scope.
- Where no accepted ADR exists, implementation must preserve the more restrictive current constitution and seek a human architecture decision.
